title: American Express Platinum Card
scouts_verdict: The 2025 refresh turned the Platinum into a credit-stacking monster — $600 hotel, $400 Resy, $300 lululemon, $300 streaming, and a bunch more. If you naturally eat at Resy restaurants, already shop at lululemon, and travel enough to use the hotel and airline credits, the $895 fee pays for itself and then some. But here's the honest truth: if you're forcing spend just to 'use' credits, you're paying $895 for lounge access and a shiny metal card. Be brutally honest about your spending habits before you apply.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Look, the Amex Platinum is the card people either love or love to argue about. It's American Express's flagship personal charge card — built for frequent travelers who want the best lounge access on the planet, complimentary hotel elite status, and enough annual credits to fill a spreadsheet. After the September 2025 refresh, the annual fee jumped to $895 (yes, that's nearly $900 — no, your spouse won't be thrilled), but Amex threw in over $1,400 in new annual credits to justify it: a $400 Resy dining credit, $300 lululemon credit, an enhanced $600 hotel credit, and even an OURA Ring credit.

You earn Membership Rewards points — arguably the most versatile points currency out there — and get access to a lounge network that makes other premium cards jealous: Centurion Lounges (the flex), Priority Pass Select, Delta Sky Clubs (10 complimentary visits per year when flying Delta), and more. Oh, and the card is made of stainless steel, so there's that satisfying clunk when you drop it on the table.

Here's the thing though: this is not your everyday spending card. The earn rates outside of travel are a flat 1x, which is underwhelming at best. The entire value proposition lives in the credits, the lounges, the hotel status, and the travel protections. Smart Platinum holders pair it with the Amex Gold for daily spending — that's where the 4x on dining and groceries lives — and use the Platinum for what it does best: making airports feel less terrible.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• Centurion Lounge Access (the flex): The crown jewel. Complimentary access to American Express Centurion Lounges worldwide, plus Priority Pass Select, 10 complimentary Delta Sky Club visits per year (when flying Delta), Plaza Premium, Escape Lounges, and more — over 1,550 lounges across 140 countries. Your layovers will never be the same.
  • 5x Points on Flights: Earn 5x Membership Rewards points on flights booked directly with airlines or through Amex Travel (up to $500,000 per calendar year). If you're hitting that cap, congrats on the lifestyle.
  • 5x Points on Hotels via Amex Travel: Earn 5x on prepaid hotel bookings through Amex Travel. Solid, though it does lock you into the Amex portal.
  • $600 Hotel Credit: Up to $300 semiannually for prepaid Fine Hotels + Resorts or The Hotel Collection bookings through Amex Travel. FHR stays also come with upgrades, late checkout, and breakfast — genuinely luxurious.
  • $400 Resy Dining Credit: Up to $100 per quarter for dining at 10,000+ U.S. Resy restaurants (enrollment required). This one is new and a big deal for foodies.
  • $300 Digital Entertainment Credit: Up to $25/month toward Disney+, Hulu, ESPN+, Paramount+, YouTube Premium, YouTube TV, Peacock, The New York Times, and The Wall Street Journal. Basically pays for your streaming life.
  • $300 lululemon Credit: Up to $75 per quarter at retail lululemon stores or lululemon.com in the U.S. (enrollment required). Athleisure fans, rejoice.
  • $219 CLEAR+ Credit: Annual statement credit for a CLEAR+ membership. Skip the TSA line like a main character.
  • $200 Uber Cash: Up to $200 per year in Uber Cash ($15/month, $20 bonus in December). Handy if Uber is already part of your routine.
  • $200 Airline Fee Credit: Annual credit for incidental fees (baggage, seat upgrades, etc.) with one selected airline. Pick wisely — you're stuck with it for the year.
  • $120 Uber One Credit: Statement credits covering Uber One membership.
  • $200 OURA Credit: Statement credit toward an OURA Ring purchase. Sleep tracking meets credit card perks — peak 2025.
  • $300 Equinox Credit: Up to $300 per calendar year toward Equinox gym memberships or Equinox+ digital subscriptions. Enrollment required.
  • $155 Walmart+ Credit: Monthly credit covering a Walmart+ membership. Free grocery delivery? Don't mind if you do.
  • Global Entry/TSA PreCheck Credit: Up to $120 credit every 4 years. A must-have for any frequent traveler.
  • Hilton Honors Gold Status: Complimentary Gold status (enrollment required). The daily food and beverage credit at select U.S. brands (continental breakfast at select brands abroad) is the real win here.
  • Marriott Bonvoy Gold Elite Status: Complimentary Gold Elite status (enrollment required). The perks are modest, but free is free.
  • Leaders Club Sterling Status: Status at The Leading Hotels of the World with daily continental breakfast for two, late checkout when available, a 5% points bonus and up to 5 pre-arrival upgrades a year at boutique luxury properties (enrollment required). If you know, you know.
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees: Use the card abroad without added costs. Expected at this fee level, but still appreciated.

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:
• Annual Fee: $895 (increased from $695 in September 2025; existing cardholders transitioned to $895 at renewal on or after January 2, 2026). Let's be real — that's a mortgage payment in some zip codes.
  • Authorized User Fee: Additional Platinum cards at $195 each; Companion Platinum cards at no annual fee (they skip lounge access and hotel status). The Companion cards are the move if your family just needs the Membership Rewards link.
  • Foreign Transaction Fees: None
  • Late Payment Fee: Up to $40
  • Note: This is a charge card, meaning the balance must generally be paid in full each month. Amex offers a Pay Over Time feature for eligible purchases, which carries a variable APR. Translation: don't treat it like a regular credit card.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
American Express uses a personalized "as high as" welcome offer system for the Platinum Card. Offers go as high as 175,000 Membership Rewards points after spending $12,000 on eligible purchases in the first 6 months, though plenty of applicants see a lower number. The exact offer is shown after you submit the application — Amex performs a soft pull at this stage, so checking does not affect your credit score. No commitment until you see your number.

The highest publicly reported offer is 175,000 points. Targeted and referral offers can vary; historically, offers of 80,000 to 150,000 points have been available through various channels. At a valuation of roughly 2 cents per point, the 175,000-point offer is worth approximately $3,500 in travel value. That's a business-class ticket to Europe, folks.

Tip: Check the Amex website directly first to see your personalized offer. Also try CardMatch, referral links from existing Amex cardholders, and incognito browsing. Amex's once-per-lifetime rule for sign-up bonuses means you only get one shot — don't leave points on the table by jumping at the first offer you see.

sections.title: Earning Rates
sections.content:
• 5x points: Flights booked directly with airlines or through Amex Travel (up to $500,000/year, then 1x)
  • 5x points: Prepaid hotels booked through Amex Travel
  • 1x points: All other purchases

The short version: the Platinum earns amazingly on travel and poorly on everything else. That 1x on non-travel spending is, frankly, underwhelming for a card at this price point. Amex designed it this way on purpose — they want you carrying the Amex Gold Card (4x dining, 4x groceries) for daily spending and pulling out the Platinum when you book flights or flash it at the Centurion Lounge. It's a perks card, not a points-earning card. Accept that and you'll be much happier with it.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
Membership Rewards points are the Swiss Army knife of points currencies — there's almost nothing you can't do with them:

  • Transfer Partners (Best Value): Transfer to 20 airline and hotel partners (most at 1:1) including Delta, ANA, Singapore Airlines, British Airways, Virgin Atlantic, Air Canada Aeroplan, Air France/KLM Flying Blue, Hilton Honors (1:2 ratio), and Marriott Bonvoy (1:1 ratio). This is where the magic happens. Transfer partner redemptions typically yield 1.5 to 2.5 cents per point or more.
  • Amex Travel Portal: Redeem at 1 cent per point for flights and Fine Hotels + Resorts stays, or 0.7 cents for most other bookings. Platinum cardholders get a slight advantage on flights booked through the portal. Acceptable, not amazing.
  • Statement Credits: Typically 0.6 cents per point — please don't do this unless you absolutely have to.
  • Gift Cards: Usually at or below 1 cent per point value. Hard pass.
  • Charles Schwab Platinum: If you hold the Schwab version, you can cash out at 1.1 cents per point directly to a Schwab brokerage account. A legitimate option for people who'd rather invest their points than fly on them.

Best value: Transfer to airline partners for premium cabin international flights. Business and first class redemptions on partners like ANA, Singapore Airlines, or Virgin Atlantic routinely deliver 3-5+ cents per point in value. That's when Membership Rewards points really sing.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• $600 Hotel Credit: Up to $300 semiannually for prepaid Fine Hotels + Resorts or The Hotel Collection bookings through Amex Travel. FHR bookings include room upgrades, late checkout, daily breakfast, and a property credit. This is how you do hotel stays right.
  • $400 Resy Dining Credit: Up to $100 per quarter for eligible dining at 10,000+ U.S. Resy restaurants. Enrollment required, and the credit resets every quarter — set a calendar reminder or you'll forget.
  • $300 Digital Entertainment Credit: Up to $25/month toward select streaming and digital subscriptions including Disney+, Hulu, ESPN+, Paramount+, YouTube Premium, YouTube TV, Peacock, NYT, and WSJ. Basically your entire streaming bundle, covered.
  • $300 lululemon Credit: Up to $75 per quarter for purchases at retail lululemon stores (excluding outlets) or lululemon.com in the U.S. Whether this is a perk or an enabler depends on your closet.
  • $219 CLEAR+ Credit: Annual statement credit for CLEAR+ membership (subject to auto-renewal).
  • $200 Airline Fee Credit: Covers incidental fees with one selected airline per calendar year. Great for checked bags or seat upgrades, but you have to pick one airline and commit.
  • $200 Uber Cash: $15/month automatically loaded to your Uber account, with $20 bonus in December. Use it or lose it each month.
  • $200 OURA Credit: Statement credit toward the purchase of an OURA Ring. New perk, very 2025.
  • $155 Walmart+ Credit: Monthly statement credits covering a Walmart+ membership. Free grocery delivery, plus your choice of ad-supported Paramount+ or Peacock.
  • $120 Uber One Credit: Statement credits for an Uber One membership.
  • $300 Equinox Credit: Up to $300 per calendar year toward Equinox gym memberships or Equinox+ digital subscriptions. Enrollment required.
  • $120 Global Entry/TSA PreCheck Credit: Reimbursement every 4 years.
  • Centurion Lounge Access: Access for cardholder; guest policy now requires $75,000+ annual spend to bring 2 guests for free. They tightened this up — no more bringing your whole crew unless you spend big.
  • Priority Pass Select: Unlimited visits at 1,300+ lounges worldwide. The backup plan when there's no Centurion nearby.
  • Delta Sky Club Access: 10 complimentary visits per year when flying Delta on a same-day ticket. Huge if you're a Delta hub flyer.
  • Fine Hotels + Resorts Program: Upgrades, breakfast, late checkout, and property credits at 1,800+ luxury hotels. Once you book FHR, you won't go back.
  • Leaders Club Sterling Status: Boutique luxury hotel perks through The Leading Hotels of the World.
  • Hotel Elite Status: Hilton Honors Gold, Marriott Bonvoy Gold Elite — complimentary (enrollment required). Hilton Gold gets you a daily food and beverage credit at select U.S. brands, which alone has serious value.

Let's be direct: the Amex Platinum wins on lounge access — Centurion Lounges are still in a class of their own, and nothing else comes close. The 2025 refresh also gave it a credit portfolio that still tops the competition. But the Chase Sapphire Reserve earns 3x on dining (the Platinum earns 1x) for $100 less a year. And the Capital One Venture X? It eats the Platinum's lunch on pure value — $395 fee, growing lounge network, flat 2x on everything. The Platinum's $895 fee only makes sense if you actively use a significant portion of its credits. If you're leaving credits on the table, the Venture X is the smarter play.

sections.title: Best For
sections.content: The Amex Platinum is for the traveler who flies multiple times per year, actually uses airport lounges, and will make a spreadsheet to track credits (or at least set calendar reminders). With roughly $3,000 in potential annual credits after the 2025 refresh (Amex pitches $3,500+ in total value once you count lounges and FHR perks), the $895 fee can genuinely be a bargain — but only if you use the credits for things you'd buy anyway. If you find yourself buying lululemon leggings and OURA Rings just to "use the credits," you're doing it wrong. Pair it with the Amex Gold for groceries and dining to get the most from the Membership Rewards ecosystem.

title: American Express Gold Card
scouts_verdict: The Amex Gold is the best everyday spending card in the game, full stop. You're getting 4x on dining and groceries — which at 2cpp is effectively 8% back — plus $424 in credits against a $325 fee. The card literally pays you to eat. Pair it with the Platinum for the full Amex experience, or run it solo and watch your grocery trips turn into business class flights.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
If you eat food and buy groceries — and let's assume you do — the Amex Gold Card is probably the single best card you can carry for everyday spending. It earns 4x Membership Rewards points on both dining and U.S. supermarkets, which is a top-of-market rate that nobody else matches at this price point.

At $325 per year (bumped up from $250 in 2024), the annual fee sounds steep until you count the credits: up to $424 annually from $120 in Uber Cash, $120 in dining credits at select restaurants, $100 in Resy dining credits, and $84 in Dunkin' credits. Do that math and the card is paying you to hold it — before you even count the points. The Gold also earns 3x on flights booked directly or through Amex Travel, and 5x on prepaid hotels. No premium lounge access or hotel status here, but that's what the Platinum is for.

The Gold Card earns the same Membership Rewards currency as the Platinum, so all your points flow into one pool that transfers to 20+ airline and hotel partners. Ask anyone deep in the points game what their favorite two-card setup is, and nine times out of ten the answer is Amex Gold + Platinum. The Gold does the earning. The Platinum does the perks.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• 5x Points on Prepaid Hotels: Booked through Amex Travel. The card's highest earn rate, though a standard prepaid portal rate usually forfeits hotel points and elite night credit — worth comparing against booking direct. Stays booked through The Hotel Collection (two-night minimum) add a $100 credit toward eligible on-property charges, plus a room upgrade and 4pm late checkout when available, but don't count on hotel points or elite night credit there either — those generally come only with Fine Hotels + Resorts bookings, a Platinum perk.
  • 4x Points on Restaurants: Worldwide, including takeout and delivery. Up to $50,000 per calendar year, then 1x. This is the earn rate other cards dream about.
  • 4x Points on U.S. Supermarkets: Up to $25,000 per year, then 1x. Includes most major grocery chains (not Walmart or Target — those code as superstores, not supermarkets).
  • 3x Points on Flights: Booked directly with airlines or through Amex Travel. Decent for a non-premium card.
  • $120 Uber Cash: $10/month in Uber Cash, automatically added to your linked Uber account. Use it for rides or Uber Eats — just don't forget it resets monthly.
  • $120 Dining Credit: Up to $10/month at Grubhub (including Seamless), Buffalo Wild Wings, Five Guys, The Cheesecake Factory, and Wonder (enrollment required). The roster rotates — Goldbelly and Wine.com dropped off after June 30, 2026 — so check periodically.
  • $100 Resy Dining Credit: Up to $50 semiannually for in-person dining at U.S. Resy restaurants and other eligible Resy purchases (enrollment required). New with the 2024 refresh.
  • $84 Dunkin' Credit: Up to $7/month for purchases at U.S. Dunkin' locations (enrollment required). Your morning coffee habit, subsidized by Amex.
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees: Use abroad without extra charges. Always appreciated.
  • Membership Rewards Points: Access to the same transfer partner network as the Platinum (20+ airlines and hotels). Same points, same partners, same value.
  • Purchase Protection: Coverage for eligible purchases against accidental damage, theft, or loss for up to 90 days (up to $10,000 per purchase).
  • Extended Warranty: Extends manufacturer warranties by up to 1 year.

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:
• Annual Fee: $325 (increased from $250 in 2024). Not cheap, but the credits more than cover it if you use them.
  • Authorized User Fee: $0 for up to five additional Gold cards; $35 each for the sixth and beyond
  • Foreign Transaction Fees: None
  • Late Payment Fee: Up to $40
  • Note: This is a charge card with Pay Over Time capability for eligible purchases. If you carry a balance using Pay Over Time, you will pay a variable APR. The default expectation is pay in full each month.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
Amex uses a personalized welcome offer system for the Gold Card. The current public offer goes as high as 100,000 Membership Rewards points after spending $8,000 on eligible purchases in the first 6 months of card membership. Not everyone will qualify for the max — your personalized amount shows up at application time.

At a valuation of roughly 2 cents per point, the 100,000-point offer is worth approximately $2,000 in travel value. Not bad for a card you'd want to carry anyway.

Tip: Check referral links from existing Amex cardholders and the Amex website directly to compare offers before applying. Amex's once-per-lifetime bonus rule means you get one shot at this — don't rush it. Wait for the best offer you can find. And if you have (or have had) the Platinum Card, you may not be eligible for the Gold bonus at all — so if you want both, open the Gold first.

sections.title: Earning Rates
sections.content:
• 5x points: Prepaid hotels booked through Amex Travel
  • 4x points: Restaurants worldwide (up to $50,000/year, then 1x)
  • 4x points: U.S. supermarkets (up to $25,000/year, then 1x)
  • 3x points: Flights booked directly with airlines or through Amex Travel
  • 2x points: Prepaid car rentals booked through Amex Travel and cruises booked and paid through Amex Travel
  • 1x points: All other purchases

Here's where it gets fun. At a conservative valuation of 2 cents per Membership Rewards point, the 4x categories effectively return 8% back on dining and groceries. For a household spending $500/month on groceries and $400/month on dining, that is roughly $864 in annual value from earn rates alone — more than 2.5x the $325 annual fee before you even touch the credits. You're basically printing miles every time you eat. Note that since the 2024 refresh, the 4x restaurant bonus has been capped at $50,000 per calendar year.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
Gold Card points are Membership Rewards points — the exact same currency as the Platinum, with the exact same redemption power:

  • Transfer Partners (Best Value): Transfers to 20+ airline and hotel loyalty programs, most at 1:1. Top transfer partners include Delta SkyMiles, ANA Mileage Club, Air France/KLM Flying Blue, British Airways Avios, Singapore Airlines KrisFlyer, Virgin Atlantic Flying Club, Air Canada Aeroplan, and Hilton Honors (1:2 ratio). This is where your grocery points become business class seats.
  • Amex Travel Portal: Redeem at 1 cent per point for flights. No points-back bonus here — the 35% Pay with Points rebate belongs to the Business Platinum, not the personal cards. Fine in a pinch, but transfer partners are better.
  • Statement Credits: Poor value at roughly 0.6 cents per point. Just... don't.
  • Gift Cards: Variable value, anywhere from 0.5 to 1 cent per point. Meh.

Best value: Transfer to airline partners for premium cabin redemptions. Even economy award flights through partners like ANA, Aeroplan, or Flying Blue typically deliver 1.5-2 cents per point, well above portal or cash-back redemptions. The whole point of earning MR points is the transfer partner upside — use it.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• $120 Uber Cash: $10 per month, automatically credited to your Uber account. Use for rides or Uber Eats. Does not roll over month to month — use it or lose it by the 1st.
  • $120 Dining Credit: Up to $10 per month at participating restaurants and dining platforms: Grubhub (including Seamless), Buffalo Wild Wings, Five Guys, The Cheesecake Factory, and Wonder. Enrollment required. The list of participating merchants may change, so keep an eye on it.
  • $100 Resy Dining Credit: Up to $50 semiannually for in-person dining at U.S. Resy restaurants. Enroll once, but each $50 resets in January and July — mark your calendar.
  • $84 Dunkin' Credit: Up to $7 per month at U.S. Dunkin' locations. Enrollment required. Your morning Medium Iced, on Amex.
  • The Hotel Collection: Book two or more nights through Amex Travel and get a $100 credit toward eligible on-property charges, plus a room upgrade and 4pm late checkout when available.
  • Hertz Five Star Status: Complimentary mid-tier status in Hertz Gold+ Rewards, added in the 2026 refresh (enrollment and Hertz Gold+ registration required).
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees: A solid perk for international travel, and one that many competing cards don't offer.
  • Baggage Insurance Plan: Coverage for lost, damaged, or stolen baggage.
  • Trip Delay Insurance: Up to $300 per trip in reimbursed expenses when a round-trip paid entirely with the card is delayed more than 12 hours (max 2 claims per 12 months).
  • Car Rental Loss and Damage Insurance: Secondary coverage for damage or theft when you pay with the card and decline the rental company's CDW. No liability coverage, and rentals in Australia, Italy, and New Zealand aren't covered.
  • Purchase Protection: Up to $10,000 per covered purchase (and $50,000 per calendar year) for accidental damage, theft, or loss within 90 days of purchase.

Note: The Gold Card does not include lounge access, hotel elite status, or a Global Entry/TSA PreCheck credit. Those perks live on the Platinum Card. The Gold earns; the Platinum perks. That's the division of labor.

The Amex Gold dominates on dining and grocery earn rates — 4x in both categories is unmatched. The 2024 refresh added $184 in new credits (Resy + Dunkin') to further offset the fee increase. The Chase Sapphire Preferred is a much cheaper on-ramp to transferable points but earns less where it matters most. The Capital One Savor is the no-fee alternative for dining rewards, but you give up the transfer partner upside that makes the Amex Gold so powerful. If food is your biggest expense category, the Gold is the clear winner.

sections.title: Best For
sections.content: The Amex Gold is for anyone who spends real money on dining and groceries — which is, well, most people. With up to $424 in annual credits, the effective annual fee can drop below zero before you even count the value of points earned. Your restaurant tabs and grocery runs are literally funding future flights. It pairs perfectly with the Amex Platinum for a two-card setup that covers both travel perks and everyday spending, but it also works beautifully as a standalone daily driver for anyone who wants their food spending to turn into airline miles.

title: American Express Business Platinum
scouts_verdict: The 2025 refresh turned the Business Platinum into a legitimate powerhouse — but only for the right business. The bump from 1.5x to 2x on large purchases and on the tech, shipping, and hardware categories, plus the $600 hotel credit and $1,150 Dell credit? That's massive if your business actually spends in those categories. But at $895, you need to be buying Dell equipment, posting jobs on Indeed, AND traveling regularly. Otherwise, the Ink Business Preferred at $95 gives you 90% of the points value at 10% of the price.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
The Amex Business Platinum is built for business owners who spend big, travel often, and want their operating expenses to earn serious rewards. Think of it as the personal Platinum's more practical sibling — same lounge access, same hotel status, but with earning categories that actually make sense for a business. Following the 2025 refresh, the annual fee jumped to $895 (from $695), but Amex loaded it up with new benefits: a $600 hotel credit, enhanced Dell and Adobe credits, and Leaders Club Sterling hotel status. Amex now puts the card's total annual value at over $4,000 for businesses that can actually use the perks.

The headline for businesses: 5x on flights and prepaid hotels through Amex Travel, 2x on purchases of $5,000 or more (upgraded from 1.5x), and 2x (also up from 1.5x) on U.S. construction materials, hardware, electronics retailers, software/cloud providers, and shipping providers (up to $2 million per year). That last one is massive for any business buying tech, shipping product, or paying for SaaS tools. Oh, and there's the unique 35% points rebate when booking flights through Amex Travel — a perk no other card offers.

The card earns Membership Rewards points, transferable to the same 20+ airline and hotel partners as the personal Platinum. For businesses with significant spending volume and owners who travel for work, this card turns operating costs into first-class flights. That's the pitch, and it delivers — if you fit the profile.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• 5x Points on Flights and Hotels: 5x on flights and prepaid hotels booked through Amex Travel. The bread and butter for business travelers.
  • 2x Points on Purchases $5,000+: Earn 2x Membership Rewards points on single purchases of $5,000 or more (upgraded from 1.5x in the 2025 refresh). Buying equipment? Paying a big invoice? That's a lot of points.
  • 2x Points on Business Categories: U.S. construction material/hardware suppliers, electronic goods retailers, software and cloud system providers, and shipping providers (up to $2 million per calendar year). Finally, your AWS bill is earning something meaningful.
  • Centurion Lounge Access: Complimentary access to Centurion Lounges, Priority Pass Select, Delta Sky Clubs (10 visits a year when flying Delta), Escape Lounges, and Plaza Premium lounges — 1,550+ lounges across 140 countries. Business travel doesn't have to feel like business travel.
  • 35% Airline Points Rebate: Get 35% of your points back when you redeem for flights through Amex Travel with your selected airline. This is a sleeper benefit that makes portal bookings surprisingly competitive.
  • $600 Hotel Credit: Up to $300 semiannually for prepaid Fine Hotels + Resorts or The Hotel Collection bookings through Amex Travel. New with the 2025 refresh and a game-changer for road warriors.
  • $1,150 Dell Technologies Credit: Up to $150 in statement credits on direct Dell purchases, plus an additional $1,000 after spending $5,000+ at Dell in a calendar year. If your business buys Dell hardware, this is basically free money.
  • $360 Indeed Credit: Up to $90 per quarter on U.S. purchases made directly with Indeed, like sponsored job posts. Hiring? Amex is subsidizing it.
  • $250 Adobe Credit: $250 in statement credits after spending $600+ on U.S. purchases directly with Adobe per calendar year. Creative Cloud just got cheaper.
  • $200 Hilton Credit: Up to $50 per quarter for purchases made directly with Hilton. Nice perk for anyone who stays at Hiltons for work.
  • $200 Airline Fee Credit: Annual credit for incidental fees with a selected airline.
  • $120 Wireless Telephone Credit: Up to $10/month for U.S. wireless phone charges. Your phone bill, slightly less painful.
  • $120 Global Entry/TSA PreCheck Credit: $120 for Global Entry or up to $85 for TSA PreCheck, every 4 years.
  • Hilton Honors Gold Status: Complimentary (enrollment required). Daily food-and-beverage credit at U.S. Hilton hotels; continental breakfast at many Hilton hotels abroad.
  • Marriott Bonvoy Gold Elite Status: Complimentary (enrollment required).
  • Leaders Club Sterling Status: Complimentary status with The Leading Hotels of the World (enrollment required). Added in the 2025 refresh.
  • $219 CLEAR+ Credit: Annual statement credit for a CLEAR+ membership. Skip the TSA line.
  • $300 ChatGPT Business Credit: Up to $300 in statement credits per calendar year on U.S. purchases of ChatGPT Business (enrollment required). Your team's AI subscription, partly on Amex.
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees.
  • Employee Cards: No fee for Employee Business Expense Cards; Employee Business Platinum Cards are $400 each. Hand out no-fee Expense Cards to employees and rack up points on their spending.

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:
• Annual Fee: $895 (increased from $695 in the 2025 refresh; existing cardholders transitioned at renewal on or after December 2, 2025). Yes, it's steep. But for the right business, it's a rounding error compared to the value extracted.
  • Employee Cards: No annual fee for Employee Business Expense Cards; Employee Business Platinum Cards are $400 each (up from $350 before the 2025 refresh) and come with their own set of benefits.
  • Foreign Transaction Fees: None
  • Late Payment Fee: $39 or 2.99% of the past-due amount, whichever is greater
  • Note: As a charge card, the balance is generally due in full each month. Pay Over Time is available for eligible purchases with a variable APR. Cash flow planning is key here.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
The current public welcome offer for the Amex Business Platinum is as high as 300,000 Membership Rewards points after spending $20,000 on eligible purchases within the first 3 months of card membership. Amex personalizes the number, so yours may be lower. At roughly 2 cents per point, the top offer is worth approximately $6,000 in travel value. That could be a round-trip business class ticket to Asia. From a welcome bonus.

Offers vary by applicant, so check the Amex site to see what you're offered. The bonus is once per lifetime: if you have or have had the Business Platinum, you won't get it. If you're shown the full 300,000, grab it.

Tip: The $20,000 spend requirement is steep but very achievable for businesses with regular expenses. Time your application to coincide with large purchases — equipment, annual software renewals, ad spend, or inventory buys. The 2x bonus on $5,000+ purchases also kicks in from day one, stacking even more points during the welcome offer period. Smart timing can turn this into a massive points haul.

sections.title: Earning Rates
sections.content:
• 5x points: Flights and prepaid hotels booked through Amex Travel
  • 2x points: Purchases of $5,000 or more
  • 2x points: U.S. construction material and hardware suppliers
  • 2x points: Electronic goods retailers
  • 2x points: Software and cloud system providers
  • 2x points: Shipping providers
  • 1x points: All other purchases

The 2025 refresh was a significant upgrade here. The large-purchase multiplier went from 1.5x to 2x, and the four business categories got the same bump from 1.5x to 2x (up to $2 million per year combined). Let's put that in context: a business spending $100,000/year on qualifying vendors and large invoices earns an extra 100,000 points annually over the 1x base rate — worth roughly $2,000 in travel when transferred to airline partners. That's your next vacation, funded by your FedEx bills and AWS subscription. Combined with the 5x on booked travel, the card rewards businesses that consolidate spending on it.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
Business Platinum points are Membership Rewards points with all the same redemption firepower as the personal Platinum:

  • Transfer Partners (Best Value): Transfers to 20+ airline and hotel partners, mostly at 1:1 (Hilton is 1:2 and Aeromexico 1:1.6; Emirates, Cathay Pacific, JetBlue and Leading Hotels of the World transfer at less than 1:1). Same network, same value, same flexibility.
  • 35% Points Rebate: When redeeming points for flights with your selected airline through Amex Travel, you get 35% of the points back (up to 1 million points back per calendar year). This effectively makes each point worth ~1.54 cpp when booking through the portal — better than the standard 1 cpp portal rate and a legitimately clever way to book domestic flights.
  • Amex Travel Portal: Book flights at 1 cent per point. Straightforward, no-fuss option.
  • Statement Credits: Low value (~0.6 cpp). Not recommended unless you're desperate.
  • Pay With Points at Amazon: Available but poor value. Resist the temptation.

Best value: Transfer to airline partners for premium cabin flights when the sweet spots line up. When they don't, the 35% rebate makes Amex Travel portal bookings surprisingly efficient for domestic economy flights.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• $600 Hotel Credit: Up to $300 semiannually for prepaid Fine Hotels + Resorts or The Hotel Collection bookings through Amex Travel. New with the 2025 refresh and a standout addition. FHR stays include upgrades, breakfast, and property credits on top.
  • $1,150 Dell Technologies Credit: $150 base credit on Dell purchases, plus $1,000 bonus after $5,000+ in Dell spending per calendar year. If you're outfitting an office, this is enormous.
  • $360 Indeed Credit: Up to $90 per quarter on U.S. purchases made directly with Indeed, like sponsored job posts. Recruiting isn't cheap — this helps.
  • $250 Adobe Credit: $250 back after $600+ in Adobe purchases per calendar year. Designers and marketers, take note.
  • $200 Hilton Credit: Up to $50 per quarter for direct Hilton purchases. Easy to use if Hilton is your go-to chain.
  • $200 Airline Fee Credit: Annual credit for incidental fees with one selected airline per calendar year.
  • $120 Wireless Telephone Credit: Up to $10/month for wireless phone charges from major U.S. carriers. Small but steady.
  • $219 CLEAR+ Credit: Annual statement credit for CLEAR+ membership.
  • $300 ChatGPT Business Credit: Up to $300 per calendar year on U.S. ChatGPT Business purchases (enrollment required). Handy if your team already pays for it.
  • $120 Global Entry/TSA PreCheck Credit: $120 for Global Entry or up to $85 for TSA PreCheck, every 4 years. It can be anyone's application fee, as long as it's charged to the card.
  • Centurion Lounge Access: Same access as the personal Platinum — guests are $50 each unless you spend $75,000 in a calendar year, which unlocks two free guests. The lounges are just as good on a business card.
  • Priority Pass Select: Unlimited visits to 1,300+ Priority Pass lounges worldwide (enrollment required; restaurant locations excluded).
  • Delta Sky Club Access: When flying Delta on a same-day ticket, capped at 10 visits a year unless you spend $75,000 in a calendar year.
  • Hilton Gold + Marriott Gold Elite + Leaders Club Sterling Status: Complimentary with enrollment. Hilton Gold's breakfast abroad (a daily food-and-beverage credit in the U.S.) is the real MVP here.
  • Fine Hotels + Resorts Access: Premium hotel booking program with upgrades, breakfast, and credits. Business trips with FHR perks feel a lot less like work.
  • 35% Points Rebate on Flights: Unique to the Business Platinum when booking through Amex Travel with your selected airline. No other card does this.

This is the premium business card showdown, and it's closer than you'd think. The Capital One Venture X Business undercuts both on price at $395 and might actually win on raw value — 10x on portal hotels is absurd, the Capital One Lounges are genuinely excellent, and the $300 credit plus anniversary miles offset most of that fee. If you want a premium card that doesn't require a spreadsheet to justify, this is it.

The Chase Sapphire Reserve for Business has the best earning structure if you spend heavily on digital ads — 3x on social media and search engine advertising (capped at $1 million a year starting November 15, 2026) is something the Business Platinum can't match, and 8x on everything booked through Chase Travel is hard to argue with. The new Chase Sapphire Lounges are rolling out fast and the IHG Platinum Elite status is a nice throw-in. At $795 it's not cheap, but ad-heavy businesses will earn that back quickly.

The Amex Business Platinum justifies its $895 fee through sheer credit stacking. Dell, Indeed, ChatGPT, Adobe, Hilton, wireless, plus the hotel and airline credits — if your business naturally spends across those vendors, you can extract $3,000+ in annual value before you even earn a point. The Centurion Lounges remain the gold standard, and the 35% points rebate works on any Amex Travel flight with your selected airline, while Chase's Points Boost (worth up to 2 cents a point) only pops up on select bookings. But if you're not using those credits? The Venture X Business gives you 80% of the experience at less than half the price.

sections.title: Best For
sections.content: The Amex Business Platinum is for business owners who regularly make large purchases ($5,000+ at a time), have significant spend with tech/software/shipping vendors, travel frequently for work, and want to walk past the line at the Centurion Lounge. The 2025 refresh added serious value with the $600 hotel credit, enhanced Dell credit, and the bump from 1.5x to 2x on key business categories. But let's be real — if your business isn't spending at Dell, hiring on Indeed, or racking up hotel nights, the Chase Ink Business Preferred at $95 delivers better value for the money. Match the card to the business, not the other way around.

title: Chase Sapphire Preferred
scouts_verdict: The CSP is still the best entry point into transferable points at $95. You get the same 14+ transfer partners as the Reserve (though Hyatt now transfers at 4:3 on this card), 3x on dining, gas and streaming, and a $100 Chase Travel hotel credit that covers the fee on its own if you use it. If you travel even a couple times a year and want your spending to fund real trips, start here.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
The Chase Sapphire Preferred is the card that launched a thousand points obsessions. At $95 per year, it's the gateway drug to the Chase Ultimate Rewards ecosystem — giving you access to the full 14+ transfer partner network (the same one Sapphire Reserve cardholders use) along with solid earning rates on dining and travel. It's not the flashiest card in anyone's wallet, but it might be the smartest.

You earn Chase Ultimate Rewards points, one of the most valuable and flexible points currencies in the game. Points transfer 1:1 to partners like United, Southwest, British Airways, Air France/KLM Flying Blue, and more (World of Hyatt is now 4:3 on this card), or can be redeemed through Chase Travel at 1 cent each, up to 1.5 cents with Points Boost. Those transfer partners are what make the case for this card.

Chase positions the Sapphire Preferred as the on-ramp to its premium rewards ecosystem, and it nails that role. It pairs exceptionally well with no-annual-fee Chase Freedom cards (Flex, Unlimited, Rise) to build a points-earning machine that covers every spending category — without requiring you to pay $795 for the Sapphire Reserve. Start here, pool points, transfer to partners. That's the playbook.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• Transfer to 14+ Travel Partners: Transfer points 1:1 to United, Southwest, British Airways, Air France/KLM Flying Blue, Virgin Atlantic, IHG, Marriott, and more. World of Hyatt is the exception: 4:3 on this card (1,000 Chase points = 750 Hyatt points), right away if you applied on or after June 15, 2026, and from October 1, 2026 for everyone else. Still useful, just no longer the whole reason to hold the card.
  • Points Boost on Chase Travel: Points are worth up to 1.5 cents each on select hotels and flights through Chase Travel, and 1 cent on everything else there. (If you applied for the card before June 23, 2025, points earned before October 26, 2025 can still be redeemed at 1.25 cents in Chase Travel until October 26, 2027.)
  • $100 Annual Chase Travel Hotel Credit: Up to $100 in automatic statement credits for hotel stays booked through Chase Travel each account anniversary year, doubled from $50 in June 2026. Use it and it covers the $95 fee by itself.
  • 3x on Gas, EV Charging and Vacation Homes: New in June 2026: 3x points at gas stations, on EV charging, and on vacation homes booked directly with top brands like Airbnb and Vrbo.
  • Global Entry, TSA PreCheck or NEXUS Credit: Up to $120 back every four years when you pay the application fee with the card. Also new in June 2026.
  • Complimentary DashPass: One year of DoorDash DashPass membership (a $120 annual value) with free delivery and reduced fees when you activate by December 31, 2027, plus $10 off one non-restaurant order each month. Solid if you order delivery regularly.
  • A Year of Apple TV: Complimentary Apple TV for a year (a $156 value) when you activate by December 31, 2026. New in June 2026.
  • 5x Points on Lyft: Earn 5 total points per dollar on eligible Lyft purchases, including rides, bike and scooter rides, and memberships, through September 30, 2027.
  • Trip Cancellation/Interruption Insurance: Up to $10,000 per covered traveler and $20,000 per trip for pre-paid, non-refundable travel expenses. Underrated perk that can save you thousands.
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees: Use the card internationally without the typical 3% surcharge.
  • Primary Car Rental Insurance: Primary coverage (not secondary) when renting a car for business or personal use. This is a big deal — skip the rental counter CDW and save $15-30/day.

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:
• Annual Fee: $95 — one of the best values in the transferable points world.
  • Authorized User Fee: $0 per authorized user. Free is free.
  • Foreign Transaction Fees: None
  • APR: Variable, based on creditworthiness (19.24% - 27.49%)
  • Balance Transfer Fee: 5% of the amount transferred, $5 minimum
  • Late Payment Fee: Up to $40

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
The Chase Sapphire Preferred currently offers 75,000 bonus Ultimate Rewards points after spending $5,000 on purchases in the first 3 months from account opening.

Booked through Chase Travel at the base 1 cent per point, that bonus is worth $750, or up to $1,125 on Points Boost bookings at 1.5 cents. But through transfer partners, savvy redeemers can extract $1,200 or more in travel value — enough to cover a round-trip domestic flight in business class or a one-way international premium cabin ticket. Not bad for meeting a spend requirement you probably would've hit anyway.

Eligibility note (2026 update): Chase now judges bonus eligibility card by card: you can't open a Sapphire Preferred while you have one open, and the bonus may not be available if you've previously held this card or earned its bonus. This means current Sapphire Preferred holders can now apply for and earn the Sapphire Reserve bonus (and vice versa), which was not possible under the old rules. The 5/24 rule still applies: if you have opened 5 or more new credit cards in the past 24 months, you will likely be denied.

sections.title: Earning Rates
sections.content:
• 5x points: Travel purchased through Chase Travel (excluding hotel purchases that qualify for the $100 hotel credit)
  • 5x points: Eligible Lyft purchases, including rides, bike and scooter rides, and memberships (through September 30, 2027)
  • 5x points: Peloton equipment and accessory purchases over $150, on up to $5,000 in total purchases (through December 31, 2027)
  • 3x points: Dining, including restaurants, takeout, and eligible delivery services
  • 3x points: Gas stations and EV charging
  • 3x points: Vacation homes booked directly with top brands like Airbnb and Vrbo
  • 3x points: Select streaming services
  • 3x points: Online grocery purchases (excluding Target, Walmart, and wholesale clubs)
  • 2x points: Other travel purchases (airlines, hotels, car rentals booked directly)
  • 1x point: All other purchases

10% Anniversary Bonus (discontinued): Chase is retiring it as part of the June 2026 refresh. If you applied on or after June 15, 2026, you don't get it at all. If you applied earlier, purchases made through October 1, 2026 still earn the 10% bonus, paid by January 31, 2027 — and that's the last one.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
Chase Ultimate Rewards points are among the most flexible currencies in the rewards game, and here's what you can do with them:

  • Transfer Partners (Best Value): Transfer to 14+ airline and hotel partners including United MileagePlus, Southwest Rapid Rewards, British Airways Avios, Air France/KLM Flying Blue, Virgin Atlantic Flying Club, Singapore Airlines KrisFlyer, IHG One Rewards, and Marriott Bonvoy. Transfers are 1:1 except World of Hyatt, which is 4:3 on this card (1,000 Chase points = 750 Hyatt points): right away if you applied on or after June 15, 2026, and from October 1, 2026 for everyone else. Transfer partners are still the reason the CSP exists.
  • Chase Travel Portal: Redeem at 1 cent per point for flights, hotels, car rentals, and activities, or up to 1.5 cents on select hotels and flights with Points Boost. A solid fallback when transfer partners don't offer a better deal.
  • Pay Yourself Back: Redeem points as statement credits against rotating categories. Recent rates on the CSP ran 1.05 to 1.25 cents each, with 1.25 cents limited to charitable donations. Handy for flexibility.
  • Statement Credits: 1 cent per point when applied to any purchase — leaves value on the table, but it's there.
  • Gift Cards & Amazon: Generally 1 cent per point or less. Don't do this.

Best value: Transfer to airline partners for premium cabin international flights, or to World of Hyatt for hotel stays, but do the math at this card's 4:3 Hyatt ratio. A Hyatt Category 4 hotel that costs $250/night is 15,000 Hyatt points on a Low-priced night, which takes 20,000 Chase points at 4:3: 1.25 cents per point. Hyatt's new chart prices Category 4 anywhere from 12,000 to 25,000 points a night, so check the date before you transfer. Premium cabin flights are where the CSP still punches way above its weight class.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• $100 Chase Travel Hotel Credit: Up to $100 in statement credits for hotel stays booked through Chase Travel. Applied automatically each account anniversary year — nothing to activate or remember.
  • Global Entry, TSA PreCheck or NEXUS Credit: One statement credit of up to $120 every four years for the application fee, when you pay it with the card.
  • DashPass by DoorDash: Complimentary DashPass membership for one year, valued at $120/year, providing $0 delivery fees and reduced service fees on eligible DoorDash orders. Activate by December 31, 2027. DashPass members also get $10 off one non-restaurant order (groceries, retail and more) each calendar month through December 31, 2027. It doesn't roll over, so use it or lose it.
  • Apple TV: At least 12 months of complimentary Apple TV (a $156 value) for the primary cardmember when you activate on chase.com or the Chase Mobile app by December 31, 2026. If you already pay Apple for it, that plan pauses and picks back up when the free year ends.
  • Trip Cancellation/Interruption Insurance: Up to $10,000 per person, $20,000 per trip for pre-paid, non-refundable expenses when a trip is cancelled or cut short due to covered reasons. Book trips on this card for the peace of mind.
  • Primary Car Rental Coverage: Covers theft and collision damage up to $60,000 on most rental cars with an MSRP of $125,000 or less, when you charge the whole rental to the card and decline the rental company's CDW/LDW. Primary means it kicks in first — no filing through your personal auto insurance.
  • Trip Delay Reimbursement: Up to $500 per covered traveler for reasonable expenses when a common carrier delay exceeds 12 hours or requires an overnight stay.
  • Emergency Evacuation and Transportation: Up to $100,000 for emergency evacuation and medical transport if you or a covered traveler get sick or injured on a trip 100+ miles from home. New in June 2026.
  • Baggage Delay Insurance: Covers essential purchases up to $100/day for 5 days if bags are delayed 6+ hours.
  • Lost Luggage Reimbursement: Up to $3,000 per passenger for lost baggage.
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees: No 3% surcharge on purchases made outside the U.S.
  • Purchase Protection: Covers new purchases for 120 days against damage or theft, up to $500 per item, $50,000 per account.
  • Extended Warranty: Extends U.S. manufacturer warranties by one additional year on eligible items.

The Sapphire Preferred wins on one thing that matters enormously: transfer partner quality. Hyatt is still on the list, but at 4:3 on this card it's a nice extra rather than the whole case. The 1:1 airline partners like United, Southwest and British Airways do the heavy lifting now. The Amex Gold earns more on dining and groceries but costs $325 — it's a different conversation. The Capital One Venture offers the simplicity of 2x on everything, but its transfer partners don't include United, Southwest or Hyatt. The Citi Strata Premier is a solid competitor with its own transfer network, but the CSP's ecosystem advantage (Freedom cards pooling points) gives it the edge.

sections.title: Best For
sections.content: The Chase Sapphire Preferred is for anyone who wants premium transfer partners without paying a premium annual fee. If you eat out a few times a week, fill up at the pump, travel a few times a year, and like the idea of that spending turning into flights and hotel stays, this is your card. It also shines as the anchor in a broader Chase ecosystem: pool points from Freedom Flex, Freedom Unlimited, and Freedom Rise into one high-value Ultimate Rewards balance, then transfer to airline or hotel partners when you're ready to book. It's the $95 card that punches like a $300 card.

title: Chase Sapphire Reserve
scouts_verdict: The revamped Reserve throws the kitchen sink at you — $500 hotel credit, $300 dining, $300 StubHub, $300 DoorDash, free Apple subscriptions — and the 8x on Chase Travel is legitimately best-in-class. But at $795, the math only works if you actually use those category-specific credits. If you'll hit the hotel credit, eat at Exclusive Tables restaurants, and go to concerts on StubHub, this card pays for itself several times over. If you're squinting at that list thinking "maybe I'll use some of it..." the Venture X at $395 is the smarter call.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
The Chase Sapphire Reserve got a complete makeover in June 2025, and the result is... a lot of card. At $795 per year, Chase is no longer playing in the "affordable premium" space — this is a direct shot at the Amex Platinum, loaded with credits, benefits, and earning rates that are genuinely best-in-class. Whether the price tag is worth it depends entirely on whether you'll actually use what's inside the box.

The numbers are hard to ignore: 8x on Chase Travel and 4x on direct airline and hotel bookings are among the highest earn rates on any credit card. Chase now claims over $3,000 in annual value, with credits spanning hotels, dining, entertainment, rideshare, delivery, and streaming. That's a lot of credits — the question is whether they align with how you actually spend.

Like the Sapphire Preferred, the Reserve earns Chase Ultimate Rewards points transferable to 14+ airline and hotel partners. But Reserve cardholders get Points Boost worth up to 2 cents per point on select flights and hotels through Chase Travel (the Preferred tops out at 1.5 cents), and the Reserve still transfers to World of Hyatt at 1:1 after the Preferred dropped to 4:3 in 2026. Combine that with Priority Pass and the expanding Chase Sapphire Lounge network, and you've got a card built for travelers who want to go all in.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• Chase Sapphire Lounge Access: Complimentary access to Chase Sapphire Lounges by The Club for cardholder plus two guests. The lounge network is expanding and the early reviews are positive — Chase is clearly investing here.
  • Priority Pass Select: Unlimited access to 1,300+ Priority Pass lounges worldwide. Your backup plan for airports without a Sapphire Lounge.
  • $300 Annual Travel Credit: Automatic statement credits for a broad range of travel purchases including flights, hotels, car rentals, parking, tolls, and transit.
  • $500 Annual Hotel Credit (The Edit): Statement credits for stays with The Edit by Chase Travel (up to $250 per transaction). That's a lot of free hotel nights if you book through the portal.
  • $300 Annual Dining Credit: Statement credits through the Sapphire Reserve Exclusive Tables dining program ($150 per half-year). Fancy dinners, partially subsidized by Chase.
  • $300 Annual StubHub Credit: Statement credit for concert and event ticket purchases on StubHub. Concert lovers, this one's for you.
  • $300 Annual DoorDash Credit: Monthly DoorDash promos plus complimentary DashPass membership (valued at $120/year). Your late-night delivery habit, enabled.
  • $120 Annual Lyft Credit: Up to $10 per month in Lyft in-app credits. Use it for rides or lose it — doesn't roll over.
  • Complimentary Apple TV and Apple Music: Free subscriptions through June 22, 2027, a combined value of $288 per year.
  • $120 Annual Peloton Credit: Up to $10/month in statement credits toward eligible Peloton memberships through December 31, 2027.
  • IHG One Rewards Platinum Elite Status: Complimentary Platinum Elite status through December 31, 2027 — room upgrades, bonus points, and late checkout at IHG properties.
  • 8x Points on Chase Travel: Industry-leading earn rate on all travel booked through the Chase portal. That's not a typo — 8x.
  • 4x Points on Direct Flights and Hotels: Strong earn rate when booking directly with airlines and hotels. Most premium cards max out at 3-5x here.
  • Points Boost (up to 2x): Points worth up to 2 cents each on select flights and hotels booked through Chase Travel (1 cent on everything else). A 100K balance = up to $2,000 in boosted travel.
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees.

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:
• Annual Fee: $795 (applies to new applicants from June 23, 2025; existing cardholders transitioned on renewal after October 26, 2025). Not cheap. Not pretending to be.
  • Authorized User Fee: $195 per authorized user card
  • Foreign Transaction Fees: None
  • APR: Variable, based on creditworthiness (currently 19.49% - 27.99%)
  • Late Payment Fee: Up to $40

Effective annual fee: After credits ($300 travel + $500 hotel + $300 dining + $300 StubHub + $300 DoorDash + $120 Lyft + $120 Peloton + $288 Apple subscriptions), the card delivers over $2,000 in potential annual credits against the $795 fee. If you use even half of those, you're in the green. The real question isn't whether the math works — it's whether you'll use the credits.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
The Chase Sapphire Reserve currently offers 100,000 bonus Ultimate Rewards points after spending $6,000 on purchases in the first 3 months from account opening. That's a massive welcome offer.

With Points Boost at up to 2 cents per point on select Chase Travel flights and hotels, this bonus is worth up to $2,000 (or $1,000 at the standard 1 cent). Through transfer partners, particularly World of Hyatt, the value can climb past $2,000. We're talking enough points for multiple free hotel stays or a premium cabin flight — from the welcome bonus alone.

Eligibility note (2026 update): Starting in late January 2026, Chase updated its Sapphire bonus rules. You can now earn one welcome bonus per Sapphire product. Chase's terms say the bonus may not be available if you previously held that specific card or already received its bonus, and you can't be approved for a Reserve while you have one open. Holding a Sapphire Preferred no longer blocks you from earning the Reserve bonus. Chase's unofficial 5/24 rule still applies.

sections.title: Earning Rates
sections.content:
• 8x points: All travel booked through Chase Travel (flights, hotels, car rentals, activities, tours)
  • 5x points: Lyft rides (through September 30, 2027)
  • 10x points: Eligible Peloton equipment and accessory purchases over $150 (through December 31, 2027)
  • 4x points: Flights and hotel stays booked directly with airlines or hotels
  • 3x points: Dining at restaurants, including takeout and eligible delivery
  • 1x point: All other purchases

Important heads-up from the 2025 refresh: The old general 3x travel category is gone, replaced by a more targeted structure. Direct airline and hotel bookings now earn 4x (upgrade), but non-hotel, non-flight travel spending — think Airbnb, subway, cruises, tolls — dropped to 1x (downgrade). If you used to earn 3x on rideshares and transit, that's a hit. The card now rewards booking flights and hotels, not all travel. Know the difference before you swipe.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
Reserve cardholders get the full Ultimate Rewards toolkit, with enhanced rates that justify the premium:

  • Transfer Partners (Best Value): Transfer 1:1 to 14+ airline and hotel partners. The lineup is identical to the Sapphire Preferred: World of Hyatt, United, Southwest, British Airways, Air France/KLM Flying Blue, Virgin Atlantic, Singapore Airlines KrisFlyer, IHG, Marriott, and others. Hyatt transfers remain the gold standard — Hyatt's award charts can deliver outsize value on the right stays — and unlike the Preferred (cut to 4:3 in 2026), the Reserve still transfers to Hyatt at 1:1. This is where Reserve points shine brightest.
  • Chase Travel Portal (Points Boost): Redeem at up to 2 cents per point on select flights and hotels with Points Boost (the Preferred tops out at 1.5 cents); everything else books at 1 cent. A 100,000-point balance is worth up to $2,000 on boosted bookings. When transfer partners don't have the award space, this is a great Plan B. Cardholders who applied before June 23, 2025 can still redeem points earned before October 26, 2025 at 1.5 cents through October 26, 2027.
  • Pay Yourself Back: Redeem as statement credits against rotating categories, recently at 1.2 to 1.25 cents per point (1.5 cents only for select charities).
  • Statement Credits: 1 cent per point against any purchase. Leaving value on the table, but it exists.
  • Gift Cards & Shopping: Generally 1 cent per point or less. You know better.

Best value: Transfer to World of Hyatt for hotel stays or airline partners for premium cabin flights. Points Boost (up to 2 cents) is also excellent for straightforward bookings where transfer partners don't offer a significant advantage. Having both options is the Reserve's superpower.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• $300 Travel Credit: Annual statement credit for a broad range of travel purchases including flights, hotels, car rentals, parking, tolls, and transit. Easy to use.
  • $500 Hotel Credit (The Edit): Annual statement credits for hotel stays with The Edit by Chase Travel, capped at $250 per transaction. The Edit is Chase's curated hotel collection — think boutique and upscale properties.
  • $250 Select Hotel Credit (2026): Statement credit through 12/31/2026 for prepaid Chase Travel hotel bookings at select hotel chains including IHG, Montage, Pendry, Omni, Virgin Hotels, Minor Hotels, and Pan Pacific.
  • $300 Dining Credit: Annual credits ($150 per half: Jan-Jun and Jul-Dec) for dining at restaurants participating in the Sapphire Reserve Exclusive Tables program. Great if participating restaurants are near you — check the list.
  • $300 StubHub Credit: Annual credit for concert and event tickets purchased through StubHub. If you go to even two or three shows a year, this pays for itself.
  • $300 DoorDash Credit: Annual credits in monthly DoorDash promos, plus complimentary DashPass membership worth $120/year. Between the credit and DashPass, your delivery game is fully funded.
  • $120 Lyft Credit: Up to $10/month in Lyft in-app credits, plus 5x points on eligible Lyft rides. Monthly use-it-or-lose-it.
  • Apple TV + Apple Music: Complimentary subscriptions through June 22, 2027 (combined ~$288/year value). If you were already paying for these, instant win.
  • Chase Sapphire Lounge Access: Complimentary entry for cardholder + 2 guests at Chase Sapphire Lounges by The Club. The network is growing — DFW opened in July 2026, with LAX and more on the way.
  • Priority Pass Select: Unlimited access to 1,300+ airport lounges worldwide.
  • Trip Cancellation/Interruption Insurance: Up to $10,000 per person, $20,000 per trip.
  • Primary Car Rental Coverage: Primary collision/theft coverage when renting vehicles. Skip the rental counter insurance.
  • Trip Delay Reimbursement: Up to $500 per covered traveler for delays over 6 hours or requiring an overnight stay.
  • Global Entry/TSA PreCheck Credit: Up to $120 every 4 years (Global Entry, TSA PreCheck, or NEXUS).
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees.
  • $120 Peloton Credit: Up to $10/month in statement credits toward eligible Peloton memberships through 12/31/2027.
  • IHG One Rewards Platinum Elite: Complimentary Platinum Elite status through 12/31/2027 for room upgrades, late checkout, and bonus points at IHG hotels.

The Reserve now leads on raw earning rates, but the Platinum still packs more in total credits — and at $795, the Reserve is only $100 cheaper. The Amex Platinum still has the better lounges — Centurion Lounges are in a different league, and Delta Sky Club access is a killer perk. Hotel status (Hilton Gold, Marriott Gold) also stays with the Platinum, though the Reserve counters with IHG Platinum Elite. The Reserve is for people who want the best of everything and are willing to pay for it. The Venture X is for people who want 80% of the experience at half the price.

sections.title: Best For
sections.content: The Sapphire Reserve is for high-spending travelers who will actively use the credits — not just admire them. If you naturally stay at hotels, eat at restaurants, go to concerts on StubHub, order DoorDash, and take Lyft rides, the $795 fee pays for itself and then some. The 8x on Chase Travel is best-in-class, and Points Boost can make your points worth up to 2 cents each on select flights and hotels. But if the words "Exclusive Tables" and "The Edit" make you think "I'd never use that," save yourself the fee and grab the Sapphire Preferred or Venture X instead. This card rewards active use, not passive holding.

title: Chase Ink Business Preferred
scouts_verdict: The Ink Business Preferred might be the best-kept secret in the Chase lineup. For $95 a year, you get 3x on advertising, shipping, internet, phone, and travel up to $150,000 — categories where most businesses spend heavily without thinking about rewards. Access to Chase's airline and hotel transfer partners (though Hyatt transfers drop to 4:3 on October 1, 2026), a 100,000-point welcome bonus, and phone protection worth more than the annual fee. If you have a business — even a side hustle — and you don't have this card, you're leaving serious points on the table.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Here's a card that doesn't get enough credit (pun intended): the Chase Ink Business Preferred. For $95 a year — the same as the consumer Sapphire Preferred — you get 3x Ultimate Rewards points on the first $150,000 in combined spending across travel, shipping, internet/cable/phone services, and social media/search engine advertising. Those are categories where businesses routinely drop thousands per month without thinking twice.

But here's the real kicker: the Ink Business Preferred gives you direct access to Chase's transfer partner network. Chase's Ink page lists 13 airline and hotel programs — Hyatt, United, Southwest, British Airways and more. One catch: starting October 1, 2026, Ink Preferred transfers to Hyatt drop to 4:3 (1,000 Chase points = 750 Hyatt points), and the Sapphire Reserve isn't part of that cut. Many points enthusiasts hold this card alongside a Sapphire Preferred or Reserve, pooling all their Ultimate Rewards into one giant pile of travel potential.

For small business owners, freelancers, and anyone with a legitimate side hustle, this is one of the highest-value cards available at any annual fee. The 100,000-point welcome bonus alone can fund a week of hotel stays. And you're paying $95 for the privilege.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• 3x Points on Business Categories: Earn 3 points per dollar on the first $150,000 in combined annual spending on travel, shipping, internet/cable/phone services, and social media and search engine advertising. That $150K cap is generous — most small businesses won't touch it.
  • Airline and Hotel Transfer Partners: Chase lists 13 for the Ink — Hyatt, United, Southwest, British Airways, Flying Blue, Virgin Atlantic, and more. Transfers are 1:1, except Hyatt, which drops to 4:3 on October 1, 2026.
  • Points Boost in Chase Travel: Points are worth 1 cent each in Chase Travel, or up to 1.5 cents on select Points Boost flights and hotels (same as Sapphire Preferred). The old flat 1.25-cent rate is gone for new cardmembers; if you opened the card before June 23, 2025, only points earned before October 26, 2025 still get it, until October 26, 2027.
  • Cell Phone Protection: Up to $1,000 per claim for damage or theft when you pay your monthly cell phone bill with this card. Covers the phones listed on that bill. This benefit alone can replace phone insurance — and probably save you money doing it.
  • Trip Cancellation/Interruption Insurance: Up to $5,000 per person, $10,000 per trip.
  • Purchase Protection: Up to $10,000 per item for damage or theft within 120 days of purchase.
  • Extended Warranty: Extends manufacturer warranties by one year.
  • Auto Rental Collision Damage Waiver: Primary coverage when you rent for business purposes. Skip the rental counter upsell.
  • Free Employee Cards: Add employee cards at no extra cost with customizable spending limits, earning points on their purchases. Your employees spend, you earn the points. Everybody wins (mostly you).
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees.

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:
• Annual Fee: $95 — and honestly, it feels like a steal for what you get.
  • Employee Card Fee: $0 per employee card
  • Foreign Transaction Fees: None
  • APR: Variable, based on creditworthiness (currently 17.74% - 26.74%)
  • Balance Transfer: Chase's terms list a fee of $5 or 5% (whichever is greater), but also say this account may not be eligible for balance transfers — don't count on it
  • Late Payment Fee: Up to $40

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
The Chase Ink Business Preferred currently offers 100,000 bonus Ultimate Rewards points after spending $8,000 on purchases in the first 3 months from account opening.

In Chase Travel, the bonus is worth $1,000 at the standard 1 cent per point, or up to $1,500 on flights and hotels carrying a 1.5-cent Points Boost. Through transfer partners the value can reach $1,500-$2,000 or more — Hyatt is still on the list, but Ink Preferred transfers there drop to 4:3 on October 1, 2026. The 100,000-point offer is considered a strong public offer. If you're seeing 100K, that's a good time to apply.

The $8,000 spending requirement in 3 months is higher than most consumer cards, but come on — if you're running a business, you probably spend that on advertising and shipping in a slow month. Time your application around large planned purchases to hit the threshold naturally.

Eligibility note: Chase says the bonus may not be available to you if you have ever had this card, and it may also weigh factors about your business. Chase's 5/24 rule also applies to business card applications.

sections.title: Earning Rates
sections.content:
• 3x points: Travel (airlines, hotels, car rentals, trains, taxis, tolls, parking, travel agencies)
  • 3x points: Shipping purchases
  • 3x points: Internet, cable, and phone services
  • 3x points: Social media and search engine advertising (Google Ads, Meta Ads, LinkedIn, X/Twitter, etc.)
  • 5x points: Lyft rides (through September 30, 2027)
  • 1x point: All other purchases

The 3x categories have a combined annual cap of $150,000 in spending per account anniversary year. After hitting $150,000 in combined bonus spending, those categories revert to 1x. For most small businesses, the $150,000 cap is more than generous — it means you can earn up to 450,000 points per year just from the 3x categories alone. That's $5,600+ in travel value at conservative transfer partner rates. From a $95 card.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
The Ink Business Preferred gives you the Chase Ultimate Rewards arsenal — transfer partners, Chase Travel, and plenty of flexibility:

  • Transfer Partners (Best Value): Transfer 1:1 (Hyatt drops to 4:3 on October 1, 2026) to the 13 airline and hotel partners Chase lists for the Ink: World of Hyatt, United MileagePlus, Southwest Rapid Rewards, British Airways Avios, Air France/KLM Flying Blue, Virgin Atlantic Flying Club, Singapore Airlines KrisFlyer, IHG One Rewards, Marriott Bonvoy, Air Canada Aeroplan, and others. Chase's Sapphire Preferred page also lists Wyndham Rewards, and the Reserve isn't part of the Hyatt 4:3 cut.
  • Chase Travel Portal (Points Boost): Points are worth 1 cent each for travel, or up to 1.5 cents on select Points Boost flights and hotels. If you opened the card before June 23, 2025, points earned before October 26, 2025 still redeem at 1.25 cents until October 26, 2027. If you also hold a Sapphire Reserve, you can pool points and use the Reserve's Points Boost of up to 2 cents instead.
  • Pay Yourself Back: Statement credits against eligible purchases in whatever categories Chase is currently offering. Check the rate in your account before you redeem — don't assume it beats 1 cent per point.
  • Statement Credits: 1 cent per point against any purchase. Works, but you're leaving value on the table.
  • Gift Cards: Generally 1 cent per point or less. Don't.

Pro tip: If you hold both the Ink Business Preferred and a Sapphire Reserve, move your Ink points to the Reserve account to unlock the Reserve's Points Boost of up to 2 cents per point in Chase Travel. This is one of the most popular Chase stacking strategies — and it works beautifully. The Reserve also isn't on Chase's list for the Hyatt 4:3 change that hits the Ink on October 1, 2026, but check the Hyatt rate Ultimate Rewards shows before you transfer points you've moved.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• Cell Phone Protection: Up to $1,000 per claim ($100 deductible) for damage or theft to cell phones listed on your wireless bill, when you pay the bill with this card. Covers up to 3 claims per 12-month period. Let's be real — this benefit alone can save you more than the $95 annual fee. Ditch the phone insurance.
  • Trip Cancellation/Interruption Insurance: Up to $5,000 per person and $10,000 per trip for pre-paid, non-refundable expenses.
  • Auto Rental Collision Damage Waiver: Primary coverage when you rent a car for business purposes and decline the rental agency's CDW/LDW.
  • Purchase Protection: Covers eligible purchases against damage or theft for 120 days, up to $10,000 per item and $50,000 per account.
  • Extended Warranty Protection: Extends U.S. manufacturer warranties by one additional year on eligible items.
  • Roadside Dispatch: Access to roadside assistance services (towing, flat tire, lockout, etc.) for a per-service fee.
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees: No surcharge on purchases made abroad — useful for businesses with international suppliers or travel.
  • Free Employee Cards: Issue cards to employees at no cost and set individual spending limits. You earn points on all employee card spending. It's like having a points-earning army.
  • DoorDash DashPass: Complimentary DashPass for at least 12 months when you activate by December 31, 2027, plus up to $10 off one grocery or retail (non-restaurant) DoorDash order each month while you're enrolled.

The Amex Business Gold earns a higher 4x in its top categories, but at nearly 4x the annual fee — you'd need to spend a lot more to justify that gap. The Capital One Spark Cash Plus is the "I just want simple cash back" option, and that's fine, but you're giving up the massive upside of transfer partners. For businesses spending on ads, shipping, and internet services, the Ink Preferred's 3x on $150K is absurdly good value at $95.

sections.title: Best For
sections.content: The Ink Business Preferred is for small business owners, freelancers, and side-hustlers who spend meaningfully on advertising, shipping, internet services, phone bills, or travel — and want those routine expenses to generate transferable points instead of disappearing into the void. It's especially powerful when paired with a Sapphire Reserve: pool your points there to use the Reserve's Points Boost of up to 2 cents per point in Chase Travel. And honestly, the cell phone protection alone can justify the $95 fee. If you have any legitimate business expenses, this card should already be in your wallet.

title: Capital One Venture X
scouts_verdict: The Venture X is the best value in premium travel cards, and it's honestly not that close. Between the $300 travel credit, 10,000 anniversary miles, and free lounge access for you (guests and authorized users now cost extra), you're getting paid to hold this card. Flat 2x on everything, growing lounge network, transferable miles — all for an effective cost of negative five dollars. If the Amex Platinum is a luxury sports car, the Venture X is a Tesla that's somehow free after tax credits. It just makes sense.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
The Capital One Venture X walked into the premium travel card space in late 2021 and immediately made the incumbents nervous — and for good reason. At $395 per year, it delivers lounge access, transferable miles, a generous welcome bonus, and enough credits to make the card effectively free to hold. It competes with cards costing $550-$895 and doesn't break a sweat doing it.

The Venture X has quickly become the go-to recommendation for travelers who want premium perks without premium pricing. A flat 2x miles on every purchase (with portal bonuses on top), a growing lounge network, and lounge access for authorized users at $125/yr each (Chase and Amex charge $195 per authorized user card) — it's the card that makes you wonder what exactly you're paying extra for with the Amex Platinum. Issued on the Visa Infinite network, it's accepted basically everywhere.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• Capital One Lounge & Priority Pass Access: Complimentary entry for the primary cardholder at Capital One Lounges (DFW, IAD, DEN, LAS, JFK, plus Landings at DCA and LGA, and expanding). Guests cost $45 each ($25 for kids) unless you spend $75,000 on the card in a calendar year. Also includes Priority Pass membership (guests $35 each). The Capital One Lounges are genuinely impressive — craft cocktails, chef-curated food, shower suites. Not your average Priority Pass experience.
  • $300 Annual Travel Credit: Applied at checkout on bookings made through the Capital One Travel portal each account year — covers flights, hotels, and rental cars, and you can split it across multiple bookings. No activation, no enrollment, just book and apply it.
  • 10,000-Mile Anniversary Bonus: Receive 10,000 bonus miles (worth at least $100) on each account anniversary. Combined with the $300 credit, you're looking at a negative effective annual fee. Yes, the card pays you.
  • Transferable Miles: Capital One miles transfer to 15+ airline and hotel partners (most at 1:1) including Air Canada Aeroplan, Turkish Miles & Smiles, British Airways Avios, Wyndham, and Accor. The network keeps growing.
  • Visa Infinite Benefits: Cell phone protection (up to $800/claim), travel accident insurance, trip cancellation/interruption coverage, auto rental CDW, and no foreign transaction fees. Visa Infinite is the good stuff.
  • Global Entry / TSA PreCheck Credit: Up to $120 statement credit every four years for a Global Entry or TSA PreCheck application fee.
  • Hertz President's Circle Status: Complimentary top-tier Hertz rental car status. Skip the line, get the upgrades.

sections.content:
