Let's do the math: The $300 travel credit and 10,000-mile anniversary bonus (worth ~$100) reduce the net annual cost to roughly -$5. Read that again. Capital One is effectively paying you to hold this card. You just have to book one trip through their portal per year. That's it.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content: Earn 75,000 bonus miles after spending $4,000 on purchases within the first 3 months of account opening (not available if you've received a Venture X bonus in the past 48 months). These miles are worth at least $750 when redeemed through Capital One Travel, and potentially more through transfer partners. For a card with an effective negative annual fee, that's an outstanding welcome offer. The spend requirement is reasonable too — $4,000 in 3 months is doable for most people without manufactured spending.

sections.title: Earning Rates
sections.content:
• 10x miles on hotels and rental cars booked through Capital One Travel
  • 5x miles on flights and vacation rentals booked through Capital One Travel
  • 2x miles on all other purchases

That flat 2x on everything is the Venture X's secret weapon. No categories to track, no caps, no quarterly activation nonsense. Every dollar earns 2 miles, and those miles are transferable — a combination that's genuinely rare at any price point, let alone $395. The portal bonuses stack nicely for travelers who book through Capital One Travel, though transfer partners often yield better value per mile.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
• Transfer to Partners: Mostly 1:1 transfers to 15+ airlines and hotels. Top-value partners include Air Canada Aeroplan, Avianca LifeMiles, British Airways Avios, and Wyndham Rewards. Turkish Miles & Smiles used to be the hidden gem (business class to Europe for 45,000 miles), but a February 2024 devaluation raised those prices sharply and made connecting itineraries price per segment.
  • Capital One Travel Portal: Redeem at a fixed 1 cent per mile for flights, hotels, and car rentals. Simple, no-fuss option.
  • Cover Your Purchases: Apply miles as a statement credit against recent travel purchases at 1 cent per mile. Effectively 2% cash back on travel — decent floor value.
  • Gift Cards & Cash Back: Available but typically yield less than 1 cent per mile — don't bother.

The sweet spot for Venture X holders is transferring miles to airline partners for premium cabin redemptions, where valuations of 1.5-3+ cents per mile are very achievable. Since Turkish's 2024 devaluation, Air Canada Aeroplan and Avianca LifeMiles are usually the better picks for Star Alliance business class.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• $300 Annual Travel Credit: Applied at checkout on Capital One Travel portal bookings. Resets each account anniversary year. No hoops to jump through.
  • 10,000 Anniversary Miles: Deposited automatically each year on account anniversary. Free points for existing.
  • Capital One Lounges: Free for the primary cardholder. Guests are $45 each ($25 for kids) unless you spend $75,000 in a calendar year, and authorized users need the $125/yr lounge add-on. Lounges feature chef-curated menus, craft cocktails, shower suites, and relaxation rooms. These are genuinely excellent lounges — not the sad Priority Pass experience you're used to.
  • Priority Pass: Lounges only — Capital One excludes Priority Pass restaurant credits and other non-lounge experiences, and guests cost $35 each. The fallback for airports without a Capital One Lounge.
  • Global Entry / TSA PreCheck: $120 credit every 4 years.
  • Hertz President's Circle: Complimentary elite status for car rentals. Top-tier Hertz status for free — upgrades and skip-the-line access.
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees: Use freely abroad without surcharges.
  • Cell Phone Protection: Up to $800 per claim ($50 deductible, 2 claims/year) when you pay your monthly cell phone bill with the card. Another perk that quietly pays for itself.

Here's the uncomfortable truth for Amex and Chase: the Venture X hits the lowest effective cost among premium travel cards with a $395 fee and a single portal booking a year, while matching or exceeding most benefits. The Sapphire Reserve only ties it on paper, and that takes a $795 fee plus two prepaid stays with The Edit. Lounge access for authorized users at $125 a head? But for most travelers, the Venture X delivers 80-90% of the premium experience at roughly half the annual fee.

sections.content:

  • Families or couples who want lounge access for authorized users — $125/yr each, cheaper than the $195 per authorized user Chase and Amex charge

  • First-time premium cardholders who want to try the premium lifestyle without committing to an $895 fee
  • International travelers who need no foreign transaction fees and Visa Infinite acceptance worldwide

title: Capital One Venture
scouts_verdict: The Venture is the reliable mid-tier card that never tries too hard and never lets you down. 2x on everything (5x on hotels, vacation rentals, rental cars and activities booked through Capital One Travel), solid transfer partners (Turkish Miles & Smiles is a hidden gem), no category nonsense. It won't dazzle — the CSP has Hyatt, the Strata Premier has broader 3x categories — but it also won't make you think about which card to use at checkout. If you want a simple, no-drama travel card at $95, this is the one.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
The Capital One Venture is the "I don't want to think about bonus categories" card, and there's absolutely nothing wrong with that. At $95 per year, it earns 2x miles on every purchase — no tracking, no caps, no quarterly activations, no merchant category code headaches. Just swipe and earn. Book hotels, vacation rentals, rental cars or activities through Capital One Travel and that jumps to 5x.

With access to Capital One's growing 15+ transfer partner network and a solid 75,000-mile welcome bonus, the Venture sits comfortably in the mid-tier travel card segment, going head-to-head with the Chase Sapphire Preferred. It won't win awards for flashy perks or category multipliers, but it will quietly earn you miles on every single dollar while you go about your life. Sometimes boring is beautiful.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• Unlimited 2x Miles on Every Purchase: No categories to track, no caps, no enrollment. Every dollar, every purchase, at least 2 miles. The simplicity is the benefit.
  • 5x Through Capital One Travel and Entertainment: Hotels, vacation rentals, rental cars and activities booked through Capital One Travel earn 5x, and so do tickets bought through Capital One Entertainment. Flights booked through the portal earn the standard 2x.
  • Transferable Miles: Access to 15+ airline and hotel transfer partners, most at 1:1 (Emirates, EVA Air and Japan Airlines transfer at 2:1.5, JetBlue at 5:3 and Accor at 2:1, while I Prefer is a better 1:2) — the same partners available to Venture X holders. Turkish Miles & Smiles, Aeroplan, Avios — the good stuff is all here.
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees: Use anywhere abroad without additional charges. Essential for any travel card.
  • Global Entry / TSA PreCheck Credit: Up to $120 reimbursement every four years. Put toward Global Entry's $120 fee, it covers more than a full year's annual fee, once every four years.
  • Travel Accident Insurance: Coverage when purchasing travel with the card.
  • Flexible Redemption: Use miles through the travel portal, transfer to partners, or erase recent travel purchases via Purchase Eraser. Options are nice to have.

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:
Annual Fee$95

At $95 per year, the Venture needs roughly $4,750 in annual spending for its 2x miles (at 1 cent each) to earn back the fee — a bar most cardholders clear in a few months. And that break-even calculation doesn't factor in the transfer partner upside, which can push the value of your miles well beyond 1 cent each, or the Global Entry credit.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content: Earn 75,000 bonus miles after spending $4,000 on purchases within the first 3 months of account opening. At a minimum floor value of 1 cent per mile, that is $750 in travel — a fantastic return on a $95 annual fee card. Transfer to the right partner and you can push that well above $1,000. The $4,000 spend requirement is very reasonable for most people. The welcome offer also includes a one-time $300 Capital One Travel credit for hotel and vacation rental bookings, valid for the first cardholder year (limited-time offer — check if still available before applying). One catch: you're not eligible if you've earned a Venture or Venture X new cardmember bonus in the past 48 months.

sections.title: Earning Rates
sections.content:
• 5x miles on hotels, vacation rentals, rental cars and activities booked through Capital One Travel (flights booked there earn the standard 2x)
  • 5x miles on tickets bought through Capital One Entertainment
  • 2x miles on all other purchases

The simplicity is the feature, not a limitation. No rotating categories, no spending tiers, no activation requirements. Every dollar earns at least 2 miles, and those miles are transferable to airline and hotel partners — a combination that's surprisingly rare at this price point. You won't maximize every spending category, but you'll never miss a bonus either.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
• Transfer to Partners: Transfers to 15+ airlines and hotels, most at 1:1, including Air Canada Aeroplan, Turkish Miles & Smiles, British Airways Avios, Avianca LifeMiles, and Wyndham Rewards. Check the ratio before you move miles: Emirates, EVA Air and Japan Airlines are 2:1.5, JetBlue is 5:3 and Accor is 2:1 (I Prefer goes the other way, 1:2). Turkish Miles & Smiles is the standout — some of the best business class award rates available anywhere.
  • Capital One Travel Portal: Book travel at 1 cent per mile. Straightforward and easy.
  • Purchase Eraser: Erase recent travel purchases at 1 cent per mile as a statement credit. Basically turns this into a 2% travel cash back card — not exciting, but reliable.
  • Gift Cards & Cash Back: Available but at reduced value — hard pass.

The optimal play is accumulating miles and transferring to partners for outsized value, particularly on premium cabin flights. For simpler needs, the Purchase Eraser is a hassle-free alternative that still returns an effective 2% back on travel purchases. Either way, you're getting solid value.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• Global Entry / TSA PreCheck Credit: Up to $120 every 4 years. Every traveler should have this.
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees: Use freely when traveling internationally.
  • Travel Accident Insurance: Coverage for accidental death or dismemberment when the card is used to purchase travel.
  • Auto Rental CDW: Secondary collision damage waiver when renting a car and declining the rental company's coverage.
  • 24/7 Travel Assistance: Access to Capital One's travel assistance hotline for emergencies abroad.

Let's be honest — the Venture doesn't come with free lounge access, hotel status, or annual travel credits. Capital One Lounges and Landings will sell you a discounted pass ($45 per visit for adults, $25 for kids 2-17, under-2s free, and the same rates for your guests), and Priority Pass isn't included. It's a mid-tier card and it acts like one. If those perks matter to you, the Venture X is worth the step up to $395 for the lounges, the $300 credit, and the anniversary miles. The regular Venture is for people who want great earn rates and flexibility without the premium frills.

title: Capital One SavorOne
scouts_verdict: The SavorOne is the best category rewards card you can get with fair credit — but you need to earn that title. The $39 annual fee means you have to spend enough on dining, groceries, entertainment, and streaming to justify the cost. If you're clearing $109/month on groceries alone, the 3% cash back covers the fee and everything else is gravy. No foreign transaction fees, 8% back on Capital One Entertainment, and 5% on hotels and rental cars booked through Capital One Travel are perks you won't find on most fair-credit cards. But let's be real: if your credit is good enough for the no-fee Savor card, get that instead. Same rewards, no fee, plus a $200 welcome bonus. The SavorOne is the stepping stone, not the destination — and it's a genuinely good one.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
The Capital One SavorOne is Capital One's dining-and-groceries rewards card built specifically for people with fair credit. It charges a $39 annual fee — a change from its previous $0 incarnation — but delivers the same 3% cash back on dining, groceries, entertainment, and streaming that you'd get on the no-fee Savor card designed for excellent credit. Think of it as the on-ramp to Capital One's Savor ecosystem for anyone still building their credit profile.

Capital One revived the SavorOne name in 2025, repositioning it as the fair-credit sibling to the regular Savor card. Unlike the Savor, there's no welcome bonus and the APR is higher, but the earning structure is identical. If your credit score isn't quite in the "good" range yet and you spend meaningfully on food and entertainment, this card lets you earn real rewards while you work on getting there. Spend about $109 a month on groceries alone and the 3% cash back covers the annual fee.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• 3% Cash Back on Dining: All restaurants, takeout, delivery, and fast food. No cap. Your DoorDash habit is now a legitimate rewards strategy.
  • 3% Cash Back at Grocery Stores: Supermarkets and grocery stores (excluding superstores like Walmart and Target). Your weekly grocery run, paying you back.
  • 3% Cash Back on Entertainment: Movie theaters, concerts, sporting events, amusement parks, and similar venues. Fun now comes with a 3% rebate.
  • 3% Cash Back on Popular Streaming Services: Netflix, Spotify, Hulu, Disney+, and other qualifying subscriptions. Your couch time is earning money.
  • 5% Cash Back on Hotels and Rental Cars: When booked through Capital One Travel. Surprisingly strong for a fair-credit card.
  • 8% Cash Back on Capital One Entertainment Purchases: Tickets bought through the Capital One Entertainment platform. If you're buying concert tickets anyway, might as well get 8% back.
  • 1% Cash Back on All Other Purchases: Unlimited, no caps on any category. The 1% base rate is the one weak spot — a flat 1.5% card beats this on non-category spending.
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees: Rare for a fair-credit card and genuinely useful for international travel. Most cards in this credit tier charge 3%.
  • Automatic Credit Line Reviews: You're automatically considered for a higher credit line in as little as 6 months. Handy when you're building credit.
  • Credit-Building Tools: CreditWise credit monitoring and alerts to help you track your progress toward better credit.

The $39 annual fee is a real cost, and you need to be honest about whether your spending justifies it. At 3% back on groceries, you need to spend roughly $1,300 per year ($109/month) just to break even on the fee. If your grocery and dining spending clears that bar — and if you're building credit and can't qualify for the no-fee Savor card — the math works out fine. The 28.99% APR is steep, so carrying a balance on this card is an expensive mistake. Pay in full every month or the rewards math flips against you fast.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content: There is no welcome bonus on the Capital One SavorOne. That's the trade-off for a card that accepts fair credit. If you have excellent credit, look at the Capital One Savor instead — it offers a $200 cash bonus after spending $500 in the first 3 months, with no annual fee. Good-but-not-excellent credit? Capital One's Savor for Good Credit also skips the annual fee, though there's no bonus. The SavorOne is not the card for sign-up bonus chasers; it's the card for people who need a solid everyday earner while they build their credit score.

sections.title: Earning Rates
sections.content:
• 8% cash back on Capital One Entertainment purchases
  • 5% cash back on hotels, vacation rentals, rental cars and activities booked through Capital One Travel
  • 3% cash back on dining, groceries, entertainment, and popular streaming
  • 1% cash back on all other purchases

The earning structure is identical to the no-fee Savor card — 3% across four major everyday categories is genuinely excellent, especially for a fair-credit card. Most cards in this credit tier offer 1-2% at best. The 1% on everything else is the only weak link. Pair it with a flat-rate card like the Capital One Quicksilver for non-category spending and you've got a solid two-card setup.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
• Statement Credit: Redeem cash back as a credit to your account at any amount — no minimum redemption. Simple. Clean. Done.
  • Check: Request a check mailed to you. Old school but available.
  • Gift Cards: Redeem for gift cards from various retailers, though value is typically 1:1 with no bonus. No real advantage here.
  • Cover Your Purchases: Apply rewards against recent purchases. Functionally the same as a statement credit.

Unlike the Venture cards, SavorOne rewards don't transfer to airline or hotel partners. What you earn is what you get — a clean 3% return on your bonus categories, redeemed as cash. No optimization required, no spreadsheet needed. For people building credit, that simplicity is a feature, not a bug.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• No Foreign Transaction Fees: Extremely rare for a fair-credit card. Most cards in this tier hit you with 3% on every foreign purchase — this one doesn't.
  • Extended Warranty: Additional warranty protection at no charge on eligible items you buy with the card.
  • Travel Accident Insurance: Coverage when purchasing travel fares with the card.
  • Capital One Travel Portal Access: Book through the portal for elevated 5% earn on hotels and car rentals.
  • Capital One Cafe Perk: 50% off all handcrafted beverages at any Capital One Cafe nationwide.

Let's be clear: this is not a travel card. No lounge access, no Global Entry credit, no hotel status. But for a $39 fair-credit card, the perks punch way above their weight. No FTF, travel accident insurance, and extended warranty is a stronger benefits package than most no-fee cards offer — including some designed for excellent credit. The cafe discount is a nice cherry on top if you live near one.

title: Citi Custom Cash
scouts_verdict: The Custom Cash is a scalpel, not a sledgehammer. Use it for one spending category per month — groceries, dining, gas, whatever your biggest expense is — and let it auto-detect your top category for an effortless 5% return. On its own, it's a solid free card. Pair it with a Strata Premier and suddenly your grocery points transfer 1:1 into airline miles. That's a free card doing premium-card work. One catch: Citi stopped taking new applications on May 28, 2026 — if you have one, keep it; if you don't, Citi now points you to the Double Cash.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Heads up: Citi stopped accepting new applications for the Custom Cash on May 28, 2026. If you already have one, nothing changes — Citi says existing cardmembers keep the card and its benefits. If you don't, you can't open one anymore; Citi now steers new applicants to the Double Cash. Everything below is for current cardholders.

The Citi Custom Cash is a clever little card with one party trick, and it does that trick really well. It automatically earns 5% cash back on your highest eligible spending category each billing cycle — up to $500 in spending. No activation, no choosing, no quarterly opt-in nonsense. Citi figures out where you spent the most and gives you 5% on it. After $500, you're back to 1%.

Think of it as a surgical tool, not a Swiss Army knife. Eligible 5% categories include restaurants, gas stations, grocery stores, select travel, select transit, select streaming, drugstores, home improvement stores, fitness clubs, and live entertainment. That's a wide net. The play is simple: use this card for one specific spending category each month — groceries, dining, gas, whatever — and let it auto-detect your top category. Pair it with a flat-rate card for everything else and you've got a smart two-card setup.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• Automatic 5% Cash Back: Earns 5% in your top eligible spending category each billing cycle — no activation, no choosing, no hassle. It just... works. Refreshingly hands-off.
  • Wide Category List: Ten eligible 5% categories covering dining, gas, groceries, streaming, transit, travel, drugstores, home improvement, fitness, and entertainment. Odds are, your biggest monthly expense is on this list.
  • No Annual Fee: $0 per year. Free card, 5% back. Hard to complain.
  • Citi ThankYou Points Compatible: Rewards are earned as ThankYou Points. Here's the power move: if you hold a Citi Strata Premier or Strata Elite, your Custom Cash points transfer to airline and hotel partners at the full premium-card ratios — 1:1 to most airlines. (Solo, the card can transfer too, but at reduced ratios — 1:0.7 to most airlines.) That turns 5x grocery points into airline miles. Massive.
  • 24-Month Extended Warranty: Citi added this in late 2024 — it doubles the original manufacturer's or store warranty, up to a max of 24 months. Quiet, but handy for electronics. (The 0% intro APR was a new-account offer, so it ended when Citi stopped taking applications.)
  • Citi Entertainment Access: Presale tickets and preferred seating for concerts, sports, and events. A nice cherry on top.

One thing to watch: the 3% foreign transaction fee means this card stays home when you travel abroad. Use a no-FTF card internationally and keep the Custom Cash for domestic spending where it shines.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content: None — the card is closed to new applicants. Citi stopped taking Custom Cash applications on May 28, 2026, and the old welcome offer ($200 cash back, paid as 20,000 ThankYou Points, after $1,500 in spend in the first 6 months) went with it. If you want a Citi cash back card with a bonus today, Citi points you to the Double Cash.

sections.title: Earning Rates
sections.content:
• 5% cash back (5x ThankYou Points) on your top eligible spending category each billing cycle, on up to $500 in purchases
  • 5% cash back total (5x ThankYou Points) on hotels, car rentals, and attractions booked through Citi Travel — an extra 4% on top of the base 1%
  • 1% cash back (1x ThankYou Points) on all other purchases

Eligible 5% categories: restaurants, gas stations, grocery stores, select travel, select transit, select streaming services, drugstores, home improvement stores, fitness clubs, and live entertainment.

The $500 per-cycle cap means the top-category 5% maxes out at $25 per month — $300 per year in bonus value. Not going to change your life, but for a free card that requires zero effort, that's solid. For spending beyond $500 in your top category, you'll want a complementary card picking up the slack. The automatic category detection is based on merchant category codes (MCCs), so there's no gaming it — Citi picks your top category based on actual spending.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
• Statement Credit: Redeem ThankYou Points at 1 cent each against your balance. Simple and clean.
  • Direct Deposit: Cash out points directly to your bank account. Same 1 cent per point, different destination.
  • Gift Cards: Redeem for retail gift cards at 1 cent per point. No bonus, no reason to choose this over cash.
  • Transfer to Partners: If you also hold a Citi Strata Premier or Strata Elite, your Custom Cash ThankYou Points pool together and transfer to airline/hotel partners at the full premium-card ratios (1:1 to most airlines). On its own, the Custom Cash can transfer too, but at reduced ratios (1:0.7 to most airlines). This is the real unlock — your 5x grocery points become airline miles worth 1.5-2+ cents each.
  • Shop with Points: Use points at checkout with select retailers (usually poor value). Skip this one.

The real power play is pairing the Custom Cash with a Strata Premier or Strata Elite. On its own, you're getting a solid 5% cash back card. Combined with a Strata card, your 5x points become full-value (1:1) transferable currency — turning your grocery spending into first-class flights. That's a no-fee card punching way above its weight class.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• Citi Entertainment: Access to presale tickets and special experiences for concerts, dining, and sporting events. Not a travel perk per se, but a nice lifestyle bonus.
  • Extended Warranty: Doubles the original manufacturer's or store warranty, up to a max of 24 months. Quietly useful for electronics and appliances.
  • Citi Merchant Offers: Targeted statement-credit deals on shopping, dining, and travel — enroll in the offer, make the qualifying purchase, get the credit.

Let's be clear: this is not a travel card. No lounges, no Global Entry, no trip insurance, and no car rental coverage either. The Custom Cash's value is purely in its earning rates and its synergy with the Citi ThankYou ecosystem. And that's fine — not every card needs to be a travel card.

title: Citi Strata Premier
scouts_verdict: The Strata Premier is the quiet overachiever of mid-tier travel cards. Four categories at 3x for $95? The Sapphire Preferred now matches dining and gas, but neither it nor the Venture pays 3x in-store at supermarkets or on direct flights and hotels. The $100 hotel credit covers the annual fee with one $500+ Citi Travel stay, The Reserve hotel perks add genuine luxury value, and the transfer partner list — headlined by Singapore KrisFlyer and Turkish Miles & Smiles — opens up premium cabin redemptions that cards twice the price can't beat. The downsides are real: car rental coverage that's only secondary at home (it's primary abroad), no lounge access, no Global Entry credit, and Citi's travel portal still lags behind Chase and Amex. But pair it with a no-fee Double Cash for 2x on everything else (plus a Custom Cash if you already have one, since Citi stopped taking new applications in May 2026), and you've got a Citi setup that costs $95 a year total and punches way above its weight class.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
The Citi Strata Premier is one of the most underrated mid-tier travel cards on the market — and honestly, it deserves way more attention than it gets. For $95 a year, you get 3x ThankYou Points across four major spending categories: air travel, dining, groceries, and gas. That's not a typo. Four categories at 3x. The Chase Sapphire Preferred now matches it on dining and gas, but pays 3x only on online grocery and 2x on travel you book directly. The Capital One Venture gives you 2x on everything outside its travel portal. The Strata Premier simply covers more of your everyday spending at 3x.

But the real power move is what this card unlocks: Citi's ThankYou transfer partner network. We're talking Singapore Airlines KrisFlyer, Turkish Miles & Smiles, Air France/KLM Flying Blue, Cathay Pacific Asia Miles, Virgin Atlantic, JetBlue, and over a dozen more — mostly at 1:1 ratios. And here's the kicker: holding the Strata Premier doesn't just unlock full-ratio transfers for points earned on this card. It unlocks them for your Custom Cash and Double Cash points too — on their own, those cards transfer at a reduced 1:0.7 to most airlines. That's the Citi ecosystem play, and it's genuinely compelling.

The trade-off? No lounge access, no Global Entry/TSA PreCheck credit (that's the Strata Elite), and the Citi Travel portal isn't as polished as Chase's. But for a $95 card that earns 3x on the stuff you actually buy every week? It punches hard.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• 10x on Citi Travel Portal: Hotels, car rentals, and attractions booked through cititravel.com earn a massive 10x points — one of the highest portal earning rates you'll find anywhere.
  • 3x on Air Travel & Hotels: Airline purchases, travel agencies, and hotels booked outside Citi Travel earn 3x.
  • 3x on Dining: Restaurants, bars, cafes, food delivery — it all counts at 3x.
  • 3x on Supermarkets: Grocery store runs earn 3x. Your weekly Trader Joe's haul is putting in work.
  • 3x on Gas & EV Charging: Gas stations and EV charging stations both earn 3x. Your commute earns rewards.
  • 1x on Everything Else: The base rate is nothing special — but that's what the Double Cash is for in a two-card setup.
  • Transfer Partners: Transfers to 20 airline and hotel programs, mostly at 1:1, including American AAdvantage, Singapore KrisFlyer, Turkish Miles & Smiles, Flying Blue, Virgin Atlantic, JetBlue, and more.
  • $100 Annual Hotel Savings: $100 off a single hotel stay of $500+ (pre-tax) booked through Citi Travel, once per calendar year. Applied instantly at booking.
  • The Reserve Access: Book curated luxury hotels through The Reserve by Citi Travel and get daily breakfast for two, a $100 experience credit, room upgrades, and early check-in/late checkout when available.
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees: Take it overseas without getting hit by the 3% surcharge tax.
  • Citi Entertainment: Presale tickets and preferred access to concerts, sports, dining events, and more.
  • Points Pooling: Combine ThankYou Points from your Custom Cash, Double Cash, and other Citi cards into one transferable stash.
  • $0 Liability: Zero liability on unauthorized purchases for peace of mind.

$95 is the going rate for a mid-tier travel card in 2026 — the CSP, Venture, and Strata Premier all land at the same price point. The $100 annual hotel savings benefit can wipe out the entire fee with a single qualifying booking through Citi Travel. Throw in The Reserve hotel perks when you stay at luxury properties, and this card can more than pay for itself before you even redeem a single point.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
Earn 60,000 bonus ThankYou Points after spending $4,000 in the first 3 months of account opening. Redeemed through Citi Travel at 1 cent per point, that's $600 (straight cash back now pays just 0.75 cents a point, or $450, unless a Double Cash or Custom Cash is linked to the same ThankYou account). Transfer to the right airline partner — say, Turkish Miles & Smiles for a Star Alliance business class sweet spot — and you could extract $800+ in value. The $4,000 spend requirement is very doable for most households.

Eligibility note: The bonus isn't available if you currently have or previously had a Citi Strata Premier or Citi Premier account. Citi swapped its old 48-month rule for this once-per-lifetime language in September 2026, so if you've ever held either card, this bonus is off the table.

sections.title: Earning Rates
sections.content:
• 10x points — Hotels, car rentals, and attractions booked through cititravel.com
  • 3x points — Airlines, travel agencies, and hotels booked outside Citi Travel
  • 3x points — Restaurants and dining
  • 3x points — Supermarkets and grocery stores
  • 3x points — Gas stations and EV charging stations
  • 1x points — All other purchases

The headline here is breadth. Even the refreshed Sapphire Preferred still pays just 1x on in-store groceries and 2x on flights and hotels booked direct, and the Venture pays 2x outside its travel portal. The Strata Premier pays 3x on all of those, plus dining and gas. If your household spends on groceries, eats out, fills up the car, and travels a few times a year, you're earning 3x on a massive chunk of your budget without even trying. The 10x on portal bookings is gravy — though the Citi Travel portal experience is a work in progress compared to Chase or Amex, so YMMV on whether you want to use it for hotel bookings.

No cap on points earned, and points never expire as long as the account is open. That's a quiet but meaningful perk.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
• Transfer to Partners (best value): Transfers to 20 airline and hotel programs. At 1:1: American AAdvantage, Singapore KrisFlyer, Turkish Miles & Smiles, Air France/KLM Flying Blue, Cathay Pacific Asia Miles, JetBlue TrueBlue, Virgin Atlantic Flying Club, Avianca LifeMiles, Etihad Guest, Japan Airlines Mileage Bank, EVA Air, Qantas, Qatar Airways, Thai Airways, and Wyndham Rewards. At other ratios: Emirates Skywards (1:0.8), Choice Privileges (1:1.5), Accor Live Limitless (1:0.5), Preferred Hotels I Prefer (1:2), and Leading Hotels of the World Leaders Club (1:0.2). Minimum transfer: 1,000 points in increments of 1,000.
  • Citi Travel Portal: Book flights, hotels, car rentals, and attractions at 1 cent per point. Functional but not flashy.
  • Cash Back: Statement credit, check, or direct deposit at just 0.75 cents per point since August 2025 — 1 cent if a Double Cash or Custom Cash is linked to the same ThankYou account.
  • Shop with Points: Amazon, CVS, and other online retailers. Terrible value — avoid this.
  • Gift Cards: Various retailers through thankyou.com. Rarely better than 1 cpp.

The whole point of this card is transfer partners. Singapore KrisFlyer is the crown jewel — one of the best ways to book Star Alliance business and first class at a fraction of the cash price. Turkish Miles & Smiles is another standout for United-operated flights at fixed award rates. Wyndham transfers at 1:1 can be surprisingly useful for domestic hotel stays. Note that Emirates transfers at a 1:0.8 ratio (1,000 points = 800 Skywards miles), which is less favorable but still usable for Emirates redemptions.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• $100 Annual Hotel Savings: $100 off a single hotel booking of $500+ (excluding taxes and fees) through cititravel.com or by calling 1-833-737-1288, once per calendar year. You must pre-pay the full stay with your Strata Premier card, ThankYou points, or a combination. The discount applies instantly at booking.
  • The Reserve by Citi Travel: Access to a curated collection of luxury 4.5- and 5-star hotels with perks: daily breakfast for two, $100 experience credit for on-property spending (spa, dining, etc.), room upgrades when available, and early check-in/late checkout when available.
  • Trip Cancellation & Interruption: Up to $5,000 per trip and $10,000 per 12-month period for non-refundable common carrier travel expenses when your trip is canceled or cut short for a covered reason. Must be paid with the card.
  • Trip Delay Protection: Up to $500 per trip for meals, lodging, and essential expenses when your travel is delayed by 6+ hours. Maximum of two claims per 12-month period.
  • Lost or Damaged Luggage: Up to $3,000 per trip if your luggage is lost, stolen, or damaged during transit by the carrier. Limited to actual purchase price or replacement cost. Two claims per 12-month period.
  • MasterRental Car Insurance: Coverage when you rent a car and pay with the Strata Premier: secondary in your home country, primary when you rent abroad. Covers the cash value of the vehicle, reasonable towing costs, and up to $500 in loss-of-use charges. You must decline the rental company's collision damage waiver to qualify. At home, secondary means your personal auto policy pays first.
  • Purchase Protection: Covers damage or theft of eligible purchases for up to 90 days after purchase. Up to $10,000 per incident, $50,000 per year.
  • Extended Warranty: Adds 24 months to the manufacturer's warranty, up to 7 years of total coverage from the purchase date. Maximum coverage of $10,000 per item.
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees: Use it internationally without the typical 3% surcharge.
  • Citi Entertainment: Presale tickets and exclusive access to concerts, sports events, dining experiences, and more.

Notable absences for a $95 card: no Global Entry or TSA PreCheck credit (reserved for the $595 Strata Elite), no airport lounge access, and no streaming or dining statement credits. If you want dining credits, look at the Amex Gold (at a much higher $325 annual fee). But the travel insurance suite here is genuinely solid — trip cancellation, trip delay, lost or damaged luggage coverage, purchase protection, and extended warranty all in one $95 package. Most people undervalue this stuff until they need it.

At the same $95 price point, the Strata Premier still wins on everyday breadth — 3x at the supermarket and on flights and hotels booked direct, where the refreshed CSP pays 3x only on online grocery and 2x on direct travel, and the Venture pays 2x outside its travel portal. The hotel credit is now a wash, since the CSP matched it at $100. Where the CSP fights back: 3x on gas and dining too, a Global Entry/TSA PreCheck credit, a bigger 75,000-point bonus, a more polished travel portal, the mature Chase ecosystem (Freedom Unlimited + Flex feeding into Sapphire), and arguably stronger transfer partners for domestic travel like United and Southwest — though new CSP cardholders now get a weaker 4:3 ratio to Hyatt (existing ones follow on October 1, 2026). The Venture wins on simplicity — 2x everything, no categories to think about, plus Capital One's improving partner list. The Amex Gold is a different beast entirely at $325: higher earning on dining and groceries, plus up to $424 in annual credits (dining, Uber, Resy, Dunkin') that can cover the whole fee if you use them all, but it costs more than 3x the Strata Premier and doesn't earn bonus rates on gas or on travel outside flights and Amex Travel bookings.

sections.title: Best For
sections.content:
• Families who spend broadly across groceries, gas, dining, flights, and hotels — and want 3x on all of it without juggling multiple cards or tracking rotating categories.
  • Award travel enthusiasts who want access to Singapore KrisFlyer, Turkish Miles & Smiles, and Flying Blue in their transfer partner toolkit.
  • Citi ecosystem builders pairing with a Double Cash (2x on everything) and/or a Custom Cash they already hold (5x on up to $500 in its top eligible spending category each billing cycle; closed to new applicants since May 2026) to funnel all points into one transferable pool.
  • Budget-conscious travelers who want the most everyday earning power for $95 — the Strata Premier is one of the few $95 cards that pays 3x at the supermarket, the pump, restaurants, and on airfare and hotels booked outside Citi Travel.
  • International travelers who need no foreign transaction fees and a respectable travel insurance package without paying $300+ annually.

title: Citi Strata Elite
scouts_verdict: The Strata Elite is Citi's most serious premium card ever — and it legitimately competes. The earning rates through Citi Travel are best-in-class (12x on hotels is wild), the $700+ in annual credits can more than offset the $595 fee, and AA transfer access at 1:1 is a genuine differentiator no other transferable currency offers. The Admirals Club passes and Priority Pass together give you solid lounge coverage. Where it stumbles: the insurance package trails the CSR (secondary domestic car rental, no baggage delay coverage), the best earning rates require portal booking, and the 6-hour trip delay trigger is just average. If you're a Citi ecosystem person or an AA loyalist who also wants transferable points flexibility, this is your card. If you want set-it-and-forget-it simplicity, the Venture X still wins on pure value.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
The Citi Strata Elite is Citi finally throwing a haymaker at the premium travel card heavyweights. Launched in July 2025 as the world's first Mastercard World Legend card, it carries a $595 annual fee and comes loaded with up to 12x earning on portal hotel bookings, a stack of annual credits worth up to $700+, Admirals Club passes, Priority Pass Select, and a solid insurance package.

This is Citi's direct shot at the Chase Sapphire Reserve and Capital One Venture X — and honestly, it's a compelling one. The earning rates through Citi Travel are aggressive, the Splurge and Blacklane credits add genuine flexibility, and access to 20 airline and hotel transfer partners (including American Airlines at 1:1) gives you real firepower for premium redemptions. The card isn't perfect — the insurance benefits lag behind the CSR in a couple of areas, and some credits require booking through Citi's portal — but if you're in the Citi ecosystem or want AA access without the AAdvantage Executive card's limitations, this deserves serious consideration.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• Up to 12x points per $1 on hotels, car rentals, and attractions booked through cititravel.com
  • 6x points per $1 on flights booked through cititravel.com
  • 6x points per $1 at restaurants on Citi Nights purchases (Friday & Saturday, 6 PM – 6 AM ET)
  • 3x points per $1 at restaurants and restaurant delivery services (all other times)
  • 1.5x points per $1 on everything else — no dead categories
  • $300 annual hotel credit on stays of 2+ nights through Citi Travel
  • $200 annual Splurge Credit — choose up to 2 brands from 1stDibs, American Airlines, Best Buy, Future Personal Training, or Live Nation
  • $200 annual Blacklane credit — $100 Jan–Jun, $100 Jul–Dec for chauffeur rides
  • 4 Admirals Club passes per year for access to ~50 AA lounges
  • Priority Pass Select for primary cardholder, authorized users, and up to 2 guests each
  • The Reserve by Citi Travel — $100 experience credit, daily breakfast for two, early check-in/late checkout, room upgrades, free Wi-Fi at luxury properties
  • $120 Global Entry/TSA PreCheck credit every 4 years
  • No foreign transaction fees
  • 20 airline and hotel transfer partners including American Airlines (1:1), JetBlue, Virgin Atlantic, Cathay Pacific, Singapore Airlines, Emirates, and more
  • Citi Entertainment — presale tickets and exclusive access to concerts, sports, dining, and arts events
  • Mastercard World Legend perks — Priceless experiences, priority restaurant reservations, entertainment ticketing access

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:
• Annual fee: $595
  • Authorized user fee: $75 per user (each AU gets their own Priority Pass Select membership with up to 2 guests)
  • Foreign transaction fees: None
  • Citigold banking credit: $145 annual statement credit toward the fee (Citigold clients)
  • Citigold Private Client credit: $595 credit in year one, then $145 annually thereafter

The math on justifying $595: you get up to $300 (hotel) + $200 (Splurge) + $200 (Blacklane) + $30/yr amortized Global Entry = roughly $730 in annual credits before you earn a single point. That's a net positive on paper — the real question is whether you'll actually use the Blacklane and Splurge credits. The Splurge Credit is flexible enough (American Airlines, Best Buy) that most people can find value, and Blacklane works for airport transfers in major cities. Citigold clients get an even sweeter deal with the fee offset.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
Standard offer: Earn 75,000 ThankYou points after spending $6,000 in the first 3 months. That's $750 if you redeem through the Citi Travel portal at 1 cent per point, or roughly $1,275–$1,425 if you transfer to airline partners.

A limited-time 100,000-point offer has appeared through certain channels — keep an eye out, as it pops up periodically and represents significantly better value.

Eligibility note: As of September 2026 the bonus is once per lifetime. Citi's terms say it's not available if you currently have or previously had a Citi Strata Elite account, and you may also be ineligible for the bonus based on your history of opening, closing and using cards. That replaced the old 48-month rule, so if you've never had the card, make your one shot count.

The $6,000 spend requirement in 3 months is moderate — higher than the Venture X ($4,000) but lower than some Amex Platinum targeted offers. Very doable for most people who are considering a $595 annual fee card.

sections.title: Earning Rates
sections.content:
CategoryPoints per $1Details
Hotels, Car Rentals & Attractions12xMust book through cititravel.com
Flights6xMust book through cititravel.com
Restaurants (Citi Nights)6xFriday & Saturday, 6 PM – 6 AM ET only
Restaurants & Delivery3xAll other times, includes delivery services
Everything Else1.5xNo category exclusions

The earning structure here is genuinely strong. That 12x on portal hotels is the highest hotel multiplier among the big transferable-points cards — for context, the CSR gives 8x on Chase Travel bookings, the Venture X gives 10x on Capital One Travel hotels, and the Amex Platinum gives 5x on flights and prepaid Amex Travel hotels. The 6x on portal flights is competitive too.

The Citi Nights 6x is a fun twist — essentially double restaurant earnings on Friday and Saturday evenings. If your social life runs on weekend dinners, this adds up fast. And the 1.5x floor on everything else means there are zero dead-spend categories, which is something the Amex Platinum (1x on non-bonus) can't say.

The catch: those top-tier rates require booking through Citi Travel. If you prefer booking directly with hotels for elite status benefits or airline flexibility, you're looking at 1.5x instead of 12x or 6x. That's the trade-off.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
ThankYou points transfer to 20 travel partners — 15 airlines and 5 hotel programs. The headline partners:

  • Airlines (1:1 unless noted): American Airlines, JetBlue, Virgin Atlantic, Cathay Pacific, Emirates Skywards (1:0.8), Etihad Guest, EVA Air, Japan Airlines, Singapore Airlines, Turkish Airlines, Qatar Airways, Avianca LifeMiles, Thai Airways, Qantas, Flying Blue (Air France/KLM)
  • Hotels: Accor Live Limitless, Choice Privileges, Wyndham Rewards, The Leading Hotels of the World, Preferred Hotels & Resorts (I Prefer)

The American Airlines 1:1 transfer is the marquee here — Citi is the only major transferable currency with direct AA access, which is huge for domestic travelers. Singapore Airlines, Virgin Atlantic, and Turkish are also excellent for premium cabin redemptions to Europe and Asia.

You can also redeem through the Citi Travel portal, as statement credits, for gift cards, or to pay with points at checkout — though transfers to partners almost always yield the best value. Portal redemptions are decent but won't give you the outsized value of a well-planned partner transfer.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
Annual Credits

  • $300 Hotel Credit: Up to $300 off a prepaid hotel stay of 2 nights or more booked through cititravel.com. Calendar year benefit. The minimum 2-night requirement is slightly annoying but reasonable for a hotel credit.
  • $200 Splurge Credit: Pick up to 2 brands from 1stDibs, American Airlines, Best Buy, Future Personal Training, and Live Nation. Calendar year. The AA option makes this easy to use — flights and other purchases billed by American Airlines count (book on aa.com, not through Citi Travel), though AA car rentals, hotel bookings, status boosts and AA Cargo are excluded. Best Buy is also practical for everyday purchases.
  • $200 Blacklane Credit: $100 from January through June, $100 from July through December. Blacklane offers professional chauffeur services — airport transfers, city-to-city rides, hourly hires. Useful in major cities, though if you're not a Blacklane user, this credit takes effort to maximize.
  • $120 Global Entry/TSA PreCheck Credit: Statement credit every 4 years for your application fee.

Lounge Access

  • 4 Admirals Club passes per calendar year: Each pass admits one adult (18+) and up to 3 children under 18. Requires a same-day boarding pass for an American Airlines or oneworld partner flight. These are calendar year passes, so you get a fresh set every January. Access to ~50 Admirals Club locations.
  • Priority Pass Select: Unlimited visits for the primary cardholder and authorized users, each with up to 2 guests. Access to 1,500+ lounges worldwide (valued at $469/year for membership alone). This is the same tier offered by the CSR and Venture X, though the Venture X stopped including free guests in February 2026.

The Reserve by Citi Travel

Book luxury hotels through The Reserve collection and get:

  • $100 experience credit per stay (spa, dining, etc.)
  • Daily breakfast for two guests
  • Complimentary Wi-Fi
  • Early check-in and late checkout (subject to availability)
  • Room upgrades (subject to availability)

These mirror what you'd get with Amex Fine Hotels + Resorts or Chase's The Edit — a solid perk if you're booking high-end properties anyway.

Travel Protections

  • Trip Delay Protection: Up to $500 per trip when your flight is delayed 6+ hours. Covers meals, lodging, and essential expenses. Round-trip travel only (one-way tickets can make up the round trip); pay the full fare with the card, or with the card plus ThankYou points. Maximum 2 claims per 12-month period. This is secondary coverage (pays after airline reimbursement). The 6-hour trigger is standard but not best-in-class — the CSR triggers at 6 hours too, but some cards do better.
  • Trip Cancellation/Interruption: Up to $5,000 per trip, $10,000 per account per 12 months. Round-trip travel only (one-way tickets can make up the round trip); pay the full fare with the card, or with the card plus ThankYou points.
  • Lost or Damaged Luggage: Up to $5,000 per trip ($2,000 for NY residents). Note: this covers lost or damaged baggage — the card does not include separate baggage delay insurance for purchasing essentials while waiting. The CSR does offer baggage delay coverage, so this is a gap.
  • MasterRental Coverage (Car Rental Insurance): Secondary coverage for domestic rentals, primary coverage for international rentals (outside your country of residence). Covers the cash value of the vehicle plus up to $500 in loss-of-use charges. Decline the rental company's CDW/LDW to activate. The international primary coverage is a nice touch, but the domestic secondary coverage means your personal auto insurance kicks in first for U.S. rentals — the CSR offers primary coverage everywhere.
  • Purchase Assurance Plus: Up to $10,000 per item, $50,000 annual cap. Covers theft or damage to eligible purchases within 120 days of purchase (90 days for NY residents).
  • Extended Warranty: Extends the manufacturer's warranty by up to 24 months on eligible items with an original warranty of 24 months or less. Up to $10,000 per item.

Other Perks

  • Citi Entertainment: Access to presale tickets and exclusive experiences for concerts, sporting events, dining, and arts
  • Mastercard World Legend: Priority restaurant reservations at thousands of restaurants, Priceless experiences worldwide, and entertainment/event ticketing access
  • No foreign transaction fees

vs. Chase Sapphire Reserve: The CSR costs $200 more at $795/year, has primary car rental insurance everywhere (the Strata Elite is only primary internationally), and includes baggage delay coverage the Strata Elite lacks. But the Strata Elite fights back with higher portal earning rates (12x vs. 8x on Chase Travel hotels), a lower annual fee ($595 vs. $795), Admirals Club passes, AA transfer access, and a 1.5x base rate vs. 1x. If you value credits and earning, the Strata Elite wins. If you want the cleanest insurance package, the CSR still edges ahead.

vs. Amex Platinum: The Platinum costs $300 more and its credits are spread across many specific merchants (lululemon, Resy, Uber, etc.) that can feel forced. The Strata Elite's credits are more practical for most people. The Platinum wins on lounge access (Centurion Lounges are genuinely excellent) and 5x on flights booked directly with airlines, no portal required (its 5x on hotels needs prepaid Amex Travel bookings). But the Strata Elite's 1.5x base rate crushes the Platinum's 1x on non-bonus spend.

vs. Capital One Venture X: The Venture X is the value king at $395 with a $300 travel credit making it effectively $95/year. It has Priority Pass too, but since February 2026 Venture X Priority Pass guests cost $35 each and authorized users need a $125 add-on, while the Strata Elite still includes two free guests for you and each AU. It also offers Capital One's own excellent lounges. The 2x base rate on everything is technically higher than 1.5x. But the Strata Elite demolishes it on portal multipliers (12x vs. 10x hotels), annual credits ($700+ vs. $300), and the Admirals Club passes are unique. The Venture X is the budget-friendly choice; the Strata Elite is for maximizers willing to work the credits.

sections.title: Best For
sections.content:
• American Airlines flyers who want AA lounge access plus 1:1 point transfers without being locked into an AAdvantage co-brand card
  • Portal bookers who are comfortable booking hotels and flights through Citi Travel to unlock those 12x and 6x rates
  • Weekend diners who eat out on Friday and Saturday nights and want to capitalize on the 6x Citi Nights bonus
  • Credit maximizers who will actually use the Splurge, Blacklane, and hotel credits — if you'd use all three, the card essentially pays for itself
  • Citigold/Private Client members who get annual fee credits, making the effective cost even lower
  • International travelers who benefit from no FTF, primary international car rental coverage, and a deep bench of global airline transfer partners

Skip this card if: You always book directly with hotels for elite status benefits (the portal requirement kills the best earning rates). You want primary domestic car rental insurance (get the CSR or Venture X instead). You don't travel enough to use the Admirals Club passes and Blacklane credits. Or you just want a simple, low-fee premium card (the Venture X at $395 is hard to beat on pure value).

title: Citi Double Cash
scouts_verdict: The Citi Double Cash has been the default "just give me a good card" recommendation for years, and the ThankYou Points upgrade made it even better. Pair it with a Strata Premier and your 2% card quietly becomes a 2x fully transferable points card that costs you nothing to hold. If you're building a Citi setup, this is the foundation. If you just want simplicity, it's still one of the best no-fee cards around.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
The Citi Double Cash Card has been the answer to "what's a good simple card?" for the better part of a decade — and for good reason. It earns an effective 2% cash back on everything (1% when you buy, 1% when you pay), charges no annual fee, and doesn't ask you to think about categories, caps, or quarterly activations. It just works.

But here's the real plot twist: Citi moved the Double Cash into the ThankYou Points ecosystem, so it now earns 2x ThankYou Points per dollar instead of straight cash back. On its own, that's the same 2% value. But pair it with a Citi Strata Premier or Strata Elite and those points become fully transferable to airline and hotel partners — suddenly your boring grocery runs are funding business class flights. That's the kind of upgrade that turns a good card into a great one.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• 2% on Everything: 1% when you swipe, 1% when you pay. No rotating categories, no caps, no enrollment, no thinking.
  • ThankYou Points: Rewards come as 2x ThankYou Points, which transfer to 20 partners at full ratios when you hold a Strata Premier or Elite (reduced ratios on their own).
  • $0 Annual Fee: Free forever. This card deserves a permanent spot in your wallet.
  • 0% Intro APR on Balance Transfers: 0% for 18 months — one of the longest intro periods you'll find.
  • Citi Entertainment: Presale access to concerts, sports, and events. Not the main draw, but a nice bonus.

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:

The 3% foreign transaction fee is the one real blemish. Leave this card at home when you travel internationally — grab your Strata Premier or any no-FTF card instead.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content: The Double Cash offers $200 cash back (20,000 ThankYou Points) after spending $1,500 within the first 6 months. Not a jaw-dropper, but the spending requirement is so low and the timeframe so generous that you'd almost have to try to miss it. It's free money with training wheels. One catch: no bonus if you've earned a Double Cash bonus (or converted into a Double Cash after earning a bonus) in the past 48 months.

sections.title: Earning Rates
sections.content:
• 2x ThankYou Points (2% cash back) on every purchase — 1x when you buy, 1x when you pay your bill
  • 5x ThankYou Points (5% cash back) on hotels, car rentals and attractions booked through Citi Travel — the base 2x plus 3 bonus points

That's the whole menu. Outside that Citi Travel bump, it's one rate everywhere. No spending tiers, no quarterly activation dance. The simplicity is the feature. One caveat: you need to pay at least the minimum on time to keep earning — fall behind and you stop earning points on that cycle's purchases (not just the payback 1%) until you're current again. So, you know, pay your bill.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
• Statement Credit: Redeem ThankYou Points at 1 cent each. Straightforward 2% cash back.
  • Direct Deposit: Cash out to a linked bank account.
  • Transfer to Partners (with a qualifying card): If you hold a Strata Premier or Strata Elite, your Double Cash points pool together and transfer to 20 airline and hotel partners (1:1 for most) — potentially worth 1.5–3+ cents per point.
  • Gift Cards: Various retailers, typically at 1 cent per point. Fine.
  • Check: A physical check ($5 minimum). What year is it?

The real unlock here is full-ratio transfer partner access through a companion Strata Premier or Elite. Without one, the Double Cash can still transfer, but at reduced ratios (1:0.7 to most partners) — so on its own it's mostly a solid 2% card. With one, it becomes a 2x-everywhere points card with full-ratio transfers — think Capital One Venture vibes, but with no annual fee on the Double Cash itself. That's a genuinely powerful proposition.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• Citi Entertainment: Presale access and preferred seating for concerts, sports, and events.
  • 0% Intro APR on Balance Transfers: 18 months at 0%. Great for consolidating higher-interest debt.
  • Extended Warranty: Secondary coverage that stretches the manufacturer's warranty on eligible purchases.

Let's be honest — this isn't a travel card and it doesn't pretend to be one. No lounge access, no Global Entry credit, no trip insurance, not even rental car coverage. The Double Cash is a pure earning engine. Pair it with a travel-focused card and let each do what it does best.

title: Bank of America Premium Rewards
scouts_verdict: Don't sleep on this one. The BofA Premium Rewards looks like a generic mid-tier card until you add BofA Rewards into the equation. At the $100K Preferred Honors tier, you're earning 2.25x on everything (2.625x if you've got $1M+ for Premier) — a flat rate that embarrasses most premium cards at any price. Without it? Look elsewhere. This card rewards your BofA relationship and nothing else.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
The Bank of America Premium Rewards card is kind of a sleeper. On paper, it's a $95 travel card with a decent 2x/1.5x earning structure, some travel credits, and no foreign transaction fees. Fine. Not exciting. But here's where it gets interesting: if you bank with Bank of America or Merrill and have some assets parked there, the BofA Rewards program (which replaced Preferred Rewards in May 2026) can supercharge this card into something genuinely elite.

At the Preferred Honors tier ($100K+ in combined balances), your earning rates jump by 50% — turning that 1.5x base into 2.25x on everything and that 2x on travel and dining into 3x. Park $1M+ and the Premier tier's 75% boost takes you to 2.625x and 3.5x. Suddenly this modest $95 card is out-earning premium cards that cost five times as much. The catch? You need the BofA relationship to make it sing.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• 2x on travel and dining, 1.5x on everything else: Clean, simple earning structure with no caps or categories to track.
  • $100 Airline Incidental Credit: Calendar-year statement credit for baggage fees, seat upgrades, in-flight purchases, and airline lounge fees on most U.S. airlines — no need to pick one.
  • TSA PreCheck / Global Entry Credit: Up to $100 reimbursement every four years. Skip the line on BofA's dime.
  • BofA Rewards Boost: 10% to 75% more points depending on your tier — 50% at Preferred Honors ($100K+ in combined balances), 75% at Premier ($1M+). This is the card's entire personality.
  • No foreign transaction fees: Use it abroad without getting dinged.
  • Visa Signature benefits: Auto rental CDW, extended warranty, purchase protection, travel and emergency assistance.

Use the $100 airline credit and you're already net positive on the $95 fee. Throw in the amortized Global Entry credit and you're making money before you earn a single point. For a mid-tier card, the fee math works out really well.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
Earn 60,000 bonus points after spending $4,000 in purchases within the first 90 days. Heads up: you may not be eligible if you have (or had) this card in the past 24 months.

At the fixed 1 cent per point value, that's $600 in travel through the BofA portal. For a $95 card, that's a very strong first-year proposition. No transfer partner acrobatics needed — just book and go.

BofA Rewards tiers (based on combined BofA deposit and Merrill investment balances): Member (10% boost, no minimum — you just need an eligible BofA checking account), Preferred Plus (25% boost, $30K+), Preferred Honors (50% boost, $100K+), Premier (75% boost, $1M+). Heads up: BofA Rewards replaced Preferred Rewards on May 26, 2026, and the 75% boost that used to kick in at $100K now takes $1M. If you enrolled in Preferred Rewards before May 26, 2026, your existing card may keep its old bonus (75% for former Platinum Honors members) for a while, but new cards earn at the new tier's rate. Points are worth a flat 1 cent each when redeemed for travel or cash back. No guessing games, no devaluation anxiety — just clean, simple math.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
• Travel portal: Book flights, hotels, and car rentals at 1 cent per point through the BofA travel center.
  • Statement credit: Redeem at 1 cent per point. Cash is cash.
  • Cash back: Deposit into a BofA checking or savings account.
  • Gift cards: Also 1 cent per point, the same as cash, so there's no penalty (or advantage) to choosing them.

Here's the tradeoff you make with BofA: there are no transfer partners. Zero. You can't move points to Hyatt or United or anyone else. That means no 3-cent-per-point redemptions on aspirational first class flights. But it also means no agonizing over sweet spots or watching your points get devalued overnight. You always know exactly what your points are worth. For a lot of people, that simplicity is the point.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• $100 Airline Incidental Credit: Automatically applied each calendar year for incidentals (baggage fees, seat upgrades, change fees, in-flight purchases, airline lounge fees) on most U.S. airlines — no need to pick one (Allegiant, Spirit and Sun Country don't count).
  • $100 TSA PreCheck / Global Entry Credit: Statement credit every 4 years when you charge the application fee to your card.
  • No foreign transaction fees: Clean for international use.
  • Visa Signature perks: Auto rental CDW, baggage delay and lost luggage reimbursement, trip delay and cancellation/interruption insurance, roadside dispatch.

Suddenly you're earning 2.25x on everything (2.625x at Premier, $1M+) — no other $95 travel card can touch that. The BofA Premium Rewards is the ultimate "loyalty pays" card.

sections.title: Best For

  • People who want one card that just works everywhere without chasing bonus categories or managing transfer partners
  • Travelers on a budget who want a low-fee card with airline credits and Global Entry reimbursement

Let's be direct: if you don't have meaningful BofA/Merrill balances, the Chase Sapphire Preferred or Capital One Venture will serve you better. This card's superpower is rewarding banking loyalty — and few banks do that as aggressively. (One rival worth knowing: U.S. Bank's no-fee Smartly card pays up to 4% cash back if you keep $100K+ in U.S. Bank Smartly Checking or Safe Debit accounts and also have a Smartly Savings account, though only on the first $10K of purchases each billing cycle.)

title: Bank of America Premium Rewards Elite
scouts_verdict: The Premium Rewards Elite is BofA's premium play, and for BofA Rewards Premier members ($1M+), it's quietly dominant. You get 2.625x on everything (2.25x at the $100K Preferred Honors tier) with zero category management, Priority Pass with two guests, and $480 in credits that drop the effective fee to around $70. The catch is real though: without a high BofA Rewards tier, this is a mediocre $550 card and you should look at the Venture X instead.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
The Bank of America Premium Rewards Elite is BofA's big swing at the premium travel card segment — and whether it lands depends entirely on one question: are you a BofA Rewards member with serious money at BofA and Merrill? (BofA Rewards replaced Preferred Rewards in May 2026.) At $550 a year, this card goes toe-to-toe with the Chase Sapphire Reserve and Amex Platinum, but it takes a fundamentally different approach. Instead of transferable points and aspirational award charts, you get fixed-value points turbocharged by BofA Rewards, plus a pile of credits and Priority Pass for you and two guests.

At the top Premier tier ($1M+ in combined balances), the earning rates become absurd — 3.5x on travel and dining, 2.625x on everything else. The $100K Preferred Honors tier still gets a solid 3x and 2.25x. Pair that with $300 in airline credits, a $150 lifestyle credit, lounge access, and a 20% bonus when redeeming for airfare, and you have a premium card that quietly crushes the competition for BofA loyalists. For everyone else? There are better options at this price.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• Priority Pass + 2 Guests: Unlimited access to 1,900+ lounges and experiences worldwide, and you can bring two friends. That guest policy is among the most generous in the game.
  • $300 Airline Incidental Credit: Calendar-year credit for checked bags, seat upgrades, in-flight purchases, and airline lounge fees on select U.S. airlines — no need to pick one.
  • $150 Lifestyle Credit: Annual credit for streaming, food delivery, fitness subscriptions, and rideshare. The kind of stuff you're already spending on.
  • TSA PreCheck / Global Entry Credit: Up to $120 reimbursement every four years.
  • BofA Rewards Boost: 10% to 75% bonus on the points you earn from purchases, depending on your tier — 50% at Preferred Honors ($100K+), 75% at Premier ($1M+). This is where the card transforms.
  • 20% Airfare Boost: Flights booked with points through BofA Travel cost 20% fewer points, so each point is worth 1.25 cents. Elite-exclusive perk.
  • No foreign transaction fees.
  • Visa Infinite: Premium-tier protections including primary rental car CDW, trip cancellation/delay, lost luggage, and emergency evacuation.

The math here is pretty compelling: $300 airline credit + $150 lifestyle credit + ~$30/year amortized Global Entry = $480 in credits. That brings the effective fee down to roughly $70 a year. At that price, you're getting Priority Pass with two guests and boosted earning rates for less than the cost of a nice dinner. Not bad.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
Earn 75,000 bonus points after spending $5,000 in purchases within the first 90 days.

At 1 cent per point, that's $750 in value. Use the 20% airfare boost through BofA Travel and you're looking at $937.50. Combined with first-year credits, this card is heavily net-positive out of the gate — making that $550 sticker price a lot less scary.

You're not paying $550 for better earn rates — you're paying for the credits, the lounge access, and the 20% airfare redemption boost. The BofA Rewards multiplier works the same way on both cards. So if you don't need the premium perks, the regular Premium Rewards gives you the same earning power for $455 less.

Heads up: BofA Rewards replaced Preferred Rewards in May 2026, and the 75% boost that used to kick in at $100K now takes $1M+ (Premier). Platinum Honors members who enrolled before May 26, 2026 may keep 75% on an existing card for a while, but new cards earn at the new tier's rate.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
• Airfare (Elite exclusive): 1.25 cents per point for flights through BofA Travel (you pay 20% fewer points). That 20% boost is why this is a better flight redemption card than its sibling.
  • Other travel: 1 cent per point for hotels, rental cars, etc.
  • Statement credit: 1 cent per point. Straightforward.
  • Cash deposit: Direct deposit into your BofA checking or savings.
  • Gift cards: Available, but meh value.

No transfer partners — and that's the elephant in the room. You won't be booking Hyatt aspirational stays or United Polaris redemptions with these points. But you also won't be checking award availability at 3am or stress-refreshing for saver space. Fixed-value has its perks (pun intended). The 20% airfare bonus is BofA's way of nudging you toward flight bookings, and it's a nice sweetener.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• $300 Airline Incidental Credit: Up to $300 each calendar year on select U.S. airlines — no need to pick one (Allegiant, Spirit and Sun Country don't count); covers baggage fees, seat upgrades, change fees, in-flight food/drinks, and airline lounge fees.

title: Hilton Honors American Express Aspire
scouts_verdict: If Hilton is your ride-or-die hotel chain, the Aspire is still a slam dunk — even after the Priority Pass removal. A free night at a Waldorf Astoria can be worth more than the entire $550 fee. Diamond status means space-available upgrades and executive lounge access without grinding 50 nights. And the 200,000-point welcome offer (through January 13, 2027) is the best this card has ever had. But be honest with yourself: if you stay at Hilton fewer than 5-6 times a year, a flexible points card will treat you better.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
If Hilton is your hotel chain — like, genuinely your go-to, not just the one you occasionally book — the Hilton Honors American Express Aspire is probably the single best hotel credit card you can get. For $550 a year, you get automatic Diamond status (Hilton's second-highest tier, behind only the new Diamond Reserve), a free night reward certificate that can be worth more than the annual fee on its own, a $400 resort credit, and earning rates that are frankly absurd at Hilton properties.

Let's talk numbers: 14x base at Hilton hotels, which stacks with Diamond status to hit 34x total at most Hilton brands. That's roughly a 17-20% return at Hilton properties. The card also earns 7x on flights, car rentals, and U.S. restaurants, and 3x on everything else. The per-point value is lower than Amex Membership Rewards (roughly 0.5 to 0.6 cents each), but the high earn rates more than compensate.

One thing to know upfront: Priority Pass lounge access was removed from this card in 2024. That stings. But Diamond status still gets you into Hilton executive lounges, and the credit package is strong enough to justify the fee for dedicated Hilton travelers. Just don't buy this card expecting airport lounge access anymore.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• Automatic Diamond Status: Hilton's second-highest tier (only the new Diamond Reserve, which takes 80 nights or 40 stays plus $18,000 in Hilton spend, sits above it) — normally requires 50 nights, 25 stays, or $11,500 in eligible Hilton spend per year. You get suite upgrades (when available), executive lounge access, daily food and beverage credit, and a 100% bonus on base points. Basically, the VIP treatment without the grind.
  • 14x at Hilton (34x with Diamond): On eligible purchases at Hilton hotels and resorts worldwide. This is where the card really shines.
  • 7x on Flights, Car Rentals, U.S. Restaurants: Flights booked direct or through Amex Travel, car rentals direct, and dining out.
  • 3x on Everything Else: A respectable base rate that keeps non-category spending productive.
  • Free Night Reward: One per year (usable any day of the week), valid at most Hilton properties including Waldorf Astoria and Conrad. This alone can be worth $300-$800+ at a luxury property. Earn additional Free Night Rewards by spending $30,000 (one night) and $60,000 (a second night) on the card in a calendar year.
  • $400 Hilton Resort Credit: Up to $200 semiannually for eligible resort purchases. Spa day, dinner, golf — it all counts at qualifying resorts.
  • $200 Flight Credit: Up to $50 per quarter for flights purchased directly or through Amex Travel.
  • $219 CLEAR+ Credit: Annual statement credit for a CLEAR+ membership.
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees.

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:
• Annual Fee: $550
  • Authorized User Fee: No additional fee. But heads up — authorized users don't get Diamond status or lounge access.
  • Foreign Transaction Fees: None
  • APR: Variable APR on purchases (yes, this is a credit card, not a charge card — but carrying a balance on a $550 card is a choice you should not make).
  • Note: Priority Pass lounge access was removed as of February 1, 2024. RIP.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
Right now the Aspire is offering 200,000 Hilton Honors points after spending $6,000 in the first 6 months — and you still get the card's annual Free Night Reward in year one. This limited-time offer runs through January 13, 2027, and it's the best welcome bonus in the card's history. If you've been on the fence, this is the time.

At 0.5 to 0.6 cents per point, the bonus alone is worth roughly $1,000 to $1,200 in hotel stays. Add the free night certificate — easily $300-$800+ at a Waldorf Astoria or Conrad — and you're looking at roughly $1,300 to $2,000 in first-year value before you even touch the resort and flight credits.

Pro tip: Amex's once-per-lifetime rule applies here, so you can't get the bonus if you have or have ever had the Aspire. Having held the Surpass or the Hilton Business card doesn't disqualify you, but read the offer terms carefully before applying.

sections.title: Earning Rates
sections.content:
• 14x points: Purchases at Hilton hotels and resorts (34x total with Diamond status bonus at most brands; 24x at Home2 Suites, Homewood Suites, Spark and Tru, which earn 5 base points per dollar)
  • 7x points: Flights booked directly with airlines or through Amex Travel
  • 7x points: Car rentals booked directly with select companies
  • 7x points: U.S. restaurants
  • 3x points: All other eligible purchases

Those multipliers look wild, but let's keep it real: Hilton points are worth roughly 0.5 to 0.6 cents each. So 7x on dining works out to about 3.5 to 4.2% back — good, but not dramatically better than a 4x Membership Rewards card. Where this card becomes genuinely unbeatable is at Hilton properties: 34x with Diamond status translates to roughly 17-20% back. Put every Hilton charge on this card. Every single one.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
Hilton Honors points live in the Hilton ecosystem:

  • Hotel Stays (Best Value): Free nights range from 5,000 to 250,000 points depending on property and dates. As a Diamond member, you may score upgrades on award stays too.
  • Points + Cash: Combine points and money for stays, though the value is usually worse than going all-points.
  • Fifth Night Free: Book 5 consecutive nights on points and night #5 is free — an automatic 20% discount on longer stays.
  • Amazon Shop With Points: Terrible value. Hard pass.
  • Transfer to Airlines: 10,000:1,000 ratio. Awful unless there's a transfer bonus and you need a small top-up.
  • Experiences and Events: Concerts, events, experiences. Value varies wildly.

The move: Redeem for premium Hilton properties — Waldorf Astoria, Conrad, LXR. A Waldorf night that costs $600+ and requires 95,000 points gives you 0.63+ cents per point. That's well above average and makes the earn rates even more compelling.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• Diamond Status: The best Hilton status a card can get you (only the new Diamond Reserve tier, earned purely through stays and spend, sits above it). Suite upgrades when available, executive lounge access (breakfast, evening apps, drinks), daily food and beverage credit at most U.S. properties (continental breakfast abroad), late checkout, and 100% bonus on base Hilton points. This is the reason most people get this card.
  • Free Night Reward: Issued in year one and after each anniversary. Valid at almost all Hilton properties, including Waldorf Astoria and Conrad. Using this at a luxury property is the single best way to justify the annual fee.
  • $400 Resort Credit: Up to $200 semiannually at participating Hilton resort properties. Dining, spa, golf, resort charges — but the property must carry a "resort" designation, so check before you book.
  • $200 Flight Credit: Up to $50 per quarter for direct airline or Amex Travel flight purchases. Replaces the old $250 airline incidental fee credit.
  • $219 CLEAR+ Credit: Annual statement credit for CLEAR+ membership.
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees: Use it internationally without surcharges.

The elephant in the room: Priority Pass Select was removed February 1, 2024. You still get lounge access at Hilton properties through Diamond status, but airport lounge access is gone unless you carry another card for that.
