The Aspire gets you Diamond, the best Hilton status any credit card can give you, plus the most generous resort credits. Yes, losing Priority Pass hurts — the Marriott Brilliant still has it. But the Aspire's uncapped free night certificate (hello, Waldorf Astoria) and Diamond status perks make it the clear winner for anyone who's genuinely loyal to Hilton. If you split stays across multiple chains, a flexible points card is probably smarter.

sections.title: Best For
sections.content:
The Aspire is built for one person: the dedicated Hilton loyalist who stays at Hilton properties multiple times a year and wants Diamond status without the 50-night grind. If you book Hilton resorts regularly, the $400 resort credit and free night reward can cover the annual fee before you even think about points. The current 200,000-point welcome offer (through January 13, 2027) is the best in the card's history — if this card has been on your radar, stop waiting.

Not the right card for: hotel chain hoppers, people who stay at Hilton once or twice a year, or anyone who expects airport lounge access (that ship has sailed).

title: Bilt Mastercard Blue
scouts_verdict: The Bilt Blue is the most obvious card for any renter or mortgage-payer in America. Transferable points on housing payments — for free. That alone justifies the wallet slot. The 1x everyday rate is nothing special, and that's the catch: under Bilt 2.0 your housing points depend on everyday spend on this card (75% of your rent for 1x, 100% for 1.25x). Rent alone gets you a flat 250 points. So route enough spending here to hit your tier, let a stronger card handle the rest, and make sure this is the card paying your rent every single month.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
The Bilt Mastercard Blue does one thing that no other no-annual-fee card can: it earns transferable rewards on rent and mortgage payments without charging you a transaction fee. That's it. That's the pitch. And honestly? For the millions of Americans whose largest monthly expense is housing, that pitch is enough.

Under the Bilt 2.0 revamp, the Blue earns 1x points on everyday (non-housing) purchases, with housing earnings scaling up to 1.25x based on how much everyday spending you put on the card. Or pick the Flexible Bilt Cash option instead: 4% back in Bilt Cash on everyday spend on top of your base points, which you can then spend to unlock up to 1x on housing. And the full Bilt transfer partner network — Hyatt, United, Air Canada, Turkish, Atmos Rewards (Alaska/Hawaiian), and more — is available at $0 per year. No other free card gives you transferable points and housing rewards. It's genuinely in a class of one.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• Earn on Rent and Mortgage: Up to 1.25x on housing payments with no transaction fees. This is the card's entire reason for existing, and it's a good one.
  • $0 Annual Fee: Free to hold. No excuses not to have it.
  • Transferable Points: Full access to Bilt's 1:1 transfer network — Hyatt, United, Air Canada Aeroplan, Turkish Miles&Smiles, Virgin Atlantic, Atmos Rewards (Alaska/Hawaiian), and more.
  • 1x on Everyday Purchases: The base rate won't blow you away, but it's free points.
  • Optional 4% Bilt Cash: Earn 4% Bilt Cash on everyday purchases alongside your base points if you choose the Flexible Bilt Cash option. The catch: that option swaps the up-to-1.25x housing tiers for up to 1x on housing, unlocked by spending $3 of Bilt Cash per 100 points. You run one option at a time and can switch for the next billing cycle.
  • Rent Day (1st of each month): Double points on everyday purchases (up to 1,000 bonus points), transfer bonuses, and partner offers. It's become a whole thing.
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees: Take it traveling.
  • Mastercard Benefits: Cell phone protection, purchase assurance, and MasterRental coverage.

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:
Annual Fee$0
Foreign Transaction FeeNone
Rent / Mortgage Payment FeeNone
Late Payment FeeUp to $41

Zero fees where it counts. You pay nothing for the card, nothing for housing payments, and nothing for foreign transactions. The value proposition here is almost comically simple: turn your biggest monthly bill into points, for free.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
New cardholders get $100 in Bilt Cash upon approval — no spending requirement at all.

It's modest. It's not going to fund a vacation. But it's a guaranteed perk just for getting approved, which is more than you can say for most welcome offers. Just remember Bilt Cash isn't cash: you can't cash it out or use it as a statement credit. The real value of this card is the ongoing housing rewards, not the sign-up bonus.

Fine print: no bonus if you have, or have ever had, a Bilt Card 2.0 (the Column-issued Blue, Obsidian or Palladium), or already got a Bilt Card 2.0 welcome bonus. Bilt Cash also expires at the end of each calendar year, with up to $100 rolling over.

sections.content:

Housing Earning Tiers

On the Housing-only option (the default), your housing rate depends on your Everyday Spend Ratio — basically, how much you use the card for non-housing purchases relative to your monthly housing payment:

  • 25% ratio: 0.5x on housing
  • 50% ratio: 0.75x on housing
  • 75% ratio: 1.0x on housing
  • 100% ratio: 1.25x on housing
  • Under 25%: a flat 250 points per billing cycle

Or pick the Flexible Bilt Cash option: you earn 4% back in Bilt Cash on everyday spending on top of your base points, then spend $3 of Bilt Cash per 100 points ($30 per 1,000) to unlock up to 1x on housing. You give up the tiers above, and you can switch options for the next billing cycle.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
• Transfer Partners: 1:1 transfers to United, Hyatt, Air Canada Aeroplan, Turkish Miles&Smiles, Virgin Atlantic, IHG, Atmos Rewards (Alaska/Hawaiian), and more. American Airlines left Bilt in June 2024.
  • Bilt Travel Portal: Book flights and hotels directly with points.
  • Rent / Mortgage: Use points to cover future housing payments — a unique Bilt perk.
  • Home Down Payment: Put points toward a down payment or closing costs on a home at 1.5 cents each. Seriously.
  • Fitness: Redeem for SoulCycle, Rumble, and other fitness classes.
  • Statement Credits, Lyft, Amazon, and Gift Cards: Pay down your Bilt Card balance, cover Lyft rides, shop at Amazon.com, or grab gift cards with points. Easy, but usually a weaker use than transfers.
  • Bilt Cash: Can't be turned into a statement credit. Spend it on monthly Lyft, Walgreens and Grubhub credits, Bilt Travel hotel bookings, or transfer-bonus upgrades, or, on the Flexible Bilt Cash option, use it to unlock points on housing.

Transfers are the play. Hyatt especially — you can squeeze 2+ cents per point out of premium hotel stays, which means your rent payments are quietly funding your next vacation. That's a pretty good deal for a free card.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• No Annual Credits: This is a $0 card, so no travel credits. Fair enough.
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees: Useful when traveling abroad.
  • Cell Phone Protection: Up to $800 per claim ($50 deductible) when you pay your phone bill with the card, up to 2 claims per 12 months. Underrated perk.
  • Purchase Assurance: Coverage for new purchases against damage or theft.
  • MasterRental Coverage: Rental car insurance through Mastercard.
  • Rent Day Perks: On the 1st of each month, Bilt runs promotions — transfer bonuses, double points on everyday card spend (up to 1,000 bonus points), and partner deals. Mark your calendar.

sections.title: Competitor Comparison
sections.content:
CardAnnual FeeEarn RateKey Differentiator

Every other no-fee card earns more on everyday spending. The Double Cash gives you 2x everywhere. The CFU gives you 1.5x with bonus categories. But none of them earn a single point on your rent or mortgage. If housing is your biggest expense (and for most people, it is), the Bilt Blue fills a gap that literally no one else does.

sections.title: Best For
sections.content:
• Renters and homeowners who want to turn their biggest monthly bill into transferable points — for free
  • Points beginners who want a zero-risk entry into Hyatt, United, Atmos Rewards (Alaska/Hawaiian), and other transfer partners
  • Anyone who pays rent or a mortgage and isn't currently earning rewards on it (which is... almost everyone)

Don't expect much from the 1x everyday rate on its own. But under Bilt 2.0 it no longer pays to use the Blue only for housing either. On the default Housing-only option, rent alone earns a flat 250 points per billing cycle, and the real housing multiplier needs everyday spend on this card worth at least 25% of your rent (75% for 1x, 100% for 1.25x). Put enough daily spending here to hit your tier and let a stronger category card handle the rest. Think of it as a housing specialist that needs some everyday spend to really pay off. But as a specialist? It's unmatched.

title: Bilt Mastercard Obsidian
scouts_verdict: The Bilt Obsidian hits the sweet spot for renters and homeowners who want category bonuses with their housing rewards. At $95 with a $100 hotel credit, the fee is effectively negative — and 3x dining with Hyatt transfer access is a sneaky-powerful combo. It doesn't quite match the Sapphire Preferred's travel breadth, but no $95 card on the planet lets you earn transferable points on rent.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
The Bilt Mastercard Obsidian is the Goldilocks card in the Bilt 2.0 lineup — more firepower than the free Blue, less commitment than the premium Palladium. At $95 a year, it brings 3x on your choice of dining or groceries, 2x on travel, and the same housing-earning engine that makes all Bilt cards unique. Plus, the $100 annual hotel credit effectively makes the fee disappear.

Here's why it's interesting: this card plays in the same sandbox as the Chase Sapphire Preferred and Citi Strata Premier, but it brings something neither of them can — rewards on your rent or mortgage. If you're a renter who dines out a lot or a homeowner with a big grocery budget, the Obsidian gives you CSP-level category earning and points on housing. That's a combination nobody else at $95 can match.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• 3x on Dining or Groceries: Pick one bonus category for the year — dining (unlimited) or groceries (up to $25,000/year). Choose wisely.
  • 2x on Travel: Airlines, hotels, car rentals and cruise lines booked direct. Book through the Bilt Travel portal and it's 3x on flights and 4x on hotels. (Trains, transit and taxis earn just 1x.)
  • Up to 1.25x on Housing: Earn on rent, mortgage, and HOA fees with no transaction fees. The Bilt special.
  • $100 Bilt Travel Hotel Credit: Two $50 credits per year (one for Jan–Jun, one for Jul–Dec, no rollover) for hotel stays of 2+ nights booked through the Bilt portal. Use both and this wipes out the annual fee.
  • Optional 4% Bilt Cash: Switch to the Flexible Bilt Cash option and you earn 4% Bilt Cash on everyday purchases on top of your base points. The catch: you give up the tiered housing points and instead unlock up to 1x on housing by spending Bilt Cash ($3 per 100 points).
  • Full Transfer Partner Access: 1:1 transfers to Hyatt, United, Air Canada, Turkish Airlines, Atmos Rewards (Alaska/Hawaiian), and more.
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees.
  • World Elite Mastercard: Cell phone protection, travel insurance, concierge services.

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:
Annual Fee$95
Authorized User Fee$50 per user per year
Foreign Transaction FeeNone
Rent / Mortgage Payment FeeNone
Late Payment FeeUp to $41

The $100 hotel credit more than covers the $95 fee — book a 2-night-plus hotel stay through the Bilt portal in each half of the year (the credit comes as $50 for Jan–Jun and $50 for Jul–Dec) and you're net positive. Effective cost: essentially $0 or better. That makes the category bonuses and housing rewards pure upside.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
New cardholders receive $200 in Bilt Cash upon approval — no minimum spending requirement. It's once per person: you're not eligible if you have or ever had a Bilt Card 2.0, or already got a Bilt Card 2.0 welcome bonus. And spend it — Bilt Cash expires at the end of each calendar year (up to $100 rolls over).

No hoops, no $4,000 in 3 months. Just get approved and the $200 shows up. It's refreshingly simple. The real value, of course, is the ongoing earning on housing plus category bonuses — that's where the Obsidian pays dividends month after month.

sections.title: Earning Rates
sections.content:

Dining or Groceries (choose one)3x
Hotels via Bilt Travel portal4x
Flights via Bilt Travel portal3x
Travel booked direct (airlines, hotels, car rentals, cruise lines)2x

Housing Earning Tiers

Same tiered system as all Bilt cards (on the default Housing-only option) — earn more on housing by using the card for everyday spending too:

  • 25% ratio: 0.5x on housing
  • 50% ratio: 0.75x on housing
  • 75% ratio: 1.0x on housing
  • 100% ratio: 1.25x on housing

Quick note: the grocery 3x is capped at $25,000 per year (plenty for most households); dining 3x is unlimited. Pick the category that matches your spending. If you eat out more than you cook, go dining. If your Costco runs are legendary, go groceries.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
• Transfer Partners: 1:1 transfers to United, Hyatt, Air Canada Aeroplan, Turkish Miles&Smiles, Virgin Atlantic, IHG, Atmos Rewards (Alaska/Hawaiian), Avianca LifeMiles, and more.
  • Bilt Travel Portal: Book flights and hotels with points.
  • Rent / Mortgage: Apply points toward housing payments.
  • Statement Credit: Redeem points (1,000 minimum) toward your Bilt Card balance.
  • Home Down Payment: Put points toward a home down payment at 1.5 cents each.
  • Fitness Classes: Redeem points for classes at Bilt's partner studios.
  • Bilt Cash: Use it in the Bilt ecosystem — Bilt Travel hotel bookings, monthly Lyft/Walgreens/Grubhub credits, the Point Accelerator. It can't be turned into a statement credit.

Transfers to Hyatt are the money move. At 1.5-2.5 cents per point on premium stays, your 3x dining rate effectively becomes 4.5-7.5% back when you funnel those points into a nice hotel. That's better than almost any cash back card at any price.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• $100 Bilt Travel Hotel Credit: Two $50 credits per year (one for Jan–Jun, one for Jul–Dec, no rollover) for hotel stays of 2+ nights booked through the Bilt portal.
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees: Spend freely abroad.
  • Cell Phone Protection: Up to $800 per claim ($50 deductible), up to 2 claims per 12 months. Pay your phone bill with this card.
  • World Elite Mastercard: Travel insurance, rental car CDW, concierge services, and airport experiences.
  • Rent Day (1st of each month): Special promotions and bonus transfer opportunities. Set a monthly reminder.

sections.title: Competitor Comparison
sections.content:

Chase Sapphire Preferred$953x / 2-5x / 1xBroader travel bonuses, Ultimate Rewards transfers
Citi Strata Premier$953x / 3-10x / 1x3x on more categories, ThankYou transfers

The Obsidian doesn't beat the CSP or Strata Premier on pure earning. But it does something they can't: earn on housing. If your rent is $2,000 a month and you hit the 1.25x tier, that's 2,500 transferable points per month that Chase and Citi cardholders simply don't get. Over a year, that adds up fast.

sections.title: Best For
sections.content:
• Renters and homeowners who dine out — 3x dining plus housing rewards on one card is a powerful combo
  • Grocery-heavy households who can max out the 3x grocery option alongside housing earnings
  • CSP-curious renters who want Sapphire-caliber earning with housing rewards on top

The Obsidian makes sense if you'll use the $100 hotel credit and earn meaningfully on both housing and your 3x category. If you don't pay rent or a mortgage, a Chase Sapphire Preferred is probably the simpler $95 choice — but if you do, the Obsidian has a real edge.

title: Bilt Mastercard Palladium
scouts_verdict: The Bilt Palladium is a legit premium card contender. Flat 2x everywhere with transferable points, $600 in annual credits that beat the $495 fee, Priority Pass for you and two guests, and up to 1.25x on rent or mortgage with no transaction fee. If you pay rent or a mortgage and want one card to handle everything, the Palladium makes an argument that the Venture X and CSR simply can't.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
The Bilt Mastercard Palladium is Bilt's premium flagship, and it wants to be your one card for everything. At $495 a year, you get a flat 2x on all everyday spending, up to 1.25x on housing, Priority Pass lounge access with two guests, $400 in hotel credits, $200 in annual Bilt Cash, a concierge, and access to the full Bilt transfer partner lineup. Oh, and if you pick the Flexible Bilt Cash option instead of the tiered housing points, you also get 4% back in Bilt Cash on top of that 2x. It's a lot.

Here's the pitch in plain English: the Palladium is a Capital One Venture X competitor that also earns on your rent or mortgage. If you're a high spender who wants one premium card that does everything without category micromanagement — and you happen to pay housing — this is the card that was designed for you. The $600 in annual credits exceed the $495 fee before you earn a single point, and the flat 2x earn rate means you never have to think about which card to pull out.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• 2x on Everything: Flat-rate earning on every non-housing transaction. No categories, no caps, no mental gymnastics.
  • Up to 1.25x on Housing: Earn on rent, mortgage, and HOA fees with no transaction fees. The Bilt signature move.
  • $400 Bilt Travel Hotel Credit: Two $200 credits per year (one per half-year) for hotel stays of 2+ nights booked through the Bilt portal. This alone covers most of the fee.
  • $200 Annual Bilt Cash Bonus: Credited at account opening and every January 1st after that. Free money, recurring.
  • Priority Pass + 2 Guests: Unlimited access to 1,300+ lounges. Bring your travel crew.
  • 4% Bilt Cash on Everyday Spending: Stacks on top of the 2x base if you choose the Flexible Bilt Cash option. The catch: that option swaps the up-to-1.25x housing tiers for up to 1x on housing, unlocked by spending $3 of Bilt Cash per 100 points. You run one option at a time and can switch for the next billing cycle.
  • Full Transfer Partner Access: 1:1 to Hyatt, United, Air Canada, Turkish, Virgin Atlantic, IHG, Atmos Rewards (Alaska/Hawaiian), and more.
  • Mastercard Concierge: White-glove help with travel, dining, and events. The kind of perk that's nice until you actually need it — then it's amazing.
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees.
  • World Legend Mastercard: Top-tier protections — cell phone coverage, travel insurance, rental car CDW.

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:
Annual Fee$495

Let's do the math: $400 hotel credit + $200 Bilt Cash = $600 in annual value, as long as you book a 2+ night Bilt Travel hotel stay in each half of the year and spend the Bilt Cash before it expires. The fee is $495. You're $105 ahead before earning a single point, sipping a single lounge coffee, or calling the concierge once. That's not creative accounting — that's just credits exceeding the fee. Straightforward.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
Earn 50,000 Bilt Points + Gold Status after spending $4,000 on everyday purchases in the first 90 days, plus $300 in Bilt Cash on approval.

Eligibility note: no welcome bonus if you have, or have ever had, a Bilt Card 2.0 (Blue, Obsidian or Palladium issued by Column N.A.), or have already received a Bilt Card 2.0 welcome bonus. Upgrading from another Bilt card may get you an upgrade bonus instead.

That's a strong package. The 50,000 points are fully transferable — route them through Hyatt at ~2 cents per point and you're looking at up to $1,000 in hotel value. Add the $300 Bilt Cash and first-year credits, and the Palladium pays for itself several times over in year one. Premium card sticker shock, first-year value that more than compensates.

Bilt's own ecosystem bumps a few things above the 2x base: 4x on hotels and 3x on flights booked through Bilt Travel, 4x on Lyft with linked accounts, and up to 5x at Bilt Dining partner restaurants.

Housing Earning Tiers

Same formula across all Bilt cards — on the Housing-only option (the default), your housing rate scales with your Everyday Spend Ratio, meaning your non-housing card spend as a share of your housing payment:

  • 25% ratio: 0.5x on housing
  • 50% ratio: 0.75x on housing
  • 75% ratio: 1.0x on housing
  • 100% ratio: 1.25x on housing
  • Under 25%: no multiplier, just a flat 250 points per billing cycle

The flat 2x on everything is this card's killer feature. No choosing categories, no caps, no rotating quarterly nonsense. Every swipe earns at least 2x. Pick the Flexible Bilt Cash option to layer on 4% Bilt Cash and your effective return on everyday spending is well above 2% — and that's before you even consider transfer partner value. For people who hate optimizing and just want one great card, this is the answer.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
• Transfer Partners: 1:1 to United, Hyatt, Air Canada Aeroplan, Turkish Miles&Smiles, Virgin Atlantic, IHG, Atmos Rewards (Alaska/Hawaiian), Avianca LifeMiles, and more. American Airlines left Bilt in June 2024.
  • Bilt Travel Portal: Book flights and hotels directly.
  • Rent / Mortgage: Apply points toward housing payments. Yes, your credit card rewards can pay your rent.
  • Home Down Payment: Put points toward a home down payment or closing costs at 1.5 cents each.
  • Fitness and Lyft: Redeem for fitness classes and Lyft rides.
  • Bilt Cash: Can't be redeemed as a statement credit toward your card balance. Spend it on Lyft, Bilt Travel hotels, Grubhub, Walgreens and more, or use it to unlock housing points or a Point Accelerator.
  • Statement Credits and Gift Cards: Pay down your card balance or grab gift cards with points. Easy, but usually a weaker use than transfers.

Transfer partners are the highest-value play, always. At 2x earning on everything, you accumulate points fast. Move them to Hyatt for premium stays and you're looking at 4+ cents per dollar spent on everyday purchases. That turns your coffee run, your Amazon order, and your grocery haul into future hotel stays. It's a good system.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• $400 Bilt Travel Hotel Credit: Two $200 credits per year (one for January–June, one for July–December) for Bilt Travel hotel bookings of 2+ nights. Unused halves don't roll over.
  • $200 Annual Bilt Cash Bonus: Automatically credited at account opening and every January 1. No action needed, but Bilt Cash expires December 31 (up to $100 rolls over).
  • Priority Pass + 2 Guests: Unlimited entry at 1,300+ lounges (excluding restaurants). Bring your people. Authorized users get Priority Pass too.
  • Mastercard Concierge: Personalized travel planning, dining reservations, and event access.
  • Cell Phone Protection: Up to $800 per claim ($50 deductible), up to 2 claims per 12 months.
  • Trip Cancellation/Interruption: Covers non-refundable common-carrier fares (flights, trains, buses, cruises) if illness, injury or death cancels or cuts short your trip, up to $2,000 per trip.
  • Trip Delay Reimbursement: Up to $300 per trip when a common-carrier delay runs more than 6 hours (1 claim per 12 months).
  • Baggage Delay Insurance: Reimbursement for essentials if your bags go on their own adventure.
  • Extended Warranty: Extra protection on eligible purchases beyond the manufacturer's warranty.
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees.

The Palladium vs. Venture X is the real comparison. Both earn 2x on everything with transfer partners. The Palladium adds housing rewards, more credits ($600 vs. $400), and Bilt Cash — but costs $100 more and doesn't have Capital One's growing lounge network. Against the CSR and Amex Platinum, the Palladium trades lounge variety for a simpler, higher flat-rate return and the unique housing angle. If you pay rent, the Palladium has an argument that nobody else can make.

sections.title: Best For
sections.content:
• High spenders who want one premium card that earns 2x on everything without thinking about categories
  • Renters and homeowners who want premium card perks plus housing rewards — exactly the combo this card was built for
  • Points maximizers who'll leverage Hyatt and airline transfers to squeeze outsized value from a flat 2x earn rate

The Palladium is Bilt's bid to be the only premium card you need. $600 in credits that exceed the $495 fee, 2x on everything, Priority Pass with two guests, and up to 1.25x on rent or mortgage with no transaction fee. If housing is your biggest expense and you want one card to rule the rest of your spending too, this is the play.

title: Chase Freedom Unlimited
scouts_verdict: The Freedom Unlimited is the Swiss Army knife of the Chase lineup. Solo, it's a perfectly good 1.5% cash back card with a 3% kicker on dining. But pair it with a Sapphire Preferred or Reserve and it transforms — your everyday spending suddenly earns transferable points that can top 2 cents each through partners like Hyatt (though Preferred points now go to Hyatt at 4:3, not 1:1). The $200 bonus for just $500 in spend is easy money, and the 15-month 0% APR adds flexibility. The 3% foreign transaction fee means you need something else for international trips, but domestically? This belongs in your wallet if you're in the Chase ecosystem.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
The Chase Freedom Unlimited might be the most underappreciated card in the Chase ecosystem. On the surface, it's a no-annual-fee card earning 1.5% on everything, with 3% on dining and drugstores and 5% on Chase Travel portal bookings. Solid. Not flashy. But here's the thing: pair it with a Chase Sapphire Preferred or Reserve, and those "cash back" rewards transform into Ultimate Rewards points that transfer to Hyatt, United, Southwest, and more.

That dual identity — simple cash back card for casual users, transferable points engine for enthusiasts — is what makes the CFU so versatile. It also throws in a 0% intro APR for 15 months and requires exactly zero annual fees, ever. Whether you're building a Chase points strategy or just want a no-fuss card that earns well on everything, the Freedom Unlimited delivers.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• 1.5% on everything: No caps, no categories to track, no quarterly activations. Just spend and earn.
  • 5% on Chase Travel: Book through the Chase portal and earn 5x. Nice bump for travel planners.
  • 3% on dining and drugstores: Restaurants, takeout, delivery, and your pharmacy runs all earn elevated rates.
  • 0% intro APR for 15 months: On both purchases and balance transfers. Useful for big buys or debt consolidation.
  • $0 annual fee: Forever. No fee creep, no strings.
  • Purchase protection: 120 days of coverage against damage or theft on new purchases.
  • Extended warranty: Adds up to one year on eligible manufacturer warranties.
  • Trip cancellation/interruption: Coverage when you book travel with the card.
  • No minimum redemption: Cash out any amount, any time.

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:
Annual Fee: $0

Foreign Transaction Fee: 3% of each transaction in U.S. dollars

Balance Transfer Fee: Either $5 or 3% of the amount transferred, whichever is greater (within 60 days); 5% or $5 minimum thereafter

Cash Advance Fee: Either $10 or 5% of the amount, whichever is greater

Late Payment Fee: Up to $40

The $0 fee is the headline. But that 3% foreign transaction fee is a dealbreaker for international spending — leave this one at home when you travel abroad and use something with no FTF instead.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
Right now: $200 bonus after spending just $500 in the first 3 months. That's the standard offer — the limited-time $250 bump from earlier this year is over. You can't get it if you already have the card or earned its bonus in the past 24 months.

$500 in 3 months is about $167 a month. Your phone bill and a few grocery trips will get you there. The card has occasionally offered bonuses as high as $300 during promo windows, so $200 isn't the ceiling — if you're not in a hurry, it can pay to wait for a bump. Either way, it's easy money.

Pro tip: if you also hold a Sapphire Preferred or Reserve, those 20,000 Ultimate Rewards points can become worth more when redeemed through Chase's transfer partners. The bonus is good; the ecosystem makes it better.

No caps on any category, all rewards earned as Ultimate Rewards points (1 point = 1 cent as cash back). The 1.5% base rate is what separates this from the pack — most no-fee cards give you just 1% on non-bonus spending. That extra half percent adds up faster than you'd think when it applies to literally everything.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
Points from the Freedom Unlimited can be redeemed for:

  • Cash back as a statement credit or direct deposit (1 point = 1 cent)
  • Gift cards from major retailers (generally 1 cent per point)
  • Travel through Chase Travel at 1 cent per point
  • Amazon purchases at checkout using Shop with Points (only 0.8 cents per point, so cash back is the better deal)

But here's the real play: hold a Chase Sapphire Preferred or Sapphire Reserve, and you can pool your Freedom Unlimited points with that card. For new Sapphire cardholders, Chase Travel redemptions start at 1 cent per point, but Points Boost pushes select flights and hotels to up to 1.5 cents (Preferred) or 2 cents (Reserve) — so your 1.5% base rate can work out to 2.25% or even 3% on the right booking. More importantly, you unlock transfers to Hyatt, United, Southwest, and more (just note that Preferred points go to Hyatt at 4:3, not 1:1 — right away if you applied on or after June 15, 2026, and from October 1, 2026 for everyone else). The CFU on its own is fine. The CFU in the Chase ecosystem is genuinely excellent.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
It's a free card, so don't expect the Ritz. But the protections are surprisingly decent:

  • Trip cancellation/interruption: Up to $1,500 per person and $6,000 per trip for prepaid, non-refundable travel.
  • Auto rental CDW: Secondary coverage in the U.S., primary when you rent abroad. Not bad for a $0 card.
  • Roadside assistance: Pay-per-use towing and roadside help, 24/7 in the U.S. and Canada.
  • Travel and emergency assistance: 24/7 hotline for medical, legal, and travel emergencies.

No lounge access, no TSA PreCheck credit, no hotel status — those are Sapphire territory. But for a card that costs nothing to hold, having trip insurance and rental car coverage is a nice touch.

On paper, the Double Cash and Active Cash beat the CFU with their 2% flat rate. But the CFU has two advantages they can't match: 3% on dining and drugstores (both earn more than 2% in those categories), and seamless integration with the Chase Sapphire ecosystem. If you have or plan to get a Sapphire card, the CFU's effective value blows past 2%. If you don't? A flat 2% card is probably better for pure cash back.

sections.title: Best For
sections.content:
• Chase Sapphire cardholders who want the best everyday earner in the Ultimate Rewards ecosystem
  • New credit card users looking for a simple, no-fee starting point with room to grow
  • Balance transfer seekers who need 15 months of breathing room at 0% APR
  • Dining regulars who want 3% back at restaurants without paying an annual fee
  • Future points enthusiasts who want to start earning transferable points now and add a Sapphire card later

Skip this if: you travel internationally a lot (3% FTF), you just want the highest flat rate possible (get a 2% card), or you have zero interest in the Chase ecosystem. For everyone else, the Freedom Unlimited earns its wallet spot.

title: Chase Freedom Flex
scouts_verdict:
The Freedom Flex is the overachiever of the Chase family. While its sibling the Unlimited is content being reliable and boring, the Flex rewards you for paying attention — and it rewards you handsomely. Those 5% quarterly categories on Amazon, gas stations, and dining can pile up points fast if you plan around them, and the fixed 3% on dining and drugstores means even a lazy quarter isn't wasted.

But here's the change that matters most: as of September 20, 2026, the Flex charges no foreign transaction fees, which makes it a rare no-fee rotating-category card you can actually take abroad. The trade-off? Chase retired the cell phone protection that same day, so don't lean on the Flex to cover your phone anymore. Add the limited-time $250 sign-up bonus and 0% intro APR, and the value proposition is still borderline unfair for a $0 card.

The power move? Carry both the Freedom Flex and Freedom Unlimited alongside a Sapphire. The Flex handles rotating categories and dining, the Unlimited mops up everything else at 1.5%, and the Sapphire turns all those points into first-class flights and Hyatt stays. If you're only picking one Freedom card, grab the Flex if you'll activate those categories — grab the Unlimited if that sounds like homework.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Look, there are a lot of no-annual-fee cash back cards out there, but the Chase Freedom Flex is the one that keeps showing up at the top of every list — and it deserves to be there. It's built around quarterly rotating 5% cash back categories, plus fixed bonus rates on dining, drugstores, and Chase Travel. Think of it as the successor to the original Chase Freedom, now a World Elite Mastercard — and, since September 20, 2026, one that charges no foreign transaction fees.

Here's the thing that makes the Flex special: it earns Chase Ultimate Rewards points. Pair it with a Sapphire card and suddenly those points become transferable to airlines and hotels — turning a free cash back card into a legitimate travel rewards engine. The combo of 5% rotating categories, 3% on dining, and transferable points makes this arguably the most rewarding no-fee card you can carry, as long as you don't mind setting a quarterly reminder on your phone.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• 5% cash back on up to $1,500 in combined purchases in rotating bonus categories each quarter (activation required)
  • 5% cash back on travel purchased through Chase Travel
  • 3% cash back on dining (including takeout and delivery) and drugstore purchases
  • 1% cash back on all other purchases
  • No annual fee
  • 0% intro APR for 15 months on purchases and balance transfers
  • No foreign transaction fees (the old 3% fee was dropped on September 20, 2026)
  • Perks including 6 months of complimentary DashPass (activate by Dec 31, 2027) and 2% total cash back on Lyft rides through September 30, 2027
  • Purchase protection and extended warranty coverage

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:
Annual Fee: $0

Foreign Transaction Fee: None (Chase dropped the old 3% fee on September 20, 2026)

Balance Transfer Fee: Either $5 or 3% of the amount transferred, whichever is greater (within 60 days); 5% or $5 minimum thereafter

Cash Advance Fee: Either $10 or 5% of the amount, whichever is greater

Late Payment Fee: Up to $40

The short version: no annual fee, which is awesome, and as of September 20, 2026, no foreign transaction fee either. Heading to Paris or Tokyo? The Flex can finally come along without a 3% surcharge on every swipe. Home or abroad, it costs you nothing to hold forever.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
Earn a $250 bonus after you spend $500 on purchases in the first 3 months from account opening. That's a limited-time bump from the standard $200 offer, so don't sit on it.

Spending $500 in 3 months is about as easy as a welcome bonus gets — that's a couple grocery runs and a phone bill. Right now the Flex's limited-time $250 beats the Freedom Unlimited's $200, and it represents a 50% return on the required spend. Not bad for doing what you'd do anyway.

One catch to remember: Chase's 5/24 rule. If you've opened 5 or more credit cards (across all issuers) in the past 24 months, Chase will likely say no. Plan your applications accordingly. Also, the card isn't available to you if you currently have the Flex or received a Flex bonus in the past 24 months.

  • Q3 (Jul–Sep): Gas stations, public transit, EV charging, select live entertainment, United Way donations
  • Q4 (Oct–Dec): Grocery stores (excluding Walmart and Target), dining, American Red Cross donations

And here's the part people forget: you must activate each quarter's bonus by the activation deadline — online, in the Chase app, by phone, in person or by email. Activate partway through the quarter and Chase still applies the 5% retroactively to that quarter's earlier purchases, but skip activation and you're earning a sad 1% instead. Set a calendar reminder. Seriously.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
On its own, you can redeem for the usual stuff:

  • Cash back as a statement credit or direct deposit
  • Gift cards from popular retailers
  • Travel through Chase Travel portal
  • Amazon checkout via Pay with Points

But here's where the magic happens: pool your points with a Sapphire Preferred or Sapphire Reserve and those points get supercharged. Chase Travel redemptions now start at a flat 1 cent per point, but Points Boost deals on select flights and hotels push them up to 1.5 cents (Preferred) or 2 cents (Reserve), so your 5% rotating category earnings can be worth up to 7.5% or even 10% toward travel. That's elite territory for a free card.

Transfer partners include World of Hyatt, United MileagePlus, Southwest Rapid Rewards, British Airways Avios, Air France/KLM Flying Blue, and more. Hyatt transfers are the crown jewel here — you can regularly get 2+ cents per point, making those quarterly bonus categories ridiculously lucrative.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
For a card that costs zero dollars, the Freedom Flex packs a surprising amount of protection and perks into the fine print:

  • No foreign transaction fees: Gone as of September 20, 2026 (it used to be 3%)
  • Trip cancellation/interruption insurance: Up to $1,500 per person, $6,000 per trip
  • Auto rental collision damage waiver: Up to $60,000; secondary in the U.S. (primary if you have no other auto insurance), primary abroad
  • Purchase protection: 120 days against damage or theft, up to $500 per item
  • Extended warranty: Adds 1 year to eligible U.S. manufacturer warranties of 3 years or less
  • Travel and emergency assistance: Legal and medical referrals when you're away from home (you pay for any services)
  • DoorDash DashPass: 6 months complimentary when you activate by Dec 31, 2027, then it auto-renews at the regular monthly rate

Let's be real — dropping the foreign transaction fee is the big win. On $2,000 of spending abroad, that's $60 you no longer hand over, on a card that costs nothing to hold. The catch: cell phone protection was discontinued on September 20, 2026, so pay your phone bill with a card that still covers it.

The Flex and Discover it are basically rivals who keep one-upping each other. Discover's first-year cashback match is genuinely hard to beat for new applicants — it's like getting a doubled welcome bonus. But long-term? The Flex wins thanks to the Chase ecosystem and its fixed 3% on dining and drugstores. If you're playing the long game, pick the Flex. If you want a wild first year, go Discover.

sections.title: Best For
sections.content:
• Category nerds who actually enjoy activating quarterly 5% bonuses (you know who you are)
  • Chase ecosystem builders feeding Ultimate Rewards points into a Sapphire card
  • Budget travelers who want a no-fee card that skips foreign transaction fees abroad
  • Grocery shoppers and diners looking to cash in big during Q4 2026, when grocery stores and dining both earn 5%
  • Two-card tacticians — the Flex + Freedom Unlimited combo covers rotating categories and flat-rate earning with zero annual fees

Skip this card if: you can't be bothered to activate categories every quarter (get the Unlimited instead), you need cell phone protection (it ended September 20, 2026), or you just want one simple card for everything.

title: American Express Business Gold Card
scouts_verdict:
The Business Gold is a workhorse card for businesses that spend where it counts — advertising, software, transit, and the like. That automatic 4X on your top two categories sounds almost too clever, and honestly, it usually delivers. The catch? If your spending is scattered thinly across all six eligible categories, the 4X boost might land on amounts that don't matter much. Concentrated spending is where this card flexes.

Now, about that $375 annual fee. It looks intimidating until you stack up the credits: $240 from Grubhub/office supplies (FedEx too, but only through October 1, 2026), $300 for ChatGPT Business, $155 from Walmart+, and $150 for Squarespace adds up to $845 — more than double the fee. But — and this is important — only count credits for services you'd actually use. Signing up for Walmart+ just to offset a credit card fee is the financial equivalent of buying something on sale you never wanted. The welcome offer (as high as 200,000 points) is excellent, though spending $15,000 in 3 months means this is truly a card for businesses with real expenses, not a side hustle.

The question that matters: Business Gold or Chase Ink Business Preferred? The Ink costs $95/year with 3X earning. The Amex costs $375 with 4X. If your business charges $50K+ annually in those bonus categories, the extra points from the Amex more than cover the fee difference. Below that threshold? The Ink Preferred and its Chase ecosystem might be the sharper play.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
If your business spends real money on ads, software, or transit, the American Express Business Gold Card basically reads your mind. It's a charge card that earns 4X Membership Rewards points on the two categories where your business spends the most each billing cycle, automatically picked from six eligible categories. No picking, no activating — it just watches what you buy and gives you the best deal it can.

At $375/year, it sits in the sweet spot between Amex's free business cards and the premium Business Platinum. You also get 3X on flights and prepaid hotels through amextravel.com, plus a pile of statement credits that can shave the annual fee down to almost nothing — if you're the type of business that buys office supplies and orders lunch.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• 4X Membership Rewards points on your top 2 spending categories each billing cycle from 6 eligible categories (up to $150,000/year in combined purchases, then 1X)
  • 3X points on flights and prepaid hotels booked on amextravel.com
  • 1X points on all other eligible purchases
  • $240/year in statement credits — up to $20/month for U.S. purchases at FedEx (through 10/1/2026), Grubhub, and office supply stores (enrollment required)
  • $300 ChatGPT Business credit — up to $300 per calendar year on U.S. ChatGPT Business subscription purchases (enrollment required)
  • Walmart+ membership credit — monthly statement credit worth up to $155/year
  • $150 Squarespace credit — up to $150 per calendar year for eligible U.S. purchases with Squarespace (enrollment required)
  • Flexible payment: Pay Over Time feature lets you carry a balance on eligible purchases (with interest)
  • Expense management tools including Year-End Summary, Connect to QuickBooks, and employee card spending limits
  • No preset spending limit — adapts to your purchasing patterns

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:
Annual Fee: $375

Employee Cards: $95 for the first five cards, then $95 for each additional card (no-fee Employee Business Expense Cards are also available)

Foreign Transaction Fee: None

Late Payment Fee: $39 or 2.99% of any past due Pay In Full amount, whichever is greater

Pay Over Time APR: 17.99%–28.74% variable

$375 sounds like a lot — until you do the math on the credits:

  • Grubhub/office supply credit (FedEx too, through 10/1/2026): up to $240/year
  • Walmart+ credit: up to $155/year
  • ChatGPT Business credit: up to $300/year
  • Squarespace credit: up to $150/year

That's up to $845 in credits, which technically more than covers the annual fee. The key word is "technically" — you have to actually use these services. If you're forcing yourself to order Grubhub just to chase a $20 credit, you're doing it wrong.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
Earn as high as 200,000 Membership Rewards points after you spend $15,000 on eligible purchases with the Business Gold Card within the first 3 months of Card Membership. Offers vary — Amex shows your personalized number after you apply, and you may not be eligible if you have or have had this card.

Let's be honest about that $15,000 spend requirement — it's hefty. That's $5,000/month, which means this card is calling out to businesses with real operating expenses, not someone trying to manufacture spend on gift cards. But if your business naturally drops $5K+/month on advertising, supplies, or SaaS subscriptions, you'll barely notice.

At conservative valuations (1.5–2 cents per point), the full 200,000 MR points are worth $3,000–$4,000 in travel. Transfer them to partners like ANA or Singapore Airlines and you can stretch that even further — business class to Tokyo, anyone?

sections.title: Earning Rates
sections.content:
The card automatically identifies your top 2 spending categories each billing cycle and applies 4X earning. No choosing, no fiddling — it just picks the two where you spent the most:

Eligible 4X CategoriesExamples
U.S. advertisingGoogle Ads, Meta Ads, LinkedIn Ads
U.S. computer hardware/software/cloudAWS, Microsoft, Adobe, Apple
U.S. gas stationsShell, ExxonMobil, BP
U.S. restaurantsAny restaurant purchase
TransitRideshare, taxis, trains, parking, tolls
U.S. wireless telephoneAT&T, Verizon, T-Mobile

Cap: 4X applies to the first $150,000 in combined 4X-eligible purchases per calendar year, then 1X. Additional earning: 3X on flights and prepaid hotels via amextravel.com, 1X on everything else.

The auto-selection is clever but not perfect. If your spending is spread thin across all six categories, the 4X boost might land on smaller amounts that don't really move the needle. Works best when your spending is concentrated in 2-3 categories.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
Membership Rewards points are one of the most flexible currencies in the game. Here's what you can do with them:

  • Transfer to airline partners: 16 airlines including Delta, ANA, Singapore Airlines, British Airways, Air France/KLM, JetBlue, Avianca LifeMiles, Emirates, and more (mostly 1:1; JetBlue and Emirates transfer at 5:4, Aeromexico at 1:1.6)
  • Transfer to hotel partners: Hilton Honors (1:2 ratio), Marriott Bonvoy (1:1 ratio, but less favorable), Choice Privileges (1:1) and Leading Hotels of the World (4:1)
  • Amex Travel portal: Book flights, hotels, and more at 1 cent per point (or 0.7 cpp for some redemptions)
  • Statement credits: Apply points against purchases (typically 0.6–0.7 cpp)
  • Gift cards: Variable rates, generally not the best value
  • Pay with Points at Amazon: 0.7 cpp — just don't

The money play is airline transfers, full stop. ANA first class to Japan for 72,500 points one-way from the West Coast (booked through Virgin Atlantic)? That's the kind of value that makes the annual fee look like pocket change. Singapore Airlines business class and Delta domestic awards during low-demand periods are other sweet spots worth hunting.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
Solid travel benefits here, though you won't mistake this for the Business Platinum:

  • No foreign transaction fees — good for international business spending
  • Car rental loss and damage insurance: Secondary coverage (no liability coverage)
  • Global Assist Hotline: 24/7 medical, legal, and travel emergency assistance
  • Trip delay insurance: Up to $300 per trip when a round-trip paid with the card is delayed 12+ hours (max 2 claims per 12 months)
  • Cell phone protection: Up to $800 per claim (2 claims per 12 months, $50 deductible) when you pay your wireless bill with the card
  • The Hotel Collection: $100 on-property credit plus a room upgrade when available on 2+ night stays booked through AmexTravel.com
  • Baggage insurance: Up to $1,250 for carry-on, $500 for checked bags
  • Extended warranty: Adds up to one additional year on eligible purchases
  • Purchase protection: Up to $1,000 per covered purchase (up to $50,000 per year) for 90 days after purchase

What you won't find here: no airport lounge access, no airline fee credit, no hotel status, no TSA PreCheck/Global Entry credit. If those are must-haves, you're looking at the Business Platinum — and an extra $520/year.

The elephant in the room is the Chase Ink Business Preferred: a 100K sign-up bonus (vs. up to 200K here), 3X earning (vs. 4X here), but only $95/year. That's $280 cheaper. The Amex wins on raw earning rate, but you need to actually use those statement credits to come out ahead on total value. For businesses dropping serious money in the 4X categories, the Amex earns more. For everyone else, the Ink Preferred might be the smarter pick.

sections.title: Best For
sections.content:

  • Amex Membership Rewards devotees who live for airline transfer sweet spots
  • Grubhub-ordering, office-supply-buying business owners who'd use those services anyway and can pocket $240/year in credits (FedEx counts only through October 1, 2026)
  • Walmart+ subscribers who'll gladly take $155/year in free membership
  • Businesses with shifting spending patterns — the auto-category selection adapts month to month

Skip this if: your monthly spend is low (that $15K bonus requirement is a signal this card wants volume), your spending is mostly international (most 4X categories are U.S.-only), or you need lounge access and premium travel perks baked in.

title: American Express Classic Green Card
scouts_verdict:
The Amex Green (now the Classic Green, closed to new applicants since July 2026) fills an interesting niche: it's a low-cost way to keep earning Amex Membership Rewards points, and the 3X on travel, transit, and dining covers a surprising amount of what most people spend money on. The $219 CLEAR+ credit is the swing factor that makes or breaks this card — use CLEAR and you're effectively getting paid $69/year to carry the card. That's hard to argue with.

Without CLEAR, though, the math tightens up considerably. You're paying $150/year for 3X earning and some basic protections, while the Chase Sapphire Preferred offers 3X dining (plus gas and streaming), 2X travel, a $100 hotel credit, and Chase's partner network for $95. Unless you specifically need the transit category or you're chasing ANA and Singapore Airlines transfers (which are genuinely excellent), the Sapphire Preferred is the more cost-effective play for most people.

Where the Green really sings is as a supporting player in a bigger Amex lineup. Pair it with the Gold for 4X dining and groceries, let the Green handle travel and transit, and you've got your bases covered. Or keep it as your sole MR card if your spending skews heavily toward transportation. Just don't expect lounges, hotel status, or anything resembling luxury — that's Platinum territory, and Platinum money. And if you don't already have the Green, the only way in now is a product change from the Gold or Platinum — no welcome bonus attached.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Think of the American Express Classic Green Card (you probably know it as the Amex Green) as the budget-friendly travel card of the Amex Membership Rewards family — without the premium price tag. For $150/year, you get 3X points on travel, transit, and restaurants worldwide, which is a lot of everyday spending covered at a solid rate. It sits below the Gold ($325) and Platinum ($895) in both cost and perks, and that's exactly the point.

Amex relaunched this card in 2019 after it spent years collecting dust as a forgotten product, and the new identity is clear: it's a streamlined travel-and-dining earner for people who want MR transfer partners without selling a kidney. It won't dazzle you with dining credits or grocery bonuses like the Gold, but its travel and transit earning combined with a CLEAR+ credit make it surprisingly competitive for commuters and frequent flyers.

Heads up: Amex stopped taking new applications for the Green on July 23, 2026, and on August 20, 2026 renamed it the American Express Classic Green Card. Existing cardholders can keep using it, and Gold or Platinum cardmembers can still product-change into it — but there's no way to apply for it fresh right now.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• 3X Membership Rewards points on travel worldwide (flights, hotels, car rentals, home shares)
  • 3X points on transit worldwide (taxis, rideshares, trains, buses, tolls, parking)
  • 3X points on restaurants worldwide (including takeout and delivery in the U.S.)
  • 1X points on all other eligible purchases
  • $219 CLEAR+ Credit: Annual statement credit covering a CLEAR+ membership for expedited airport security
  • No foreign transaction fees
  • Car rental loss and damage insurance
  • Global Assist Hotline for travel emergencies
  • Baggage insurance plan covering lost, damaged, or stolen luggage

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:
Annual Fee: $150

Additional Card Members: No annual fee

Foreign Transaction Fee: None

Late Payment Fee: Up to $40

Pay Over Time APR: Prime Rate + 12.74% to Prime Rate + 21.74% variable (capped at 29.99%)

Here's the fun math: the $219 CLEAR+ credit literally exceeds the $150 annual fee. If you use CLEAR, this card pays you $69/year to hold it. That's rare. But — and this is a big but — CLEAR is only useful if you fly through airports that support it. If CLEAR isn't your thing, you're evaluating this card purely on its 3X earning structure against $150, which is a tighter call.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
Note: This card is no longer accepting new applications. Amex pulled the Green from new applicants on July 23, 2026, so there's no welcome bonus to chase. The only way in now is a product change from the Amex Gold or Platinum, and that doesn't come with a bonus.

Before it closed, the public offer was 40,000 Membership Rewards points after you spent $3,000 on purchases in the first 6 months of Card Membership.

Six months to spend $3,000 was about as relaxed as welcome bonus requirements get — that's $500/month. The 40,000 points was on the modest side, though; the card peaked at 60,000 points during past promotions. If you want a fresh MR welcome bonus today, look at the Amex Gold or Amex Platinum instead.

At 1.5–2 cents per point, those 40,000 MR points were worth roughly $600–$800 toward travel. Send them to the right partner (ANA or Virgin Atlantic, for example) and you can squeeze out even more.

sections.content:

All 3X earning is uncapped — no limits, no quarterly activations, no nonsense. The transit category is where this card quietly shines. It covers rideshares (Uber, Lyft), subway systems, commuter rail, parking garages, tolls, and even ferries. If you're commuting in a major city, your daily spend is racking up points on autopilot.

Compared to the Amex Gold (4X on dining, 4X on groceries), the Green earns less on food but more on travel and transit. If your wallet leans toward transportation rather than takeout, the Green is your card.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
You get the full Amex Membership Rewards transfer partner network — the same partners whether you hold the Green, Gold, or Platinum:

  • Airline transfers (1:1): Delta, ANA, Singapore Airlines, British Airways, Air France/KLM, Air Canada Aeroplan, Avianca LifeMiles, Virgin Atlantic, and more (JetBlue, Emirates and Cathay Pacific transfer at 5:4)
  • Hotel transfers: Hilton Honors (1:2 ratio), Marriott Bonvoy and Choice Privileges (1:1), and Leading Hotels of the World (4:1)
  • Amex Travel: Book flights at 1 cpp through the portal (most hotels get just 0.7 cpp)
  • Statement credits: Just 0.6 cpp (not recommended)
  • Gift cards and merchandise: Variable rates, typically poor value

The real value is in airline transfers — always. Sweet spots include ANA round-trip business class to Japan from 100,000 points, Virgin Atlantic partner awards on ANA or Delta, and Avianca LifeMiles for Star Alliance flights. Having access to this network for just $150/year is genuinely a great deal.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
Practical perks, nothing flashy — which is fine at this price:

  • $219 CLEAR+ Credit: Covers a CLEAR+ membership for expedited identity verification at airport security and select stadiums/venues. Automatically triggered when you charge CLEAR to the card.
  • No foreign transaction fees: Use freely abroad without surcharges
  • Car rental loss and damage insurance: Secondary coverage for collision damage or theft on eligible rentals
  • Baggage insurance: Up to $1,250 for carry-on, $500 for checked baggage
  • Trip delay insurance: Up to $300 per trip when a covered delay runs more than 12 hours on a round-trip paid with the card (max 2 claims per 12 months)
  • Global Assist Hotline: 24/7 emergency assistance when traveling 100+ miles from home

What you won't get: no airport lounge access (no Centurion Lounges, no Priority Pass), no airline fee credit, no hotel status, no TSA PreCheck/Global Entry credit. For any of that, you're upgrading to the Platinum — and its $895 fee.

  • CLEAR members who turn the $219 credit into a card that pays them $69/year

  • International travelers who want no foreign transaction fees and worldwide 3X earning

Not your card if: you don't already have the Green or an Amex Gold or Platinum to downgrade from (new applications are closed), you spend heavily on groceries (get the Gold), you want lounge access or premium perks (you need the Platinum), or the Sapphire Preferred's $95 fee just makes more sense for your wallet.

title: Capital One Savor
scouts_verdict:
The Savor is one of those rare cards that just makes sense for almost everyone. No annual fee, no foreign transaction fees, and 3% back on the stuff you're already spending money on — restaurants, groceries, entertainment, streaming. No quarterly activation dance, no caps, no fine print gotchas. Swipe and earn.

The one real gotcha: if Walmart or Target is your grocery store, you're earning a measly 1% instead of 3%, which kind of defeats the purpose. But if you shop at actual grocery chains — Kroger, Publix, Trader Joe's, Whole Foods, Safeway — the 3% is the real deal. And the entertainment and streaming categories are a nice bonus that most competitors simply don't match.

This isn't the card for points-and-miles nerds chasing business class flights — rewards are straight cash back with no transfer partner gymnastics. But honestly, that's a feature for people who just want money back without playing a game. If you need one set-it-and-forget-it card for everyday spending, the Savor is one of the best free options out there. Pair it with a flat 2% card like the Citi Double Cash for non-bonus spending, and you've got a two-card setup that quietly crushes it.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
If you spend most of your money on eating, watching stuff, and being entertained — and let's be honest, who doesn't? — the Capital One Savor Cash Rewards Credit Card was basically built for you. It earns 3% cash back on dining, groceries, entertainment, and streaming services, which covers a huge chunk of what most households actually spend money on. Everything else earns 1%. Oh, and it's free.

Quick backstory: the current Savor is actually the rebranded former SavorOne (Capital One stopped offering the original $95-a-year Savor card in July 2024, then swapped the names in October 2024). The earning structure stayed the same — straightforward and generous for a no-fee card. (Confusingly, the SavorOne name has since come back as a separate $39-a-year card for fair credit — this page is about the no-fee Savor.) If you want strong cash back on food and fun without managing rotating categories or coughing up an annual fee, this is one of the best options out there.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• 3% unlimited cash back on dining, including restaurants, takeout, and delivery
  • 3% unlimited cash back on grocery stores (excluding superstores like Walmart and Target)
  • 3% unlimited cash back on entertainment (movies, concerts, sporting events, amusement parks)
  • 3% unlimited cash back on popular streaming services (Netflix, Hulu, Disney+, etc.)
  • 5% cash back on hotels, vacation rentals and rental cars booked through Capital One Travel
  • 8% cash back on Capital One Entertainment purchases
  • 1% cash back on all other purchases
  • No annual fee
  • No foreign transaction fees
  • Rewards never expire for the life of the account

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:
Annual Fee: $0

Foreign Transaction Fee: None

Balance Transfer Fee: 3% of each balance transferred in your first 12 months; after that, 4% on transfers at a promotional APR Capital One may offer you

Cash Advance Fee: Either $10 or 3% of the amount, whichever is greater

Late Payment Fee: Up to $40

Zero annual fee and zero foreign transaction fees — that's a combination you don't see often enough. Unlike the Chase Freedom Unlimited (which hits you with 3% on every international purchase), the Savor works just fine in Paris or Tokyo. This is a genuinely no-cost card to own, full stop.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
Earn a $200 cash bonus after spending $500 on purchases within 3 months of opening your account. Fine print: you're not eligible if you've received a new-cardmember bonus on the Savor in the past 48 months, and the bonus is tied to the excellent-credit Savor — the Savor for Good Credit version earns the same rewards but has no bonus.

$500 in 3 months is roughly $167/month — you'll probably hit it by accident. The $200 back represents a 40% return on your initial spending, which is solid for a free card. It won't make your jaw drop compared to premium travel card bonuses, but remember: there's no annual fee clawing back that value. The $200 is yours, and the 3% keeps rolling indefinitely at zero cost.

If you buy all your groceries at Walmart or Target, you're earning 1%, not 3%. Standard grocery chains like Kroger, Publix, Safeway, and Trader Joe's all count for the 3% bonus.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
Redemption is refreshingly simple — what you earn is what you get:

  • Statement credit: Apply cash back directly against your balance (any amount)
  • Check: Get your cash back mailed to you as a check
  • Capital One Travel: Redeem for travel bookings at 1 cent per unit
  • Gift cards: Purchase from various retailers
  • Amazon checkout: Use rewards at Amazon.com
  • PayPal: Use rewards on eligible purchases when you check out with PayPal

No transfer partners of its own and no complicated redemption charts. (If you also carry a Capital One miles card like the Venture or Venture X, you can convert Savor cash back into Capital One miles and move them to airline and hotel partners.) One heads-up: Capital One says redemption rates vary and can change, so check what options like Amazon, PayPal and gift cards will get you before you redeem. Points-and-miles enthusiasts might yawn, but for everyone else, the simplicity is actually the feature. You don't need a spreadsheet to figure out what your rewards are worth.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
For a free card, you get a respectable set of extras — though don't expect anything fancy:

  • No foreign transaction fees: Use freely in any country without surcharges
  • 5% back on Capital One Travel: Hotels, vacation rentals and rental cars booked through the portal
  • 8% back on Capital One Entertainment: Concert tickets, events, and experiences purchased through Capital One's platform
  • Extended warranty: Additional warranty protection at no charge on eligible items you buy with the card (your Mastercard Guide to Benefits has the terms)
  • 24-hour travel assistance: An emergency replacement card and a cash advance if your card is lost or stolen
  • Travel accident insurance: Automatic coverage for a covered loss when you pay your fare with the card
  • Complimentary concierge: 24/7 help with dining, entertainment and travel plans

No lounge access, and don't count on premium travel insurance — any rental car or trip coverage comes through Mastercard and varies by card, so check your Guide to Benefits before you lean on it. The Savor is an everyday earning machine, not a travel fortress. If you need serious travel protections, pair it with a dedicated travel card.

Not your card if: you do all your grocery shopping at Walmart or Target (you'll earn 1%, not 3%), you want transferable points and miles, or you need premium travel protections.

title: Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant
scouts_verdict:
The Brilliant is a fantastic card — for a very specific person. If you're already loyal to Marriott and staying at their properties regularly, the value stacks up fast. Platinum Elite status is genuinely powerful at full-service Marriotts, Westins, and Sheratons where you'll score lounge access and meaningful upgrades. The 85K free night certificate can easily cover a $500+ night at a premium property. And the $300 dining credit? If you eat out even once a month, you'll use it without trying.

But let's talk about the elephant in the room: $650 is real money. If you're not disciplined about using the $25/month dining credit (use-it-or-lose-it, no rollover), and if you don't have a Ritz-Carlton or St. Regis stay planned for the property credit, you're leaving hundreds on the table. Too many people sign up for premium hotel cards thinking they'll "figure out" the credits later. Spoiler: they don't.

The bottom line: 15+ nights a year at Marriott properties plus consistent dining out? This card practically pays for itself. Under 10 nights? Save yourself $555 and grab the Boundless. And if you're on the fence, the 150K-point welcome bonus plus $250 statement credit (available through September 30, 2026) tilts the math heavily in favor of signing up now rather than later.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
The Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant American Express Card is the top dog in Marriott's credit card lineup, and it comes with a price tag to match: $650/year. This is the card for people who've basically pledged their loyalty to Marriott and want the VIP treatment without having to sleep in 50+ hotel rooms a year to earn it. Think automatic Platinum Elite status, Priority Pass lounge access, and a free night certificate that can cover a seriously nice property.

Here's the deal: this card is outstanding if you're a frequent Marriott traveler who'll actually use all the credits. The dining credit, the property credit, the lounge access, the elite status perks — they add up fast when you put them to work. But if you're the type who gets a premium card and then forgets to use the benefits? That $650 will feel like a very expensive paperweight.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• Automatic Platinum Elite Status — Includes room upgrades when available, late checkout, lounge access at select brands, 50% bonus points on stays, and welcome gifts.
  • Free Night Award (up to 85,000 points) — Received annually after card renewal. Can be used at properties costing up to 85K points per night, covering most Marriott hotels.
  • 25 Elite Night Credits — Applied annually toward earning or maintaining higher Marriott elite status tiers.
  • Priority Pass Select Membership — Unlimited airport lounge access for you and up to 2 guests at 1,300+ lounges worldwide.
  • $300 Annual Dining Credit — Up to $25/month in statement credits at restaurants worldwide.
  • $100 Marriott Property Credit — Up to $100 toward qualifying charges on 2+ night stays at Ritz-Carlton or St. Regis properties booked direct at an eligible special rate.
  • Global Entry or TSA PreCheck Credit — Statement credit of up to $85 for TSA PreCheck or $120 for Global Entry every 4 years.
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees — Use the card internationally without extra charges.

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:
Annual Fee: $650

Foreign Transaction Fees: None

Effective Net Cost: When you factor in the free night award (worth ~$400-$600 at many properties), $300 dining credit, $100 property credit, and the value of Platinum Elite status, many cardholders can offset most or all of the annual fee. However, you need to actually use these benefits to get the value — unused credits are worth nothing.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
Earn 150,000 Marriott Bonvoy points plus a $250 statement credit after spending $6,000 on eligible purchases within the first 6 months of card membership. This limited-time offer is available through September 30, 2026.

A hundred and fifty thousand points. At roughly 0.7 cents per point, that's approximately $1,050 in hotel stays (about $1,300 once you add the $250 credit) — enough for multiple free nights at mid-tier properties or a couple of memorable nights at luxury Marriott brands. This is one of the strongest welcome offers in the hotel card world right now, and the $6,000 spend over 6 months ($1,000/month) is reasonable for a premium card.

Here's a detail that makes this even better at Marriott hotels: your earning rate stacks with elite status bonuses. As a Platinum Elite member, you get a 50% bonus on top of base earnings, which pushes your effective hotel earning rate even higher. It's like getting interest on your interest.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
Marriott Bonvoy points give you options — some great, some you should avoid:

  • Free Night Awards — Book stays at 10,000+ Marriott properties worldwide. Redemption rates vary by property and date (dynamic pricing).
  • Points + Cash — Combine points with a cash co-pay for nights when you don't have quite enough points.
  • Airline Transfers — Transfer points to 38 airline partners, mostly at a 3:1 ratio (60,000 Bonvoy = 20,000 airline miles). Transfer 60,000 points at a time to receive a 5,000-mile bonus with most partners (so 60,000 points become 25,000 miles — effectively 2.4:1). United MileagePlus gets a 10,000-mile bonus per 60,000 points.
  • Marriott Bonvoy Moments — Bid on or book unique experiences like concerts, sporting events, and culinary experiences.
  • Gift Cards & Merchandise — Available but generally poor value. Stick with hotel redemptions or airline transfers.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• $300 Dining Credit: Up to $25/month in automatic statement credits when you dine at restaurants worldwide. This resets each calendar year.
  • $100 Property Credit: Receive up to a $100 credit for qualifying charges on stays of 2+ nights at The Ritz-Carlton or St. Regis properties when you book direct with Marriott at the eligible special rate.
  • Priority Pass Select: Complimentary membership with access to 1,300+ airport lounges worldwide for you and up to 2 guests.
  • Global Entry/TSA PreCheck: Up to $85 for TSA PreCheck or $120 for Global Entry every 4 years for the application fee.
  • Marriott Platinum Elite Benefits on Property: Room upgrades (including suites when available), late checkout until 4 PM, executive lounge access at participating brands like Marriott, JW Marriott, Westin, and Sheraton (not Ritz-Carlton, St. Regis, or W), welcome gifts, and enhanced internet.

title: Marriott Bonvoy Boundless
scouts_verdict:
The Boundless is quietly one of the best deals in the hotel card game, and Chase's limited-time airline credit (up to $100, through 2026 for existing cardholders and mid-2027 for new ones) makes it even better right now. At $95/year, you get a free night certificate worth $150-$250+ at most Marriott properties, plus that airline credit effectively zeroes out the fee while it lasts. A hotel card that pays for itself before you earn a single point? That's the definition of a keeper card.

The earning structure is solid if unspectacular — 6x at Marriott, 3x on groceries/gas/dining with a $6,000 combined cap. Heavy spenders will hit that ceiling, but for most people it's fine. The real play here is simple: hold the card, collect your free night every year, use the airline credit while it's around, and treat any points you earn along the way as a bonus. It's low-maintenance value.

Deciding between this and the Brilliant? Ask yourself one question: do you stay at Marriott properties often enough to justify $555 more per year? If you're under 15 nights annually, the Boundless gives you the vast majority of the value at a fraction of the cost. And that 3 Free Night welcome bonus (each night worth up to 50K points) is genuinely outstanding — time a sign-up right and your first $3,000 of spending could bank you a long weekend's worth of hotel stays.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
The Marriott Bonvoy Boundless Credit Card from Chase is the Goldilocks option in Marriott's card lineup — not too expensive, not too basic, just right for most Marriott travelers. At $95/year, it sits between the free Bold card and the premium $650 Brilliant from Amex, giving you a free night certificate, Silver Elite status, and solid earning rates without requiring you to remortgage your house.

Here's why this card keeps winning fans: you get a free night certificate every year that's typically worth $150-$250+, which more than covers the annual fee before you even start counting bonus points. It earns Marriott Bonvoy points directly (not Chase Ultimate Rewards), making it a straightforward hotel loyalty card that does exactly what it says on the tin.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• Free Night Award — Received each account anniversary, redeemable at properties costing up to 35,000 points per night. It expires 12 months after it's issued, and Marriott lets you add up to 25,000 points on top to stretch it to a pricier hotel.
  • Automatic Silver Elite Status — Includes 10% bonus points on stays, priority late checkout, and free Wi-Fi.
  • 15 Elite Night Credits — Applied annually toward earning Gold or Platinum status, plus 1 more night credit for every $5,000 you spend on the card.
  • Path to Gold Elite — Spend $35,000 on the card in a calendar year and Gold Elite status is yours, no hotel nights required.
  • Up to $100 Airline Credit (limited-time offer) — A $50 statement credit once you spend $250+ directly with airlines in each of two half-year windows: Jan-Jun and Jul-Dec 2026 for cardmembers who had the card by 1/7/2026 (one-time activation required), or Jun 4-Dec 2026 and then Jan-Jun 2027 for new cardmembers who apply between 6/4/2026 and 12/31/2026. It's a promo, not a permanent perk.
  • Complimentary DashPass — 12 months of DashPass for DoorDash and Caviar when you activate by 12/31/2027, then it auto-renews at the monthly rate unless you cancel. While enrolled, you also get $10 off one non-restaurant DoorDash order each quarter through 12/31/2027.
  • Instacart+ and a $10 Monthly Credit — 3 months of complimentary Instacart+ when you enroll the card, plus a $10 Instacart credit each month you keep Instacart+ active, through 12/31/2027. Unused credit doesn't roll over, and Instacart+ auto-renews at $99/year after the free months unless you cancel.
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees — Use the card abroad without additional charges.
  • 5th Night Free on Award Stays — Redeem points for 5 consecutive nights and you only pay for 4 (a Marriott Bonvoy perk every member gets, card or not).

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:
Annual Fee: $95

Foreign Transaction Fees: None

Effective Net Cost: Let's do the math: a free night certificate worth $150-$250+ at most Marriott properties, plus up to $100 in airline credits while Chase's limited-time offer runs (through 2026 for existing cardmembers, mid-2027 for new ones). That's $250-$350+ in tangible value against a $95 fee while the promo lasts, and the free night alone still covers the fee after it ends. This card can be net positive before you even earn a single point. In the hotel card world, that kind of math is rare — and it makes the Boundless one of the easiest keeper cards to justify.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
Earn 3 Free Night Awards after spending $3,000 on eligible purchases within the first 3 months of account opening.

Each one is valid at properties costing up to 50,000 points per night and expires 12 months after it's issued. At mid-range Marriott hotels, that can easily represent $750-$1,100+ in hotel value. Here's the thing about free night certificates: they work on high-demand dates when cash rates are inflated, which means they're often worth more than you'd expect. Time this right and you could fund an entire long-weekend getaway.

Mind Marriott's eligibility rules, though: the card isn't available to you if you currently have the Boundless, the Bold or an older Chase Marriott Premier or Premier Plus card (or earned a new cardmember bonus on one in the last 24 months), and recent Amex Marriott cards can block the bonus — having the Marriott Bonvoy American Express Card now or in the last 30 days, approval for a Brilliant, Bevy or Marriott Business Amex in the last 90 days, or a new cardmember or upgrade bonus on one in the last 24 months, knocks you out.

While it runs, it effectively covers the entire annual fee.

  • 15 Elite Night Credits: Head start toward Gold Elite (requires 25 nights) or Platinum Elite (requires 50 nights), and you earn 1 more night credit for every $5,000 you spend. Big spenders can skip the night counting entirely: $35,000 in purchases in a calendar year earns Gold Elite outright.

Use it or lose it (no rollover), and Instacart+ bills $99/year once the free months end unless you cancel. Great if you already order groceries; a trap if you forget.
