Skip this if: you barely travel (the Bold at $0 is better for occasional Marriott visits), you want Platinum status and premium perks (upgrade to the Brilliant), or you'd rather earn transferable points than hotel-specific currency.

title: Marriott Bonvoy Bold
scouts_verdict:
Nobody is going to brag about the Marriott Bonvoy Bold at a dinner party. It's not that kind of card. It's the kind of card you toss in your wallet because it costs nothing and quietly gives you something back — Silver Elite status, a handful of night credits, 2x on groceries and streaming, and a free DashPass. Modest? Sure. But free is a powerful price.

The refreshed 2x categories (rideshare, food delivery, streaming, phone bills) make it more useful day-to-day than the old version, but that 1x base rate means you should only reach for this card in bonus categories and at Marriott hotels. For everything else, a 2% cash back card will serve you better.

Here's who should actually get the Bold: someone who stays at Marriott a few times a year, wants to passively accumulate points, and would rather not think about annual fees. Just don't count on it as a sidekick to a premium Marriott card: Chase won't approve the Bold while you hold a Boundless, and the Brilliant already earns at least 2x on everything, so the Bold's bonus categories add nothing (and its 5 night credits won't stack on top of the Brilliant's). The 45K welcome bonus is modest, but with only $1,000 to spend, it's basically a free $300 hotel weekend for minimal effort.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Let's be real: the Marriott Bonvoy Bold Credit Card from Chase isn't going to make anyone's heart race. It's the entry-level Marriott card, and its biggest selling point is dead simple — it's free. No annual fee, no drama. It's for people who stay at Marriott a few times a year and want to accumulate some points without paying for the privilege.

It doesn't have the free night certificate of the Boundless or the Platinum Elite status of the Brilliant. What it does have is automatic Silver Elite status, a surprisingly broad set of 2x earning categories (refreshed in 2024-2025 to include rideshare, streaming, and food delivery), and a complimentary DashPass membership. Think of it less as a credit card to get excited about and more as a smart, zero-cost tool to keep in your wallet.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• $0 Annual Fee — No cost to hold the card, making it risk-free for occasional Marriott travelers.
  • Automatic Silver Elite Status — Includes 10% bonus points on stays, priority late checkout, and free in-room Wi-Fi.
  • 5 Elite Night Credits — Applied annually toward earning higher Marriott elite tiers.
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees — Use the card internationally without surcharges.
  • Complimentary DashPass (12 months) — Free DashPass membership for DoorDash and Caviar when activated (available through 12/31/2027), providing $0 delivery fees on eligible orders.
  • Points Redemption for Travel Credit — Redeem Bonvoy points as statement credits for qualifying airline or Marriott hotel purchases, up to $750/year.

Annual Fee: $0

Foreign Transaction Fees: None

Effective Net Cost: Zero. Zilch. Nada. No annual fee means every single point you earn is pure gravy. You won't get a free night certificate like the Boundless or Brilliant, but you also won't pay a cent to hold this card. It's an excellent "sock drawer" card for maintaining Silver Elite status at zero cost.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
Earn 45,000 Marriott Bonvoy points after spending $1,000 on eligible purchases within the first 3 months of account opening.

Fine print: Chase won't approve the card if you currently have a Boundless or Bold (or one of the old Chase Marriott Premier cards), or if you earned a new-cardmember bonus on one in the past 24 months. Amex Marriott cards count too — you won't get this bonus if you were approved for a Brilliant, Bevy or Marriott Business Amex in the last 90 days, earned a new-cardmember or upgrade bonus on one in the last 24 months, or have had the old no-fee Marriott Bonvoy Amex in the last 30 days. Chase's unpublished 5/24 rule is also reported to apply.

Let's not sugarcoat it — 45,000 points isn't going to get you a suite at the St. Regis. But with Marriott's dynamic pricing, it's enough for a couple of nights at a lower-priced Marriott (think Courtyard, Fairfield, Four Points). At a typical valuation of 0.7 cents per point, that's roughly $315 in hotel value. For a free card with a $1,000 spend requirement, that's essentially a free hotel weekend for doing your normal shopping.

Not your card if: you stay at Marriott frequently (the Boundless is absolutely worth the $95 upgrade for the free night alone), you want high earning rates across all spending, or you're trying to fast-track to elite status (5 night credits is a crawl when you need 25 for Gold).

title: Wells Fargo Active Cash
scouts_verdict:
The Active Cash is the answer to the question: "What if a credit card just... worked?" Two percent back on everything, no annual fee, no categories to remember, no quarterly activation rituals. In a world full of cards trying to be clever, this one is content to be straightforward — and it's better for it.

What pushes it past other flat-rate cards is the stuff you don't expect at $0/year. Cell phone protection covering up to $600 per claim? Its closest 2% rival, the Citi Double Cash, doesn't offer that at all. Visa Signature perks like the Luxury Hotel Collection and 24/7 concierge are genuine bonuses, not the kind of filler benefits that sound nice on paper but mean nothing in practice. And if you pair this with a Wells Fargo Autograph, you unlock transfer partners — turning a simple cash back card into part of a real points strategy.

The only real weakness: that 3% foreign transaction fee means this card needs to stay home when you fly overseas. But for everything domestic — groceries, gas, bills, subscriptions, the random impulse buy at 11 PM — this is as good as it gets for free. It's not exciting, and that's exactly why it works.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Some cards try to impress you with complicated category structures and rotating bonuses. The Wells Fargo Active Cash Card takes the opposite approach: 2% cash back on everything, no annual fee, end of story. No categories to track, no bonuses to activate, no spending caps. Just a flat, unlimited 2% on every single purchase you make. It's the sweatpants of credit cards — not flashy, but comfortable and effective.

Since its launch, the Active Cash has been a top-tier pick for anyone who values simplicity. And in 2026, it still holds up as one of the best flat-rate cash back cards in the U.S., backed by Visa Signature benefits that include some surprisingly premium perks for a free card.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• Unlimited 2% cash rewards on all purchases — no categories, no caps
  • $0 annual fee — free to hold indefinitely
  • 0% intro APR for 12 months from account opening on purchases and qualifying balance transfers (requested within 120 days)
  • Cell phone protection — up to $600 per claim ($25 deductible) when you pay your phone bill with the card; covers theft and damage, up to 2 claims per 12 months
  • Visa Signature Concierge — 24/7 concierge for dining, travel, and event bookings
  • Visa Signature Luxury Hotel Collection — room upgrades, free Wi-Fi, complimentary breakfast, and late checkout at select hotels
  • No expiring rewards — cash rewards stay as long as the account is open
  • Roadside dispatch via Visa Signature (pay-per-use)

Free to hold, simple to use. The only blemish is the 3% foreign transaction fee — which means this card should stay in your domestic lineup. International trips call for a different card.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
Earn a $100 cash rewards bonus after spending $500 in purchases within the first 3 months of account opening.

$500 in 3 months is practically a participation trophy — most people will hit this through normal grocery and gas spending without even trying. The $100 bonus is on the small side (down from the long-running $200), but it's straightforward, just like the card itself. One catch: you may not get the bonus if you currently have an Active Cash or opened one in the last 48 months, even if that account is now closed.

That's the whole table. One line. One rate. Every dollar earns 2% back — at the grocery store, at the gas pump, on your electric bill, at that overpriced coffee shop you keep going to. No quarterly activations, no caps, no thinking. This simplicity is the card's entire identity, and it does it perfectly.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
Cash rewards redemption is straightforward:

  • Statement credit — apply rewards against your balance
  • Direct deposit — deposit rewards into a Wells Fargo account
  • Gift cards — redeem for select retailer gift cards
  • ATM withdrawal — withdraw rewards as cash at Wells Fargo ATMs

Pro tip that most people miss: if you also hold a Wells Fargo Autograph or Autograph Journey card, you can pool your rewards and access transfer partners for potentially higher value. Suddenly that boring 2% cash back card becomes part of a transferable points strategy.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
No travel credits or lounge access here — but the Visa Signature perks are better than you'd expect on a free card:

  • Visa Signature Luxury Hotel Collection — automatic room upgrades (when available), complimentary breakfast, late checkout, and food/beverage credits at participating hotels
  • Visa Signature Concierge — 24/7 service for travel bookings, restaurant reservations, and event tickets
  • Roadside dispatch — pay-per-use service available through Visa
  • Auto rental collision damage waiver — secondary in the U.S. and primary abroad, up to $50,000, when you pay for the whole rental with the card and decline the rental company's coverage

That said, the 3% foreign transaction fee is a non-starter for international travel. Keep this card in the domestic rotation and bring something else abroad.

The Double Cash counters with access to Citi ThankYou transfer partners and a bigger welcome bonus ($200 vs. $100). Both are excellent; the Active Cash edges ahead on raw perks, the Double Cash on points flexibility.

sections.title: Best For

• Simplicity lovers who want top-tier flat-rate cash back without an annual fee or any mental overhead
  • Category-tracking haters — one rate on everything, every day, no exceptions

  • Phone bill payers — the cell phone protection can save you hundreds per year on carrier insurance

Not your card if: you travel internationally (3% FTF is a dealbreaker) or you want premium perks like lounge access and travel credits.

title: Wells Fargo Autograph
scouts_verdict:
The Wells Fargo Autograph is quietly one of the best no-annual-fee cards you can get, and it flies under the radar compared to flashier options. Six categories at 3x, no foreign transaction fees, and direct access to transfer partners — all for $0/year. Most cards offering this kind of flexibility charge $95 to $250 annually. The Autograph just hands it over and doesn't ask for anything back.

The transfer partners are the headline act. British Airways, Virgin Atlantic, Air France/KLM, JetBlue — all at 1:1 ratios with no minimums. A well-timed transfer to British Airways for a short-haul award or Virgin Atlantic for a premium cabin seat can easily get you 1.5 to 2+ cents per point. And unlike the Chase Freedom Flex, you don't need a $95-to-$795 Sapphire card lurking in the background to make transfers happen.

The ultimate move? Pair the Autograph with the Active Cash. Use the Autograph for its 3x categories, the Active Cash for everything else at 2%, pool the points, and transfer to partners. Boom — you have a powerhouse rewards system with a combined annual fee of exactly zero dollars. Try to beat that.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Here's a card that punches way above its weight class: the Wells Fargo Autograph Card earns 3x points across six spending categories — restaurants, travel, gas stations and EV charging, transit, streaming services, and phone plans — plus 1x on everything else. And the kicker? No annual fee. Oh, and it comes with transfer partners. For free. That's the kind of combination that used to require a $95+ annual fee card.

It's no surprise this was named The Points Guy's No-Annual-Fee Card of the Year for 2026. The Autograph has become a go-to for rewards enthusiasts who want category bonuses and the ability to transfer to airlines and hotels — without paying for the privilege. It's the card that made people realize you don't always have to spend money to earn points the smart way.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• 3x points per dollar on restaurants, travel, gas, EV charging, transit, streaming, and phone plans
  • 1x points per dollar on all other purchases
  • $0 annual fee
  • No foreign transaction fees — great for international travel
  • Airline and hotel transfer partners — 10 partners with 1:1 transfer ratios (except Choice Hotels and Wyndham at 1:2)
  • Cell phone protection — up to $600 per claim ($25 deductible) when paying your phone bill with the card
  • 0% intro APR for 12 months on purchases
  • No minimum transfer amount — transfer as few as 1 point to partners

Read that fee column again: $0 annual fee and $0 foreign transaction fees. You can carry this card internationally, use it every day at home, and it never costs you a dime. That's a rare double-zero that even some $95/year cards can't match.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
Earn 20,000 bonus points after spending $1,000 in purchases in the first 3 months of account opening. That's worth $200 in cash redemption value — or potentially more when transferred to airline partners.

$1,000 in 3 months is manageable for just about anyone with normal spending habits. And while $200 isn't a jaw-dropping bonus, remember: you're not paying an annual fee, so every cent of that bonus is pure profit.

Restaurants, gas, travel, transit, streaming, phone plans — that's literally where most people spend most of their money. You don't have to change your habits to earn well with this card; your habits are already the bonus categories.

sections.title: Redemption Options

This is where the Autograph gets really interesting for a free card:

  • Book travel through the Wells Fargo rewards portal at 1 cent per point
  • Statement credits applied to your balance

Transferring to partners is the power move. British Airways short-haul awards, Virgin Atlantic premium cabin seats, Air France/KLM deals — these can easily yield 1.5 to 2+ cents per point. Most cards with transfer partner access charge you $95-$250/year for the privilege. This one? Free.

The transfer partner list keeps expanding, and with 1:1 ratios and no minimum transfer amounts, the flexibility here is real. You're getting the kind of redemption power that used to be reserved for premium cardholders.

title: Discover it Cash Back
scouts_verdict:
The Discover it Cash Back is the most underrated card in America. In an era of flashy travel cards with $795-$895 annual fees, a free card that effectively gives you 10% cash back in bonus categories for an entire year is borderline absurd. The Cashback Match is the single best first-year offer in the credit card industry — automatic, unlimited, and no-strings-attached. Nobody else is doing this. Nobody.

After year one, the card settles into a reliable 5%-on-rotating-categories, 1%-on-everything-else rhythm. That's good but not dominant. The real strategy is pairing it correctly: use the Discover for 5% categories, a flat 2% card for everything else, and you've built a no-fee reward system that rivals cards with annual fees. The quarterly activation takes 30 seconds and is only mildly annoying.

The knock on Discover is the network. Domestically you're fine — most merchants take it. Internationally and at some smaller businesses, you'll occasionally get turned away. Never carry this as your only card. But as part of a multi-card strategy, especially in your first year, the Discover it Cash Back is almost impossible to outvalue on pure math. Get it, maximize year one, and keep it forever.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
The Discover it Cash Back has a party trick that no other card can match: Cashback Match. Discover literally doubles every cent of cash back you earn in your entire first year — no caps, no catches, no fine print gotchas. That means the 5% rotating quarterly categories effectively become 10%, and the base 1% becomes 2%. For 12 full months. It's the kind of offer that makes you wonder what Discover knows that other issuers don't.

Beyond the first-year fireworks, this is a solid no-annual-fee card with rotating 5% bonus categories and 1% on everything else, running on the Discover network. That network is the one caveat — it's accepted at most U.S. merchants but notably weaker internationally. Still, as a domestic cash back card and especially as a first credit card, the Discover it is extremely hard to beat.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• 5% Cash Back on Rotating Categories — Earn 5% back on up to $1,500 in purchases per quarter in rotating bonus categories (activation required each quarter).
  • 1% Cash Back on Everything Else — Flat 1% on all non-bonus purchases.
  • Cashback Match (First Year) — Discover automatically matches ALL cash back earned at the end of your first year. Unlimited, no minimum, no sign-up required.
  • $0 Annual Fee — No annual fee, ever.
  • 0% Intro APR — 0% intro APR on purchases and balance transfers for 15 months (then 18.49%-28.49% variable).
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees — Unusual for a no-fee card, making it usable abroad.
  • Free FICO Score — Access your FICO credit score online.
  • Cash Back Never Expires — Rewards don't expire for the life of the account.

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:
Annual Fee: $0

Foreign Transaction Fees: None

Late Payment Fee: None the first time you pay late, then up to $41

Balance Transfer Fee: 3% intro fee for the first 15 months, then 5%

Effective Net Cost: Absolutely nothing. This card is free to own, and the rotating categories plus first-year match deliver genuine value without you spending a single dollar on fees. There's no reason not to keep this card open long-term — even if you only pull it out for bonus category quarters, it's earning money for you.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
The Discover it Cash Back doesn't do a traditional sign-up bonus — it does something better. The Cashback Match means Discover matches 100% of all cash back you earn during your entire first year.

Think of it as an unlimited, uncapped welcome bonus that grows with how much you use the card. Max out the 5% categories ($1,500/quarter x 4 = $6,000 at 5%) and spend moderately elsewhere, and a typical first-year haul is $300-$500 in cash back, doubled to $600-$1,000 after the match. No other no-annual-fee card comes anywhere close to that kind of first-year value. Not even in the same zip code.

2026 Rotating Categories:

  • Q1 (Jan-Mar): Grocery stores, wholesale clubs, select streaming services
  • Q2 (Apr-Jun): Restaurants and home improvement stores
  • Q3 (Jul-Sep): Gas stations and EV charging, public transit (including airlines), drugstores
  • Q4 (Oct-Dec): Utilities, restaurants, entertainment

Don't forget: You must activate the 5% categories each quarter through your Discover account. It doesn't apply retroactively, so any purchases you make before activation earn just 1%. Takes 30 seconds online — set a calendar reminder for the 1st of January, April, July, and October.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
Discover keeps things beautifully simple:

  • Statement Credits — Apply cash back as a credit to your account balance. Available in any amount.
  • Direct Deposit — Transfer cash back directly to your bank account.
  • Gift Cards — Redeem for gift cards from popular retailers, and select partner gift cards occasionally add 5% to 20% in value.
  • Amazon Checkout — Use cash back directly at Amazon.com at checkout (1:1 value).
  • PayPal — Use cash back to pay when you check out with PayPal at select merchants.
  • Charitable Donations — Donate cash back to select charities.

No transfer partners, no complicated redemption charts, no devaluation anxiety. Cash back is always worth face value — a dollar is a dollar. The gift card bonuses are a nice little kicker when a retailer you already shop at is on the partner list.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
Let's be honest — this is not a travel card, and it doesn't pretend to be. But it does have a couple of useful features for travelers:

  • No Foreign Transaction Fees: A rare perk for a no-annual-fee card. You can use it abroad without extra charges, though Discover network acceptance is limited outside the US.
  • Free FICO Score: Handy for monitoring credit health, especially if you're building toward a premium travel card application.

What's missing: No travel insurance, no rental car coverage (Discover dropped it back in 2018), no trip delay/cancellation coverage, no purchase protection, no lounge access. If travel perks matter, pair this with a dedicated travel card and use the Discover purely for cash back.

Not the card for: people who want a flat 2% on everything (get the Citi Double Cash or Wells Fargo Active Cash), frequent travelers who need travel protections, or anyone who'll forget to activate quarterly categories and lose out on 5%.

title: IHG One Rewards Premier
scouts_verdict:
Here's the bottom line: the IHG Premier is the most underrated hotel card on the market. Full stop. You're getting Platinum Elite status for $99 — the same tier competitors charge $550-$650 to hand out. Sure, IHG's Platinum isn't going to get you upgraded to a palace suite, but it's real status with real perks at a fraction of the price.

The earning structure is sneaky good, too. That 3x on everything means this card actually works as a daily driver, not just a hotel card you dust off for travel. Most hotel cards give you 1-2x on everyday spending, so 3x is doing real work. And at IHG properties, stacking bonuses push you to 26x per dollar — those points pile up fast on a multi-night stay.

Let's be honest about the downsides: IHG points are worth less per point than Marriott or Hyatt, and a Holiday Inn Express isn't exactly a Ritz-Carlton. But if you travel frequently, stay at IHG properties even once or twice a year, and want a card that over-delivers for under $100, the Premier is a no-brainer. The 140K welcome bonus alone covers up to 4 award nights at thousands of IHG hotels. For $99, that's kind of ridiculous.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Look, most hotel credit cards at the $99 price point give you a participation trophy and call it "status." The IHG One Rewards Premier Credit Card from Chase actually gives you Platinum Elite status — the real deal, with room upgrades, late checkout, and welcome amenities. For a card that costs less than dinner for two at a nice restaurant, that's kind of absurd.

IHG's portfolio spans over 6,000 properties across 100+ countries — we're talking InterContinental, Kimpton, Holiday Inn, Crowne Plaza, Hotel Indigo, and more. The card pairs that Platinum Elite status with an anniversary free night certificate, a 4th Night Free benefit on award stays, and earning rates that quietly embarrass cards costing three times as much. If you stay at IHG properties even occasionally, this card is punching way above its weight class.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• Automatic Platinum Elite Status — Room upgrades when available, welcome amenity, extended checkout, bonus points on stays, and complimentary internet. No qualifying nights required — just open the card.
  • Anniversary Free Night Award — Shows up every year after your card anniversary, good at properties costing up to 40,000 points per night. This alone can be worth more than the annual fee.
  • 4th Night Free on Award Stays — Redeeming points for 4+ consecutive nights? The 4th night is on the house. That's a built-in 25% discount on longer stays.
  • $50 United TravelBank Cash — Annual credit after registering your card with your MileagePlus account. Free money for flights.
  • Global Entry/TSA PreCheck Credit — Up to $120 every 4 years for the application fee. Skip the security line on IHG's dime.
  • Complimentary DashPass — 1-year membership for DoorDash/Caviar with $0 delivery fees on eligible orders.
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees — Use it worldwide without the surcharge tax.
  • $100 Statement Credit + 10K Bonus Points — Hit $20,000+ in spending in a calendar year and get rewarded for the loyalty.
  • Diamond Elite at $40K Spend — Put $40,000 on the card in a calendar year and you (the primary cardmember) get bumped to Diamond Elite through December 31 of the following year.
  • $10 Monthly Instacart Credit — Up to $120 a year while you keep an active Instacart+ membership, and the card throws in 3 months of Instacart+ free to start. Runs through 12/31/2027.

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs

Annual Fee: $99

The real math: The free night certificate alone (up to 40K points, worth $100-$200+ at most IHG properties) covers the annual fee. Toss in the $50 United TravelBank credit and Platinum Elite status, and you're looking at $200-$400+ in annual value for just $99. That's not marketing spin — the value-to-cost ratio here is genuinely one of the best in the hotel card space. It's almost hard to lose money on this card.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
Earn 140,000 IHG One Rewards bonus points after spending $3,000 on purchases in the first 3 months from account opening. Heads up: you're not eligible if you currently have a personal IHG card or earned a new-cardmember bonus on one in the last 24 months.

Here's the thing about IHG points: they're worth roughly 0.5-0.6 cents each, so this bonus clocks in at approximately $700-$840 in hotel value. That's enough for 3-4 nights at mid-range IHG properties or 1-2 nights at premium InterContinental or Kimpton hotels. And because of the 4th Night Free benefit, longer stays stretch that welcome bonus even further. Not bad for a $99 card.

Let's be real — these earning rates are quietly ridiculous. That 3x base rate on everything else? Most hotel cards give you 1-2x on non-category spending. IHG gives you 3x on your electric bill, your Amazon order, your random Target run. And at IHG properties, the bonuses stack like a layer cake: 10x card bonus + 10x base member earning + 6x Platinum Elite bonus = up to 26x total points per dollar. That adds up fast on a multi-night stay.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
IHG One Rewards points can be redeemed across their global hotel portfolio — and some options are better than others:

  • Free Night Stays — The main event. Book at 6,000+ IHG properties worldwide. Dynamic pricing means rates vary by property and date, typically ranging from 10,000-70,000+ points per night.
  • Points + Cash — Combine points with a cash co-pay when you're short on points. Handy, not thrilling.
  • 4th Night Free — Book 4+ consecutive nights on points and night four is complimentary. That's a straight 25% discount on longer award stays. Use this.
  • Airline Transfers — You can transfer points to select airline partners, but the rates are terrible. Just don't.
  • Gift Cards & Merchandise — Available through the IHG rewards catalog. Also terrible value. Stick with hotel stays.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:

  • Global Entry/TSA PreCheck: Up to $120 statement credit every 4 years for the application fee — one of the higher reimbursement amounts among hotel cards.
  • DashPass Membership: Complimentary 1-year DashPass for DoorDash and Caviar with $0 delivery fees. A nice cherry on top.
  • $100 Milestone Credit: Earn a $100 statement credit plus 10,000 bonus points in any calendar year you spend $20,000+ on the card.

title: Delta SkyMiles Gold
scouts_verdict:
The Delta Gold is the no-brainer entry point for anyone who flies Delta even a few times a year. The math is dead simple: two round trips with a checked bag saves you $180, more than covering the $150 annual fee — and year one is free, so you're playing with house money from day one.

Stack on the 2X earning at restaurants and supermarkets, and you've got a card that works for you between trips, not just at the airport. The $200 Delta flight credit after $10K in spending is a nice reward for loyalty, and the current welcome offer of as high as 80,000 miles plus a $250 statement credit is one of the richest in the entry-level airline card space — enough for a domestic round-trip or a one-way to Europe.

The honest trade-off: no companion certificate (that's the Platinum), no Sky Club access (that's the Reserve), and 1X on everything outside Delta, dining, and groceries is pretty meh. If you're a hardcore Delta loyalist flying every week, you should probably upgrade. But for the person who flies Delta a handful of times a year and wants solid value without overthinking it? The Gold nails it.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
The Delta SkyMiles Gold American Express Card is where most people start their Delta credit card journey, and honestly? For a lot of flyers, it's where they should stay. At $150 per year ($0 for the first year), it covers the essentials — free checked bag, 2X miles on dining and groceries, priority boarding — without asking you to shell out for perks you'll never use.

Think of the Gold card as the sensible sedan of the Delta lineup. It won't turn heads, but it'll get you where you need to go and save you money doing it. The $200 Delta flight credit (after $10,000 in spending) is a nice kicker, and the current welcome offer of as high as 80,000 miles plus a $250 statement credit is genuinely generous for a card at this price. No companion cert, no lounge access — just solid, no-fuss value for the occasional-to-moderate Delta flyer.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• First checked bag free on Delta flights for the cardholder and up to eight companions on the same reservation — saves $45 each way on domestic flights, $90 per round trip. Two round trips and the card more than pays for itself.
  • Second checked bag free on domestic Delta itineraries for the cardholder — another $55 each way you keep if you pack heavy.
  • $200 Delta Flight Credit after spending $10,000 on the card in a calendar year — not automatic, but worth chasing if you're close.
  • 15% off Delta Award Travel when redeeming SkyMiles for flights. Like a built-in coupon for every award booking.
  • Priority boarding on Delta flights — board before the main cabin masses.
  • No foreign transaction fees
  • $120 Rideshare Credit — up to $10/month in statement credits on U.S. rideshare purchases (Uber, Lyft, Curb and Alto) after your first card renewal. Enrollment required.
  • $100 Delta Stays Credit — up to $100 in statement credits each calendar year for prepaid hotels or vacation rentals booked through Delta Stays on delta.com.
  • 20% back on Delta in-flight purchases — food and beverages only. Headsets and Wi-Fi don't count, sadly.

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:
Annual Fee: $0 introductory for the first year, then $150 per year.

Foreign Transaction Fees: None.

Other Fees: Standard Amex fee schedule applies — late payment fee up to $40, cash advance fee of $10 or 5% (whichever is greater), and returned payment fee up to $40.

Here's the napkin math: two round trips with a checked bag saves you $180, which more than covers the $150 fee. Hit the $10K spending threshold and the $200 flight credit makes you come out way ahead. And year one is free, so you're literally playing with house money.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
Earn as high as 80,000 bonus SkyMiles plus a $250 statement credit after spending $3,000 on purchases in the first 6 months of card membership. Amex tells you your exact bonus after you apply and before you accept the card, and this limited-time offer ends November 4, 2026. Heads up: you may not be eligible if you have or have had the Delta Gold, Platinum or Reserve card.

At an approximate valuation of 1.2 cents per SkyMile, the full 80,000 miles are worth roughly $960 — add the $250 credit and this welcome offer is worth roughly $1,210. For a $150 card with the first year free, that's an outstanding return. We're talking enough miles for a round-trip domestic flight or even a one-way to Europe in economy. Don't sleep on this one.

sections.content:

Nothing flashy, but nothing to complain about either. The 2X on restaurants and supermarkets means this card does real work during the 95% of your life that you're not at the airport. The 1X on everything else is, admittedly, just okay — but you're not carrying this card for everyday maximization. You're carrying it because you fly Delta and like saving money on bags.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
SkyMiles earned with the Delta Gold card can be put to work in a few ways:

  • Delta flights: Book award flights directly through Delta, with the 15% TakeOff 15 discount stretching your points further. This is where you want to redeem.
  • Delta Vacations: Use miles for flight + hotel vacation packages
  • Pay with Miles: Take up to $50 off a delta.com fare for every 5,000 miles you redeem
  • Seat upgrades: Use miles for Delta Comfort or Delta First upgrades
  • Hotels, car rentals and experiences: Use miles on Delta Stays hotels, Delta Car Rentals or SkyMiles Experiences — possible, but rarely the best use of your miles.
  • Transfer to partners: Delta is part of SkyTeam, but SkyMiles are not transferable to other airline programs. What you earn stays with Delta.

The best bang for your miles is always booking Delta flights directly, especially with that 15% discount sweetening the deal.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• $200 Delta Flight Credit: Earned after $10,000 in calendar-year spending on the card. Think of it as a reward for putting real volume through the card, not a freebie.
  • Free checked bags: Your first bag is free on Delta flights (saving $45 per bag per direction on domestic routes), and on domestic itineraries your second bag is free too. The single most tangible perk on this card.
  • Priority boarding: Board with Zone 5. Small luxury, big satisfaction.
  • 20% in-flight savings: Statement credit on food and beverages purchased during Delta flights.
  • $100 Delta Stays Credit: Up to $100 back each calendar year on prepaid hotels or vacation rentals booked through Delta Stays on delta.com.
  • $120 Rideshare Credit: Up to $10/month on U.S. rideshare purchases (Uber, Lyft, Curb and Alto), starting after your first card renewal. Enrollment required.

No lounge access, no companion cert, no TSA PreCheck credit. This is an essentials-only card, and it owns that lane.

The Delta Gold wins the sign-up bonus battle handily — up to 80,000 miles plus a $250 credit vs. up to 60,000 from United and 50,000 from AA. The $200 flight credit is also the largest, though it requires $10K in spending to unlock. The United Explorer counters with 3X on United purchases and a bigger credit package — its Instacart and JSX credits have no Delta Gold equivalent. The Citi AAdvantage Platinum Select (which absorbed the old Barclays Aviator Red in April 2026) is cheapest at $99 and adds 2X on gas, but it has the smallest bonus of the three. Pick your airline first, then pick your card.

sections.title: Best For
sections.content:
• Occasional Delta flyers who check bags 2-4 times per year and want the fee to basically pay for itself.
  • Dining and grocery spenders who want Delta miles building up on everyday purchases without thinking about it.
  • Travelers who spend $10K+ annually on the card — that $200 flight credit is the cherry on top.
  • Credit card beginners looking for an entry point into the Delta ecosystem without a premium price tag.

Who should look elsewhere: anyone wanting lounge access (that's the Reserve), travelers who need a companion certificate (that's the Platinum), or people who fly Delta once a year or less. If you're a Delta diehard who flies a dozen+ times annually, the Platinum card's companion cert is probably worth the upgrade.

title: Delta SkyMiles Platinum
scouts_verdict:
The Delta Platinum is the card I'd hand to any couple that flies Delta. The companion certificate is the whole story — on a decent domestic round-trip that would normally cost $300-$500, your travel partner flies for just taxes and fees. That single perk can return more value than the entire $350 annual fee in one shot. If you travel with someone even once a year, the math just works.

The 3X on Delta and hotels is a nice bump over the Gold, and the MQD head start plus free checked bags for up to 9 people are genuinely useful extras. But let's not overcomplicate this: you either need the companion cert or you don't. If you do, there's no better deal in airline cards at this price.

Where it falls short: no lounge access, the credits ($150 Delta Stays plus $10 a month each for Resy and rideshare) take some effort to actually use, and if you're a solo traveler, that companion cert is just wasted cardboard. In that case, stick with the Gold at $150 and pocket the difference. But if you've got someone to share that cert with? The Platinum is one of the best values in co-branded airline cards, period.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Here's the pitch for the Delta SkyMiles Platinum American Express Card: you get an annual companion certificate that can save you $200-$500+ on a single domestic ticket, and the card costs $350 per year. If you fly Delta with another human being even once a year, the math basically does itself.

Sitting in the middle of the Delta/Amex lineup between the Gold ($150) and Reserve ($650), the Platinum is the sweet spot card. It bumps your earning to 3X on Delta and hotels, gives your whole travel party free checked bags, tosses in a $2,500 MQD head start for Medallion status chasers, and — most importantly — hands you that companion cert every anniversary. For couples, travel buddies, and families who fly Delta, this is the card that actually saves real, tangible money.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• Annual Companion Certificate — Buy one round-trip domestic, Caribbean, or Central American ticket and get a companion ticket for just taxes and fees ($22-$250). Valid in Delta Main (Main Cabin) only; Basic fares don't qualify. This is the headline act.
  • First checked bag free for the cardholder and up to 8 companions on the same reservation — yes, eight people. Since June 2026 you (the cardholder) also check a second bag free on domestic Delta flights.
  • Priority boarding on Delta flights
  • $2,500 MQD Head Start deposited into your SkyMiles account each Medallion Qualification Year — a real boost toward Silver, Gold, or Platinum Medallion status. MQD Boost adds $1 MQD for every $20 you spend on the card.
  • Up to $390 a year in statement credits — up to $150 on prepaid hotels or vacation rentals booked through Delta Stays, plus up to $10 a month each at U.S. Resy restaurants and on U.S. rideshare (those two need enrollment).
  • 20% back on Delta in-flight purchases
  • No foreign transaction fees
  • Global Entry / TSA PreCheck credit ($120 for Global Entry every 4 years, or up to $85 for TSA PreCheck)

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:
Annual Fee: $350 per year.

Foreign Transaction Fees: None.

Other Fees: Standard Amex fee structure — late payment fees up to $40, returned payment fees up to $40, and a cash advance fee of $10 or 5% (whichever is greater).

$350 sounds like a lot until you use the companion cert on a $400 round-trip ticket and basically fly your partner for free. Add the free checked bags for up to 9 people and the MQD head start, and most frequent Delta flyers aren't just breaking even — they're coming out well ahead.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
The current public offer: as high as 90,000 bonus SkyMiles plus a $300 statement credit after you spend $4,000 on purchases in the first 6 months. Welcome offers vary, so Amex shows you your actual number when you apply, and you may not get the top one. The offer ends November 4, 2026.

At roughly 1.2 cents per SkyMile, 90,000 miles is worth about $1,080, and the $300 credit brings the full package to roughly $1,380. By that math it beats the 100,000-mile offers Amex ran earlier in 2026 (about $1,200 at the same rate), but it's an as high as offer, so check the number Amex actually shows you before you commit. These elevated Delta Amex offers come and go; if you were going to get this card anyway, 90K plus $300 is a solid time to jump.

The jump from the Gold's 2X on Delta (and plain 1X on hotels) to 3X on both is meaningful if you're booking flights and hotel stays regularly. Dining and supermarkets stay at 2X — identical to the Gold. The 1X on everything else is still just okay, but let's be honest: you're not carrying this card for its earning rates. You're carrying it for that companion cert.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
SkyMiles redemption options are the same as on the Delta Gold and Reserve cards — no special perks here for being Platinum:

  • Delta flights: Book award flights through delta.com — best value, especially with the 15% SkyMiles discount
  • Delta Vacations: Use miles toward flight + hotel packages
  • Seat upgrades: Upgrade to Delta Comfort or Delta First with miles
  • Delta Sky Club: Delta no longer sells one-time Sky Club passes, so you can't use miles to buy yourself a single visit. If you're a Club member, though, you can pay a guest's entry with 5,000 miles instead of $50.
  • Hotels, rental cars and experiences: Miles also cover Delta Stays hotels, Delta car rentals, and bids on SkyMiles Experiences — handy in a pinch, but like airport sushi, rarely the best choice

SkyMiles are not transferable to partner airlines. Your best move is always redeeming directly for Delta flights, where dynamic pricing occasionally serves up solid domestic deals.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• Companion Certificate: The reason this card exists. Earned on each card anniversary, it covers one companion on a round-trip domestic, Caribbean, or Central American flight for just taxes and fees ($22-$250). Delta Main (Main Cabin) only; Basic fares don't qualify.
  • $150 Delta Stays credit: Up to $150 back each year on prepaid hotels or vacation rentals booked through Delta Stays on delta.com.
  • $120 Resy credit: Up to $10 a month at U.S. Resy restaurants. Enrollment required.
  • $120 rideshare credit: Up to $10 a month on U.S. rideshare with select providers. Enrollment required.
  • Free checked bags: First bag free for the cardholder and up to 8 travel companions on the same reservation. Traveling with a group? That's potentially hundreds in saved bag fees. On domestic Delta flights, your own second bag is free too.
  • $2,500 MQD Head Start: Applied automatically each qualification year. If you're grinding toward Medallion status, this shortcut is real. MQD Boost adds $1 MQD for every $20 you spend on the card.
  • 20% in-flight savings: Statement credit on food and beverages
  • Global Entry / TSA PreCheck credit: $120 for Global Entry every 4 years, or up to $85 for TSA PreCheck

At $350, the Delta Platinum and United Quest go head-to-head — both hand back statement credits, but it comes down to one question: companion cert or a United flight credit? The Platinum's companion cert can be worth $200-$500+ in a single use. The Quest's $200 United credit is guaranteed but smaller. If you travel with a partner, the Platinum wins. If you fly solo and want a sure-thing flight credit (plus 4X on United purchases), the Quest has the edge. The Citi Executive at $695 gives you lounge access but no companion cert and costs nearly twice as much.

sections.title: Best For
sections.content:
• Couples and travel partners who fly Delta domestically — the companion cert was literally designed for you.
  • Families and groups who benefit from free checked bags for up to 9 travelers on the same itinerary. That's a lot of saved baggage fees.
  • Delta loyalists chasing Medallion status who want the $2,500 MQD head start to close the gap.
  • Frequent Delta flyers who want the 3X bump on Delta and hotel purchases.

Who should skip it: solo travelers who rarely fly with companions (the companion cert just sits there unused), anyone who needs lounge access (step up to the Reserve), or travelers who don't fly Delta enough to justify $350/year. If you're solo, the Gold at $150 gives you most of the same everyday earning and costs $200 less.

title: Delta SkyMiles Reserve
scouts_verdict:
The Delta Reserve is a perks card, not a points card — and you need to evaluate it on those terms. A 3X/1X earning structure on a $650 card is, frankly, embarrassing compared to what competitors offer. But that's not why you carry the Reserve. You carry it for Sky Club access, a companion cert that works on First Class tickets, and $360/year in dining and rideshare credits that take almost no effort once you enroll.

The 15 Sky Club visits per year are the headline — and for a Delta hub flyer who hits the lounge regularly, that alone can be worth $500+ at day-pass prices. The companion cert upgrade to First Class and Delta Comfort is a meaningful step up from the Platinum's Delta Main-only cert. And those Resy and rideshare credits? Enroll, and then all they ask is that you eat food and get rides. Not exactly a burden.

The honest calculus: if you fly Delta 10+ times a year, use Sky Clubs, dine out, and travel with a companion — the Reserve pays for itself and then some. But if you're flying Delta a few times a year and just want the essentials, you're overpaying by hundreds. The Platinum at $350 gives you a companion cert and better everyday earning. The Reserve is a luxury — treat it like one and only carry it if you'll use every perk.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Let's get this out of the way: the Delta SkyMiles Reserve American Express Card has a $650 annual fee and earns just 1X on non-Delta purchases. If you're evaluating this card on earning rates, close this tab now. The Reserve's value lives entirely in its perks — Sky Club access, a companion cert valid in First Class, and a stack of dining and rideshare credits that chip away at that fee until it barely stings.

This is the top-tier personal card in the Delta/Amex family, and it's built for a very specific person: the frequent Delta flyer who uses Sky Clubs, travels with a companion, and dines out regularly. If that's you, the Reserve can deliver serious value. If that's not you, the Platinum at $350 probably gives you everything you need.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• Delta Sky Club access — 15 visits per year included, plus 4 one-time guest passes to bring friends along; unlimited visits if you spend $75,000+ on the card in a calendar year. At $50+ per day pass, this adds up fast.
  • Access to Centurion Lounges when flying Delta on a ticket purchased with the Reserve card, plus Escape Lounges when you fly Delta that day on a ticket bought with a U.S. Amex card (guests pay the lounge's fee) — a perk that other airline cards can't match.
  • Annual Companion Certificate valid on round-trip flights within the U.S. or to Mexico, the Caribbean, or Central America in Delta First, Delta Premium Select, Delta Comfort, or Delta Main. Yes, First Class.
  • $240 Resy dining credit — up to $20/month in statement credits at U.S. Resy restaurants after enrollment. Just eat out. That's it.
  • $120 rideshare credit — up to $10/month in statement credits on U.S. rideshare purchases with select providers. Enrollment required.
  • $200 Delta Stays credit — up to $200 back each year on prepaid hotels or vacation rentals booked through Delta Stays on delta.com.
  • $2,500 MQD Head Start each Medallion Qualification Year, plus MQD Boost ($1 MQD per $10 spent on the card).
  • First checked bag free on Delta flights, plus a free second bag on domestic Delta-operated flights for the primary cardholder, and Zone 5 priority boarding — the table stakes perks.
  • No foreign transaction fees

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:
Annual Fee: $650 per year.

Foreign Transaction Fees: None.

Other Fees: Standard Amex fee structure applies.

Let's do the real math:

  • $650 annual fee
  • Minus $240 Resy credit = $410
  • Minus $120 rideshare credit = $290
  • Minus $200 Delta Stays credit (if you book a prepaid hotel through Delta) = $90
  • Minus companion cert value (~$200-$600) = potentially $0 or negative

If you actually use the dining and rideshare credits (which just means enrolling, then eating at restaurants and taking Ubers — not exactly a hardship), the effective cost drops to $290, and to $90 if you also use the $200 Delta Stays credit. Use the companion cert on a pricey ticket and the card can be free. The key word is "if."

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
Earn two round-trip Delta Comfort Flight Certificates plus 50,000 bonus SkyMiles after spending $10,000 on purchases in the first 6 months. It's a limited-time offer for eligible new Card Members that runs through November 4, 2026. The certificates have no blackout dates and work in Delta Comfort or Delta Main on round-trip, Delta-operated flights within the U.S. 48, Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands. You'll need to book 21+ days out and pay up to $80 per person in taxes and fees.

At roughly 1.2 cents per SkyMile, the 50,000 miles are worth about $600. The two certificates are the wild card: what they're worth depends entirely on the routes you book, so save them for pricey ones. The $10,000 spend requirement is steep (about $1,667 a month for 6 months), so only go for it if your regular spending gets you there. The Reserve has offered as much as 125,000 miles before, so if you'd rather have miles than flights, it can pay to wait for the next big mileage offer.

sections.title: Earning Rates
sections.content:

All other eligible purchases1X

This is the elephant in the room. A $650 card that earns 1X on everything outside Delta? In 2026? The Platinum card — which costs $300 less — earns 2X on restaurants and U.S. supermarkets and 3X on hotels. The Reserve actually has worse everyday earning rates than the card below it. That's not a typo.

The card makes up for it with the MQD Boost: earn $1 MQD for every $10 spent, which is a powerful tool for reaching Medallion status. But as a points-earning machine, the Reserve is genuinely mediocre. Its value is in the perks, not the points.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
Redemption options mirror the other Delta Amex cards — nothing special for Reserve holders here:

  • Delta flights: Best-value redemption — book award flights on delta.com
  • Delta Vacations: Flight + hotel packages
  • Seat upgrades: Delta Comfort or First Class with miles
  • SkyMiles Experiences: Bid miles on exclusive events, dining experiences and getaways. Fun, but rarely the best use of your miles. (The old SkyMiles Marketplace for gift cards and merchandise has closed.)

Reserve cardholders get the same 15% SkyMiles discount on Delta award flights. SkyMiles remain non-transferable to partner programs — what you earn stays in the Delta ecosystem.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• 15 Delta Sky Club visits/year — access when flying Delta. Spend $75,000 on the card and visits become unlimited. At day-pass prices, regular lounge users save hundreds.
  • Centurion Lounge access when flying Delta on a Reserve-purchased ticket. These lounges are a clear step above Sky Clubs.
  • Escape Lounge access when flying Delta the same day on a ticket bought with a U.S. Amex card. Entry-time rules vary by location, and guests pay the lounge's guest fee.
  • $240 Resy dining credit — $20/month at U.S. Resy restaurants (must enroll). Low-effort perk if you eat out even occasionally.
  • $120 rideshare credit — $10/month on U.S. rideshare purchases with select providers. Enroll, take a few rides and it's done.
  • $200 Delta Stays credit — up to $200 a year back on prepaid hotels or vacation rentals booked through Delta Stays on delta.com. Worth it if you'd book a hotel anyway.
  • Companion Certificate — valid on Delta First, Delta Premium Select, Delta Comfort, or Delta Main round-trips within the U.S. or to Mexico, the Caribbean, or Central America. Issued each year after your card renews; you pay taxes and fees of $22 to $250, and Delta Basic fares don't qualify. The upgrade to First Class eligibility is a big deal vs. the Platinum's cert.
  • $2,500 MQD Head Start + MQD Boost ($1 per $10 spent)
  • Global Entry / TSA PreCheck credit — $120 for Global Entry or up to $85 for TSA PreCheck: one credit every 4 years, for whichever you apply for first
  • Global Dining Access by Resy — exclusive restaurant reservations. Nice for foodies.

Of these three, the Reserve is the only one that bundles lounge access and a companion certificate. That's its superpower. The United Club Infinite counters with unlimited lounge visits, 5X on United purchases and 2X on dining and other travel, and bigger travel credits — but no companion cert. The Citi Executive now costs the same $695 as the United card; it pairs unlimited Admirals Club access with the biggest mileage bonus of the three, but has no companion cert and no dining credit. The real question: do you value a companion cert plus capped lounge visits, or unlimited lounge visits plus better everyday earning? Your answer picks your card.

sections.title: Best For
sections.content:
• Frequent Delta hub flyers who visit Sky Clubs regularly — ATL, MSP, DTW, SEA, you know who you are.
  • Travelers chasing Delta Medallion status who need the MQD Boost to hit qualification thresholds.
  • Couples who fly premium cabins — using the companion cert on First Class tickets is where the real savings live.
  • Diners and rideshare users who'll naturally burn through the $240 + $120 in annual credits without changing their habits.

Who should pass: infrequent travelers who won't use the lounge visits (you're paying for empty chairs), anyone who needs strong everyday earning rates (1X is genuinely weak for $650), or people who already have Centurion Lounge access through the Amex Platinum. If you fly Delta 3-4 times a year and just want the basics, the Platinum at $350 is the smarter play.

title: United Explorer Card
scouts_verdict:
The 2025 refresh turned the United Explorer from a decent entry-level card into one of the best values in the airline card space. Over $500 in potential credits against a $150 fee — with the first year free — is the kind of math that makes you double-check you're reading it right.

The free checked bag for both you and a companion is a quiet winner, and the Star Alliance redemption options give United miles a flexibility edge that Delta miles simply don't have. ANA First Class to Japan? Lufthansa Business to Europe? That's where this card's miles really earn their keep.

The catch is the word "potential." Those credits are spread across Instacart, rideshare, United Hotels, Avis/Budget and JSX, plus a $100 United credit that takes $10K in spend — and each comes with its own fine print, from monthly caps to enrollment hoops. If you're disciplined about using them, this card is a steal. If you're the type who forgets to activate perks, the on-paper value evaporates fast. But for a United flyer willing to work the system, the Explorer punches way above its weight class.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
The United Explorer Card from Chase got a major glow-up in the 2025 refresh, and the result is honestly kind of wild for a $150 annual fee card ($0 the first year). We're talking $100 United credit, $120 in Instacart credits, $60 in rideshare credits, hotel credits, rental car credits, JSX credits — over $500 in potential annual value before you even count the free checked bags or priority boarding.

This is the entry-level annual-fee card in the United/Chase personal lineup (the no-fee United Gateway sits below it), and it's designed for the occasional-to-moderate United flyer who wants to stack credits without paying premium prices. The challenge? Actually using all those credits, since they come with specific merchants, monthly caps, and enrollment requirements. If you're the type who sets calendar reminders for perks, this card will reward you handsomely. If credits expire unused in your account, the math won't be as pretty.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• First checked bag free on United flights for the cardholder and a companion on the same reservation — both of you, not just you.
  • Priority boarding on United flights
  • 2 United Club one-time passes per year — a taste of the lounge life.
  • $100 United Travel Credit — earned after spending $10,000 with the card within a calendar year, delivered as United TravelBank cash.
  • Up to $60/year in rideshare credits
  • 10,000-mile award flight discount after $20,000 annual spend — reduces the miles needed for certain award flights.
  • Up to $100 JSX flight credits per year when booking flights directly with JSX.
  • Up to $100 in statement credits on United Hotels purchases
  • Up to $50 in United Travel Credits on Avis or Budget purchases
  • Up to $120/year in Instacart credits plus complimentary 3-month Instacart+ membership (25% off annual membership afterward)
  • Up to $120 Global Entry, TSA PreCheck or NEXUS credit every 4 years
  • 10% or more off United award flights booked with miles, thanks to cardmember award pricing
  • No foreign transaction fees

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:
Annual Fee: $0 introductory for the first year, then $150 per year. (Existing cardholders transitioned to the new $150 fee on or after January 1, 2026.)

Foreign Transaction Fees: None.

Other Fees: Standard Chase fee schedule applies.

On paper, the credits blow the $150 fee out of the water: $100 United credit + $120 Instacart + $60 rideshare + $100 hotel + $50 rental car + $100 JSX = $530. In reality, maximizing every single one takes effort and planning. But even hitting half of them puts you well ahead. And year one is free, so there's literally no risk in trying.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
Earn 50,000 bonus miles after spending $3,000 on purchases in the first 3 months, plus 10,000 bonus miles after adding an authorized user in the first 3 months — for a total of up to 60,000 miles.

At roughly 1.3 cents per United mile, this bonus is worth approximately $780. Not the highest in the United lineup, and the card has carried a 70,000-mile offer as recently as early 2026, so it is worth watching for an elevated promotion. That said, the $3,000 spend threshold is low and the authorized user bonus is basically free.

Important: This offer is not available if you are a current cardholder or received a new cardmember bonus on this card in the past 24 months.

The 2X on dining and hotels is solid for this price tier. Pro tip: stack with United's MileagePlus Dining program for up to 7X total at participating restaurants. The 1X on everything else is just there. Not great, not terrible.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
United MileagePlus miles are genuinely flexible — and this is where United has a real edge over Delta:

  • United and Star Alliance flights: Book award flights on United, Lufthansa, ANA, Singapore Airlines, and 20+ Star Alliance partners. This is the money move.
  • Statement credits: Use miles earned on the card for a statement credit on United ticket purchases or your annual fee
  • Upgrades: Use miles for Economy to Business/First upgrades on select routes
  • Hotels and car rentals: Book through United's travel portal
  • Merchandise and gift cards: Available through MileagePlus but the value is bad. Just don't.

The real magic is Star Alliance partner redemptions — sweet spots include ANA First Class to Japan and Lufthansa Business Class to Europe, often at far lower mile costs than United's own flights. This is where MileagePlus miles really shine.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• $100 United Travel Credit: Earned after spending $10,000 with the card within a calendar year, delivered as United TravelBank cash. Requires meaningful spend to unlock.
  • Up to $120/year Instacart credits: Monthly credits toward Instacart purchases, plus a complimentary 3-month Instacart+ membership. Great if you already use Instacart; wasted if you don't.
  • Up to $60/year rideshare credits: Statement credits on rideshare services.
  • Up to $100 United Hotels credits: Statement credits on hotels booked through United Hotels.
  • Up to $50 Avis/Budget credits: United Travel Credits on rental car bookings.
  • Up to $100 JSX credits: Statement credits on flights booked directly with JSX.
  • 10,000-mile award flight discount: Earned after $20,000 in calendar-year spend; reduces the miles needed for an eligible United award flight. Free miles, basically, if you hit the spend.
  • 2 United Club one-time passes: Single-visit lounge access — nice for special occasions.
  • Free checked bag: For cardholder and a companion on the same reservation.

Total potential annual credit value: $530. That's about 3.5x the annual fee. But potential and reality are different things — you have to actually use these credits for them to matter.

Where the Delta Gold fights back is bags (first bag free for you and up to 8 companions, plus the cardholder's second bag free on domestic flights), the sign-up bonus (up to 80K + $250 vs 60K) and the $200 flight credit (though that needs $10K in spending). sections.title: Best For
sections.content:
• Occasional-to-moderate United flyers who check bags and want priority boarding without paying premium prices.

  • Credit stackers who enjoy maximizing value — the $530 in annual credits vs. $150 fee is one of the best ratios in airline cards, if you put in the work.

Not the right card for: frequent flyers who need real lounge access (2 passes won't cut it), anyone chasing United Premier status (the Quest does that better), or people who rarely fly United or Star Alliance partners.

title: United Quest Card
scouts_verdict:
The United Quest is the ultimate status-chaser's weapon. Outside the pricier Club Infinite, no personal airline card lets you earn up to 18,000 PQP per year from spending — and 18,000 PQP is the entire PQP-only bar for Premier Platinum, as long as you also fly the four United flights every Premier tier requires. Add the 1,000 PQP annual bonus and 500 PQP sign-up bonus, and you're getting a running start that, among personal United cards, only the $695 Club Infinite beats.

The $350 fee is basically a non-issue: $200 United credit + $180 Instacart = $380 in credits against a $350 fee. You're ahead before counting the 2 free checked bags, the 10,000-mile award discount, or the JSX credits. The earning rates are solid too — 4X on United and 2X on travel, dining, and streaming covers most of a frequent traveler's spending.

Where the Quest loses to the Delta Platinum is obvious: no companion cert. If you regularly travel with someone and a companion cert would save you $300-$500, that's hard to ignore. But if you're a solo flyer, a United status grinder, or someone who prefers a guaranteed $200 credit over a situational cert, the Quest is the better card. One of the most underrated mid-tier airline cards out there.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
If you care about earning United Premier status, stop scrolling — the United Quest Card from Chase is your card. At $350 per year (up from $250 after the 2025 refresh), it offers one of the most aggressive PQP-earning structures of any personal airline card (only the $695 Club Infinite earns faster), letting you rack up qualifying points through everyday spending like groceries, gas, and streaming subscriptions.

But the Quest isn't just a status card. The $200 United travel credit, 2 free checked bags, $180 in Instacart credits, and a 10,000-mile award discount add up to $530+ in annual value — comfortably above the $350 fee. Think of it as the mid-tier United card that does everything well, with a status-chasing superpower that, among United cards, only the pricier Club Infinite tops.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• $200 United travel credit — paid as United TravelBank cash (not a statement credit) after account opening and on each anniversary. No spending threshold. Just book a United or United Express flight within 12 months, before it expires.
  • 2 free checked bags on United flights (terms apply). That's both bags, not just one.
  • Priority boarding on United flights
  • 10,000-mile award flight discount on each card anniversary — 10,000 miles off one United or United Express award that costs more than 10,000 miles. It's a discount, not miles in your account, and it expires 12 months after it posts.
  • Up to 18,000 PQP per year — earn 1 PQP per $20 spent. Second only to the Club Infinite's 28,000 PQP cap among personal United cards.
  • 1,000 PQP annual bonus deposited within 8 weeks of February 1 each year, starting the calendar year after you open the card. Free status progress.
  • Up to $180/year in Instacart credits — one $10 and one $5 Instacart credit per month with an active Instacart+ membership (through Dec 31, 2027)
  • Up to $150 in JSX credits per year when booking flights directly with JSX
  • Up to $120 Global Entry, TSA PreCheck or NEXUS credit — once every 4 years, not every year.
  • No foreign transaction fees

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:
Annual Fee: $350 per year (increased from $250 in the 2025 refresh).

Foreign Transaction Fees: None.

Other Fees: Standard Chase fee schedule applies.

The math that matters:

  • $350 annual fee
  • Minus $200 United travel credit = $150
  • Minus $180 Instacart credits = effectively -$30 (you're ahead)

Before you even factor in the checked bags, the PQP value, the award discount, or the JSX credits, the Quest is paying you back more than it costs. The $100 fee increase from 2025 stings, but the credits more than cover it.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
Earn 60,000 bonus miles and 500 Premier qualifying points (PQP) after spending $4,000 on purchases in the first 3 months from account opening, plus 10,000 more miles for adding an authorized user in those same 3 months — up to 70,000 miles total. You're not eligible if you already have the Quest or earned a Quest bonus in the past 24 months.

At roughly 1.3 cents per United mile, the full 70,000 miles are worth approximately $910. The 500 PQP is a small nudge for status seekers — the real status engine is the 1 PQP per $20 you earn on every purchase.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
Same MileagePlus redemption options as the rest of the United lineup — the Quest's perks here just make award flights cheaper:

  • United TravelBank: Convert miles to travel credits
  • Upgrades: Use miles for cabin upgrades on select routes
  • Hotels and car rentals: Through United's portal
  • Cardmember award pricing: At least 10% fewer miles on United and United Express award flights (at least 15% fewer with Premier status).

That 10,000-mile award flight discount earned on your anniversary isn't free miles: no miles land in your account. It knocks 10,000 miles off one United or United Express award that costs more than 10,000 miles, can't be combined with another discount or used on Money + Miles, and expires 12 months after it posts. Put it toward an award you'd book anyway, before it lapses.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• $200 United travel credit: Arrives as United TravelBank cash at opening and each anniversary, not as a statement credit. Book a United or United Express flight with it within 12 months or it expires, and it can't be used on Money + Miles bookings.
  • 10,000-mile award flight discount: Earned on each card anniversary, takes 10,000 miles off an award that costs more than 10,000 miles. It's a discount, not deposited miles, and each one expires 12 months after it posts. Spend $20,000 in a calendar year and you earn a second one.
  • 2 free checked bags: On United flights for you and one companion on the same reservation, as long as you buy the ticket with the card (that rule is waived for your first 90 days; terms apply). Both bags, not just the first.
  • 2 global Economy Plus seat upgrades: Earned after $40,000 in purchases each calendar year.
  • Up to $180/year Instacart credits: One $10 and one $5 Instacart credit per month through Dec 31, 2027, as long as you keep an Instacart+ membership (free for 3 months, then half off). Great if you grocery-deliver; wasted if you don't.
  • Up to $150/year JSX credits: Statement credits when booking JSX flights directly.
  • Up to $150/year Renowned Hotels credits: Statement credits on prepaid hotel stays booked through Renowned Hotels and Resorts for United Cardmembers.
  • Up to $100/year rideshare credits: Up to $8/month (Jan-Nov) and $12 in December on rideshare purchases (requires annual enrollment).
  • Up to $80/year Avis/Budget credits: $40 in United TravelBank cash on each of your first two Avis or Budget rentals every anniversary year, booked through cars.united.com and paid with the card.
  • Up to $120 Global Entry, TSA PreCheck or NEXUS credit: One statement credit every 4 years, not annually, when you pay the application fee with the card.
  • 25% back on United inflight purchases: A statement credit on food, drinks and Wi-Fi on United flights and on premium drinks in United Clubs.
  • 1,000 PQP annual bonus: Awarded within 8 weeks of Feb 1 each year, starting the calendar year after you open the card. Free status progress.
  • Up to 18,000 PQP/year from spending: 1 PQP per $20 spent. The status-chaser's secret weapon.

Total quantifiable annual credit value: $860 on paper (Chase pitches it as over $850 in partner credits) — well above the $350 fee. This is one of the strongest mid-tier airline cards for United flyers who actually use the credits.

The Quest vs. Delta Platinum at $350 is the classic showdown: travel credit or companion cert? The Quest gives you a guaranteed $200 United credit plus a PQP engine that only the pricier Club Infinite beats. The Delta Platinum fires back with a companion cert worth $200-$500+ in a single use. If you travel with a partner, the Platinum wins on sheer savings potential. If you're solo or chasing United Premier status, the Quest is the stronger play. Both are excellent — just for different people.

sections.title: Best For
sections.content:
• United Premier status chasers — if earning or maintaining status matters to you, the 18,000 PQP cap makes this card almost mandatory.
  • Moderate-to-frequent United flyers who'll use the $200 travel credit and 2 free checked bags without thinking twice.
  • Instacart regulars who can absorb $180/year in credits naturally.
  • Solo travelers who want a guaranteed travel credit instead of a companion cert they can't use.

Not ideal for: travelers who want lounge access (that's the Club Infinite), people who don't fly United enough to use the $200 credit, or couples who'd get more value from the Delta Platinum's companion certificate. Know your travel style, pick your card.

title: United Club Infinite Card
scouts_verdict:
The Club Infinite is a card you either need or you don't — and the answer hinges entirely on United Club lounges. A standalone membership costs ~$750. This card costs $695 and gives you that membership, up to $890 in credits, 5X on United plus 2X on dining and travel, and the most aggressive PQP engine in the United lineup. If you were going to buy the membership anyway, you'd be leaving money on the table by not getting this card.

The 2X on dining and travel is the unsung hero here. The Delta Reserve and Citi Executive both earn 1X on dining and most non-airline travel — meaning the Club Infinite literally earns double what its premium competitors do at restaurants, on rideshares and at most hotels. Over a year of normal expenses, that gap adds up to thousands of extra miles. And the 28,000 PQP cap is borderline absurd for status seekers — that's enough to clear Premier Platinum (18,000 PQP) and even hit the Premier 1K bar (28,000) from card spending, as long as you also fly the four United flights every Premier tier requires.

The honest downside: $695 is real money, and there's no companion cert to deliver a single big value hit like the Delta Reserve offers. The credits are spread across Instacart, rideshare, Renowned Hotels, JSX and Avis/Budget — useful if they fit your life, wasted if they don't. For the United road warrior who lives in the Club, this card is practically mandatory. For everyone else, the Quest or Explorer will serve you better without the premium price tag.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
The United Club Infinite Card from Chase (now marketed simply as the United Club Card) is for people who already know they want a United Club membership — and the question is whether getting it bundled into a credit card makes more sense than buying it standalone. Spoiler: it does. A standalone United Club membership runs about $750/year. This card costs $695 and gives you that membership plus up to $890 in annual credits plus 5X on United and 2X on dining and travel. The math is almost embarrassingly good.

The 2025 refresh bumped the fee from $525 to $695 but loaded the card with new credits: $240/year Instacart, $150/year rideshare, $200 Renowned Hotels, $200 JSX and $100 Avis/Budget credits, plus up to 20,000 miles in award flight discounts. It also boosted the PQP cap to a ridiculous 28,000 per year. For the United road warrior, this is the card that does it all — lounge access, status earning, everyday spending, and a wall of credits. For everyone else, it's probably overkill.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• United Club membership — unlimited access to United Club lounges worldwide when flying United. No visit caps, no spending thresholds. Just walk in.
  • 2 free checked bags on United flights (terms apply)
  • Premier Access travel services — priority check-in, boarding, and security. Skip the lines.
  • Up to 28,000 PQP per year — earn 1 PQP per $15 spent on all purchases. The most aggressive PQP engine on any personal United card.
  • 1,500 PQP annual bonus deposited within 8 weeks of February 1 each year, starting the calendar year after you open the card
  • 4 United Club one-time passes each card anniversary — but only once you've unlocked United Club All Access (Premier Gold status or $50,000 in card spend in a calendar year) and have an authorized user
  • Up to $240/year in Instacart credits — two $10 credits per month, plus complimentary Instacart+ membership (through Dec 31, 2027)
  • Up to $150/year in rideshare credits — up to $12/month (Jan-Nov), up to $18 in December
  • Up to $200/year Renowned Hotels credits — statement credits on prepaid hotel bookings through Renowned Hotels and Resorts for United cardmembers
  • Up to 20,000-mile award flight discount — earn 10,000-mile discount at $20K spend, another 10,000 at $40K
  • No foreign transaction fees

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:
Annual Fee: $695 per year (increased from $525 in March 2025 for new applicants; existing cardholders transitioned on or after August 1, 2025).

Foreign Transaction Fees: None.

Other Fees: Standard Chase fee schedule applies.

Here's why the fee doesn't matter:

  • $695 annual fee
  • Minus $240 Instacart credits = $455
  • Minus $150 rideshare credits = $305
  • Minus $200 Renowned Hotels credits = $105
  • United Club membership (standalone cost: ~$750/year) = effectively deep into negative territory

If you would buy a United Club membership anyway, this card isn't just free — you're getting paid to carry it. The $695 fee only looks steep if you wouldn't use the lounge access. If you would, it's one of the best deals in premium cards.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
Earn 80,000 bonus miles after spending $5,000 on purchases in the first 3 months, plus 10,000 bonus miles after adding an authorized user in the first 3 months — for a total of up to 90,000 miles. You're not eligible if you currently have any United Club card or received this card's new-cardmember bonus in the past 24 months.

At roughly 1.3 cents per United mile, this bonus is worth approximately $1,170. That's one of the strongest welcome offers in the premium airline card space. The authorized user bonus is free money — add a family member, meet the threshold, collect the miles.
