The standard welcome bonus lands in the middle too — 55,000 points for $1,500 spend, between the Plus's 50,000 and the Priority's 60,000.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
The Southwest Rapid Rewards Premier sits in the middle of the Southwest card lineup — more perks than the Plus, fewer than the Priority, and priced at $149 to match. It's the Goldilocks option for Southwest flyers who want meaningful upgrades over the base card without paying $229 for the full premium experience.

The Premier's selling points over the Plus are the 3x earning on Southwest (vs. 2x), 6,000 anniversary points (vs. 3,000), a 15% promo code on your anniversary (vs. 10%), and Preferred seat selection 48 hours before departure. You still get the core perks — free checked bags, 10,000 Companion Pass qualifying points, and 25% back on inflight purchases.

Is it the best value? It depends on your flying frequency. For moderate Southwest flyers (3-4 flights per year), the Premier hits a sweet spot. Below that, the Plus is cheaper. Above that, the Priority's seat selection at booking and free Extra Legroom upgrades make it the better deal.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• Free Checked Bags: Cardmember and up to 8 passengers on the same reservation get their first bag free. Same across all Southwest cards.
  • 6,000 Anniversary Points: Worth ~$78 in Southwest flights. More than the Plus (3,000) but less than the Priority (7,500).
  • 15% Promo Code: A 15% discount code each anniversary year on Southwest flights (excludes Basic fares). Decent savings on premium fares.
  • Preferred Seat Selection: Complimentary Preferred seat within 48 hours of departure, when available. Valued at ~$70 round trip on average.
  • 10,000 Companion Pass QP Boost: Same annual head start toward the Companion Pass as all Southwest cards.
  • 25% Back on Inflight Purchases: Statement credit on inflight drinks bought with your Southwest card. (Wi-Fi counts too, but it's already free for Rapid Rewards members.)
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees: Use it internationally without surcharges.

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:
• Annual Fee: $149 — the middle ground between Plus ($99) and Priority ($229).
  • Foreign Transaction Fees: None
  • APR: Variable, 19.24% - 27.74%
  • Balance Transfer Fee: 5% of the amount transferred, $5 minimum
  • Late Payment Fee: Up to $40

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
Earn 55,000 bonus points after spending $1,500 on purchases in the first 3 months. At ~1.3 cents per point, that's roughly $715 in Southwest flight value.

Honestly, this is a solid middle-ground welcome bonus among the three Southwest cards. The Plus offers 50,000 for $1,000 spend, and the Priority offers 60,000 for $2,000 spend. If the welcome bonus is a major factor in your decision, the Priority's 60,000 is the biggest — but it takes $500 more spend and an $80 higher annual fee.

That said, keep an eye out for limited-time Companion Pass offers — when those appear, the welcome bonus becomes secondary.

sections.title: Earning Rates
sections.content:
• 3x points on: Southwest Airlines purchases.
  • 2x points on: Grocery stores and restaurants (on the first $8,000 in combined purchases per anniversary year, then 1x).
  • 1x points on: Everything else.

The 3x on Southwest is a nice step up from the Plus's 2x, and the $8,000 cap on grocery/restaurant bonus earning is more generous than the Plus's $5,000 cap on gas and groceries (though the Plus earns 2x on gas, where the Premier earns just 1x). Still, the Priority card's 4x on Southwest and uncapped restaurant earning is better for heavy spenders.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
Same straightforward redemption system as all Southwest cards:

  • Southwest Flights: No blackout dates, no award charts. Points cover the fare at ~1.2-1.5 cents per point.
  • Pay Yourself Back: Cardmembers can redeem points for a statement credit toward the annual fee or other eligible transactions.
  • Hotels & Car Rentals: Available through Rapid Rewards but generally poor value.
  • Gift Cards: Available but a waste of points.

Keep it simple: use your points for Southwest flights. That's where the value is.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• Free Checked Bags: For you and up to 8 companions. The universal Southwest card benefit.
  • 6,000 Anniversary Points: ~$78 in flight value, automatically deposited each year.
  • 15% Promo Code: Anniversary discount on Southwest flights. Useful for premium fare bookings.
  • Preferred Seat Selection: Access to Preferred seats 48 hours before departure, when available.
  • 25% Inflight Credit: Quarter back on inflight drinks (Wi-Fi is already free for Rapid Rewards members).

What's missing vs. the Priority: No seat selection at booking, no free Extra Legroom upgrades, and 1,500 fewer anniversary points (boarding is Group 5 on both). These are meaningful gaps for frequent flyers.

sections.title: Competitor Comparison
sections.content:
• vs. Southwest Plus ($99/yr): The Premier costs $50 more but earns 3x on Southwest (vs 2x), gives 6,000 anniversary points (vs 3,000), and bumps the anniversary promo code from 10% to 15%. Worth the upgrade if you fly Southwest 3+ times a year.
  • vs. Southwest Priority ($229/yr): The Priority costs $80 more but adds seat selection at booking, unlimited free Extra Legroom upgrades, 4x on Southwest, and 7,500 anniversary points, though it has no anniversary promo code. If you fly Southwest 5+ times a year, the Priority is the better deal.
  • vs. United Explorer ($150/yr, $0 first year): Different airline ecosystem entirely. The United Explorer offers lounge passes and higher earning on United flights. Pick based on which airline you fly.
  • vs. Delta SkyMiles Gold ($150/yr, $0 first year): Nearly identical price point. Delta Gold offers 2x on Delta, restaurants and U.S. supermarkets, plus a free first checked bag (and a free second bag on domestic Delta flights). Similar value proposition for their respective airlines.

sections.title: Best For
sections.content:
• Moderate Southwest flyers: 3-4 flights per year on Southwest. Enough to justify the upgrade over Plus, not enough to warrant the Priority.
  • Grocery and restaurant spenders: The $8,000 cap on 2x grocery/restaurant earning beats the Plus card's $5,000 gas/grocery cap, and the Plus has no restaurant bonus at all.
  • Companion Pass builders: Same 10,000 QP boost as all Southwest cards, plus 3x on Southwest spending helps accumulate qualifying points faster.

Not ideal for: Occasional flyers (get the Plus), frequent flyers (get the Priority), or the welcome-bonus obsessed (the Priority's 60,000-point offer is the biggest of the three).

title: AAdvantage Aviator Red
scouts_verdict: The Aviator Red had a great run — that one-purchase, 60,000-mile welcome bonus was legendary — but the card closed to new applicants on September 30, 2025, and Citi converted every account to the Citi AAdvantage Platinum Select on April 24, 2026. The earning rates were never the point: just 2x on AA purchases and 1x on everything else. This was a card you held for the free checked bags, the companion certificate after $20K spend, and that ridiculously easy sign-up bonus. At $99 a year, the checked bag benefit alone could pay for the card in one round trip. If you had one, it's now a Platinum Select: keep it for the bags and the better earning, but the old $25 Wi-Fi credit ends October 25, 2026 and the companion certificate goes away after your next cardmember anniversary. If you're shopping for a new AA card, the Citi AAdvantage Platinum Select is the clear successor — same fee, better earning categories, active welcome bonus.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
The AAdvantage Aviator Red was one of the most interesting airline credit cards on the market — a Barclays-issued Mastercard that earned American Airlines miles with a dead-simple welcome bonus (make one purchase, pay the annual fee, get 60,000 miles). But here's the important news: Barclays has exited the AA partnership, and on April 24, 2026 Citi converted every Aviator Red into the Citi AAdvantage Platinum Select.

If you had this card, it has already been switched to that Citi product. If you're considering applying, the card stopped taking new applicants on September 30, 2025. Converted accounts keep the first checked bag free for you and companions and 2x on AA purchases, and pick up Citi's 2x at restaurants and gas stations. The Barclays-era $25 Wi-Fi credit ends October 25, 2026, and the companion certificate (after $20,000 in spending) can be earned one last time through your next cardmember anniversary.

The Aviator Red filled an important niche — a non-Citi way to earn AA miles on a credit card. With the move to Citi, AA credit cards have consolidated under one issuer. For a full AA credit card strategy going forward, look at the Citi AAdvantage Platinum Select or Citi AAdvantage Executive.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• First Checked Bag Free: Free first checked bag for you and up to 4 companions on the same domestic AA reservation. Worth $45 each way per person ($50 at the airport).
  • Companion Certificate: Earn a companion certificate after spending $20,000 in purchases during a cardmember year. Your companion flies for $99 plus taxes. Decent value on expensive routes. Citi is ending this perk: you can earn it one last time through your next cardmember anniversary.
  • $25 Inflight Wi-Fi Credit: Up to $25 back in statement credits on inflight Wi-Fi purchases per anniversary year. Ends October 25, 2026.
  • 25% Inflight Savings: 25% back as a statement credit on inflight food and beverage purchases on American Airlines flights.
  • 0% Intro APR on Balance Transfers: 0% for the first 15 billing cycles on balance transfers made within 45 days of opening. Rare on an airline card, but it was only for new accounts, and the card no longer takes applications.
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees: Use internationally without surcharges.
  • Travel Protections: Under Barclays, the card came with travel accident insurance, an auto rental collision damage waiver, baggage delay insurance and trip cancellation and interruption coverage.

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:
• Annual Fee: $99
  • Foreign Transaction Fees: None
  • APR: Variable (Barclays last listed 20.24% - 29.99%; Citi lists 19.74% - 29.74% for new Platinum Select accounts)
  • Balance Transfer APR: 0% intro for 15 billing cycles (new accounts only; the card no longer takes applications), then variable rate
  • Late Payment Fee: Up to $40

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
Note: This card is no longer accepting new applications. The card stopped accepting new applicants on September 30, 2025, and Barclays handed its AA portfolio to Citi on April 24, 2026.

The Aviator Red was famous for its absurdly easy welcome bonus: 60,000 AAdvantage miles after making just one purchase and paying the $99 annual fee. No minimum spend requirement — just one purchase of any amount within 90 days of account opening. It was one of the easiest airline card bonuses in history.

For new AA credit card applicants, consider the Citi AAdvantage Platinum Select which offers 50,000 miles after $2,500 in spend in the first 3 months (inflight and airport offers have gone up to 80,000 after $3,500 in 4 months).

sections.title: Earning Rates
sections.content:
• 2x miles on: Eligible American Airlines purchases.
  • 1x mile on: Everything else.

Under Barclays, the earning structure was bare-bones — just 2x on AA purchases and 1x everywhere else, with no bonus categories for groceries, gas, dining, or anything else. Since Citi converted the card to the Platinum Select on April 24, 2026, accounts also earn 2x at restaurants and gas stations. This was never a card you carried for everyday spending. It was a card you held for the checked bag benefit, the companion certificate, and the easy welcome bonus. For better everyday earning on AA miles, the Citi AAdvantage Platinum Select offers 2x on restaurants and gas stations in addition to 2x on AA purchases.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
AAdvantage miles redeem through the American Airlines loyalty program:

  • American Airlines Flights: Award flights on AA and partner airlines. Award pricing varies based on route, class, and availability.
  • Partner Airlines: Redeem on oneworld alliance partners including British Airways, Cathay Pacific, Japan Airlines, Qantas, and Qatar Airways. International business and first class redemptions can deliver incredible value.
  • Upgrades: Use miles for cabin upgrades on AA flights.
  • Hotels & Car Rentals: Available but generally poor value compared to flights.

AAdvantage miles are best used for partner airline premium cabin awards. A business class flight to Asia on Japan Airlines or Qatar Airways can deliver 3-5+ cents per mile in value.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• Free Checked Bag: First bag free for you and up to 4 companions on domestic AA itineraries. Savings of $90+ per round trip per person.
  • Preferred Boarding: Group 5 boarding on American Airlines flights.
  • $25 Wi-Fi Credit: Up to $25 back per year in statement credits for inflight Wi-Fi on AA-operated flights. Ends October 25, 2026.
  • Companion Certificate: After $20,000 spend, get a companion ticket for $99 plus taxes on domestic economy. Best value on long or expensive domestic routes. Citi is ending this perk: you can earn it one last time through your next cardmember anniversary.
  • 25% Inflight Savings: 25% back on inflight food and beverage purchases on AA-operated flights via statement credit.

The checked bag benefit is the real daily value driver here. Everything else is gravy.

sections.title: Competitor Comparison
sections.content:
• vs. Citi AAdvantage Platinum Select ($99/yr): Same annual fee, same free bag benefit, but Citi adds 2x on gas and restaurants and a $125 AA flight discount after $20K spend. The Citi card is strictly better for new applicants — better earning rates and still accepting applications. This is the natural successor card.
  • vs. Citi AAdvantage Executive ($695/yr): The nuclear option with Admirals Club access, 4x on AA, and 12x on AAdvantage Hotels and Cars bookings. Completely different tier and price point.
  • vs. Delta SkyMiles Gold ($150/yr): Similar bag-focused airline card for Delta flyers. Delta Gold is pricier but includes 2x on restaurants.
  • vs. United Explorer ($150/yr, $0 first year): United's mid-tier option with 3x on United purchases, free bags, and 2 United Club passes per year. More expensive but more perks.

sections.title: Best For
sections.content:
• Existing cardholders: Your Aviator Red became a Citi AAdvantage Platinum Select on April 24, 2026. Keep it for the free bags and 2x on AA, restaurants and gas. The $25 Wi-Fi credit ends October 25, 2026, and the companion certificate goes away after your next cardmember anniversary.
  • AA loyalists who wanted a non-Citi card: The Aviator Red was the last AA card open to new applicants that Citi didn't issue. Since April 24, 2026, every AA card comes from Citi.
  • Balance transfer seekers: The 0% intro APR on balance transfers was unusual for an airline card and genuinely useful, but it was only for new accounts, and the card is closed.

Not ideal for: New applicants (the card is closed to new applications). Look at the Citi AAdvantage Platinum Select instead — it has better earning rates at the same price point and is actively accepting applications.

title: Citi AAdvantage Platinum Select
scouts_verdict: The Citi AAdvantage Platinum Select is the AA card most people should get. The math is simple: $99/year (waived year one), free bags for you and 4 companions, preferred boarding, 2x on AA/gas/restaurants, and a 50,000-mile welcome bonus. With the Aviator Red discontinued (its accounts were converted to this card in April 2026), this is now the definitive mid-tier AA card. The $125 flight discount at $20K spend is a nice loyalty kicker, and the 48-month bonus restriction is standard Citi. If you fly AA regularly, this card pays for itself in bag fees alone.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
The Citi AAdvantage Platinum Select is the workhorse AA credit card — the one most American Airlines flyers should start with. At $99 per year (waived the first year), it delivers the core AA loyalty perks: free checked bags, preferred boarding, and 2x earning on AA purchases, gas stations, and restaurants. Nothing fancy, but nothing missing either.

With Barclays out of the AA partnership and the Aviator Red discontinued (its accounts were converted to this card in April 2026), the Platinum Select is now the definitive mid-tier AA card. It sits above the free Citi AAdvantage MileUp (no annual fee, minimal perks) and below the Citi AAdvantage Globe ($350/yr with four Admirals Club passes) and the premium AAdvantage Executive ($695/yr with Admirals Club). For most AA flyers, this is the sweet spot.

The $125 AA flight discount after $20,000 in annual spend is a nice loyalty reward, and the first-year fee waiver makes this an easy card to try risk-free. If you fly American Airlines even a few times a year, this card saves you money on bags alone.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• First Checked Bag Free: Free first checked bag on domestic AA itineraries for you and up to 4 companions on the same reservation. Saves $45 each way per person ($50 if you'd pay at the airport).
  • Preferred Boarding: Board ahead of general boarding on AA flights — you and up to 4 companions on the same reservation. Earlier overhead bin access and less gate chaos.
  • $125 AA Flight Discount: Earn a $125 American Airlines flight discount after spending $20,000 or more in a cardmember year and renewing your card. Decent loyalty reward for heavy spenders.
  • No Annual Fee First Year: Try the card risk-free for a full year. The Delta Gold and United Explorer waive year one too, so it's not unique, but it's still a free trial year.
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees: Use internationally without the 3% surcharge.
  • Up to $180 Turo Credit (ends Oct 18, 2026): Up to $30 back per eligible Turo trip completed by October 18, 2026. A limited-time promo, not a permanent perk.
  • Citi Entertainment Access: Presale tickets and VIP experiences through Citi's entertainment program.

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:
• Annual Fee: $0 intro for the first year, then $99. Delta Gold and United Explorer also waive year one, but at $99 after that this is the cheapest of the three.
  • Foreign Transaction Fees: None
  • APR: Variable, typically 19.74% - 29.74%
  • Balance Transfer Fee: 5% of the amount transferred, $5 minimum
  • Late Payment Fee: Up to $41

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
Earn 50,000 AAdvantage bonus miles after spending $2,500 in purchases within the first 3 months of account opening. Elevated offers of up to 80,000 miles appear periodically (most recently 80K after $3,500 in 4 months), especially through targeted or inflight offers.

50,000 AAdvantage miles is a solid haul — enough for a domestic round-trip in economy (typically 15,000-25,000 miles) twice over, or a meaningful chunk toward an international business class award on a partner airline. At ~1.4 cents per mile, that's roughly $700 in value.

The $2,500 spend in 3 months (~$833/month) is very manageable, and with the first-year fee waived, your only cost is the spending you'd presumably do anyway. Hard to argue with that math.

Important: You can't earn the bonus if you've received a Citi AAdvantage Platinum Select bonus in the past 48 months.

sections.title: Earning Rates
sections.content:
• 2x miles on: Eligible American Airlines purchases.
  • 2x miles on: Restaurants and gas stations.
  • 1x mile on: Everything else.

The 2x on restaurants and gas stations is a meaningful improvement over the old Aviator Red, which only earned 2x on AA purchases. These are high-frequency spending categories that make the card useful for daily spend, not just when you're buying flights.

That said, 1x on everything else is mediocre. For non-bonus spending, you're better off using a general rewards card like Citi Double Cash (2% on everything) or Chase Freedom Unlimited (1.5x UR on everything).

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
AAdvantage miles redeem through American Airlines' loyalty program:

  • AA Flights: Award tickets on American Airlines with dynamic pricing. Economy domestic round-trips typically cost 15,000-25,000 miles.
  • Partner Airlines: Redeem on oneworld alliance partners — British Airways, Japan Airlines, Cathay Pacific, Qatar Airways, Qantas, and more. International premium cabin awards are where these miles shine brightest.
  • Upgrades: Use miles for cabin upgrades on AA-operated flights.
  • Hotels & Car Rentals: Available but generally poor value. Stick to flights.

The best use of AAdvantage miles is partner business/first class redemptions. A one-way business class flight to Japan on JAL can cost 60,000 miles — delivering 4-5+ cents per mile in value. That's the play.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• Free Checked Bag: First bag free for you and up to 4 companions on domestic AA itineraries. At $90 per round trip per person ($45 each way prepaid), this is the primary value driver.
  • Preferred Boarding: Board before general boarding groups. Less stress, more bin space.
  • $125 Flight Discount: After $20,000 annual spend, get $125 off an AA flight. Works out to a 0.625% rebate on that spending — modest but appreciated.
  • Inflight Discount: 25% back on AA inflight food and beverage purchases.
  • Turo Credit: Up to $180 in statement credits ($30 per eligible trip) on Turo trips completed by October 18, 2026. Limited-time promo.

The perks are straightforward and practical. Aside from the short-lived Turo promo, no complicated credits to track, no convoluted redemption processes. Just bag savings, better boarding, and a spending loyalty reward.

sections.title: Competitor Comparison
sections.content:
• vs. AAdvantage Aviator Red ($99/yr): The Aviator Red is discontinued, and its accounts were converted to the Platinum Select in April 2026. The Platinum Select is the direct replacement with better earning categories (2x gas + restaurants) and the $125 flight discount. Clear upgrade.
  • vs. Citi AAdvantage Executive ($695/yr): The Executive adds Admirals Club access, 4x on AA, and 12x on AAdvantage Hotels and Cars bookings. Only worth it if you value lounge access and fly AA frequently enough to justify $695.
  • vs. Delta SkyMiles Gold ($150/yr, $0 first year): Similar perks (bag, boarding) for $51 more, plus a free second checked bag on domestic Delta flights. The Delta Gold earns 2x on restaurants and U.S. supermarkets instead of gas. Pick based on your airline loyalty.
  • vs. United Explorer ($150/yr, $0 first year): United Explorer is pricier but includes 2 United Club passes and 2x on dining and hotel stays. More premium positioning.
  • vs. Chase Sapphire Preferred ($95/yr): If you fly multiple airlines, the CSP's transferable points (including to AA partner British Airways) offer more flexibility at a lower price.

sections.title: Best For
sections.content:
• Regular AA flyers: If you fly American Airlines 3+ times a year, the bag savings alone justify the $99 fee (which is waived year one anyway).
  • AA mile collectors: The 2x on AA, gas, and restaurants makes this a solid everyday earning card within the AA ecosystem.
  • Former Aviator Red holders: Aviator Red accounts were converted to this card in April 2026 when Barclays exited the AA partnership, and you gain 2x on gas and restaurants.
  • First-time airline card holders: The waived first-year fee makes this risk-free to try.

Not ideal for: Infrequent AA flyers (you won't use the bag benefit enough), premium travelers who want lounge access (get the Executive), or travelers who prefer flexible points over airline miles.

title: Citi AAdvantage Executive
scouts_verdict: The Citi AAdvantage Executive is a one-trick pony — but it's a very good trick. The Admirals Club membership alone is worth up to $1,400/year, and you're paying $695. Everything else — the 4x on AA, free bags for 8 companions, up to $180 in Lyft, $120 car rental, $100 inflight and $500 AA Vacations credits — is bonus. The 125K welcome bonus is the largest of any AA card. But let's be honest: if you don't care about the Admirals Club, there's no reason to pay $695 when the Platinum Select exists at $99. This card is laser-focused on AA loyalists who fly frequently and want a home base in the airport. For that audience, it's excellent.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
The Citi AAdvantage Executive is American Airlines' premium credit card — and at $695 per year, it better deliver. The headline benefit is Admirals Club membership, which now costs up to $1,400/year on its own. If you want lounge access on AA flights and you fly often enough to use it, this card literally pays for itself on that one perk alone.

Beyond the lounge access, the Executive card earns 4x on AA purchases, 12x on AA hotel and car rental portal bookings, and comes with free bags for you and up to 8 companions. The 12x earning through AA portals is eye-popping on paper, though the portal prices aren't always competitive with direct booking.

This is not a card for casual travelers. It's for AA loyalists who fly frequently, value lounge access, and want to stack miles aggressively. If that's not you, the Platinum Select at $99/year covers the basics. But if you're spending $695 and actually using the Admirals Club, you're getting a deal that most premium travel cards can't match.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• Admirals Club Membership: Full access to nearly 50 Admirals Club lounges and 60+ partner lounges (including Alaska Lounges). Complimentary drinks, snacks and Wi-Fi, plus special pricing on conference rooms. Valued at up to $1,400/year.
  • Guest Access: Bring immediate family members or up to 2 traveling guests into the Admirals Club. Each authorized user (18+) gets Admirals Club access too, with the same guest allowance but no partner lounges, when holding a same-day boarding pass on an eligible flight.
  • First Checked Bag Free: Free first checked bag on domestic AA itineraries for you and up to 8 companions on the same reservation. More generous than the Platinum Select's 4-companion limit.
  • Group 4 Boarding: Priority boarding on AA flights — not the earliest group, but ahead of general boarding.
  • Up to $100 Inflight and Admirals Club Credit: Statement credits on inflight and eligible Admirals Club purchases each calendar year. (The old $120 Grubhub credit is gone for accounts opened on or after Aug. 23, 2026.)
  • Up to $500 AA Vacations Credit: Up to $250 back January–June and up to $250 July–December on eligible American Airlines Vacations packages.
  • Up to $180 Lyft Credit: Earn a $15 Lyft credit after taking 3 eligible rides in a calendar month, for up to $180 annually.
  • Omni Hotels Champion Status and Free Night: Enroll for complimentary Omni Champion status, and earn one Omni Free Night Award per calendar year after a qualifying stay of 2+ consecutive nights booked directly with Omni.
  • Avis President's Club Status: Complimentary Avis President's Club status for primary cardmembers who enroll (offered through Aug. 31, 2028).
  • Global Entry or TSA PreCheck Credit: Up to $120 statement credit every 4 years as reimbursement for your Global Entry or TSA PreCheck application fee.
  • Up to $120 Car Rental Credit: Statement credits on prepaid Avis or Budget rentals each calendar year.
  • Authorized Users with Lounge Access: Up to 3 authorized users for $175 total (~$58 each), each with their own Admirals Club access. Additional authorized users are $175 each.
  • Loyalty Point Bonuses: 10,000 bonus Loyalty Points each time you reach 50,000, 90,000, 165,000 and 240,000 Loyalty Points in a status year — up to 40,000 extra.

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:
• Annual Fee: $695 for accounts opened on or after Aug. 23, 2026 (previously $595) — steep, but compare it to up to $1,400/year for a standalone Admirals Club membership with guest privileges.
  • Authorized User Fee: $175 total for up to 3 users, $175 each for additional users. Each authorized user gets Admirals Club access.
  • Foreign Transaction Fees: None
  • APR: Variable, 19.74% - 29.74%
  • Late Payment Fee: Up to $40

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
Earn 125,000 AAdvantage bonus miles after spending $15,000 in purchases within the first 5 months of account opening. This is the highest welcome offer in the card's history (the previous high was 100,000), and Citi describes it as a limited-time offer — confirm it is still live before applying.

125,000 AAdvantage miles is a serious stash — enough for multiple domestic round-trips, several international economy tickets, or a business class award on a partner airline with miles left over. At ~1.45 cents per mile, that's roughly $1,813 in value.

The $15,000 spend requirement is steep and it is the catch: over 5 months that is $3,000 a month, so this only makes sense if you can hit it organically. Manufacturing the spend to chase the bonus rarely ends well.

Important: You can't earn the bonus if you've received a Citi AAdvantage Executive bonus in the past 48 months.

sections.title: Earning Rates
sections.content:
• 12x miles on: Eligible hotels booked through aadvantagehotels.com and car rentals through aadvantagecars.com.
  • 4x miles on: Eligible American Airlines purchases.
  • 5x miles on AA (after $150K): After spending $150,000 in a calendar year, earn 5x on eligible AA purchases for the rest of the year.
  • 1x mile on: Everything else.

The 12x on AA portals looks amazing, but check portal prices against direct booking — the portal rates aren't always competitive. The 4x on AA is solid and the best rate among AA cards. But the 1x on everything else is a glaring weakness for a $695 card. For non-AA spending, use a general rewards card like Citi Double Cash or Venture X.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
AAdvantage miles redeem through American Airlines' program:

  • AA Flights: Dynamic award pricing on American Airlines flights.
  • Partner Airlines: Oneworld partners including British Airways, Japan Airlines, Cathay Pacific, Qatar Airways, Qantas, Finnair, and more. Premium cabin partner awards deliver the best value — 3-5+ cents per mile.
  • Upgrades: Use miles for cabin upgrades on AA flights.
  • Hotels & Car Rentals: Available but poor value. Fly instead.

The strategy here is clear: earn miles at 4x-12x through AA purchases and portals, then redeem for international business/first class on partner airlines. A Qatar Airways Qsuites flight for 70,000 miles one-way? That's where these miles earn their keep.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• Admirals Club Membership: The card's raison d'etre. 100+ Admirals Club and partner lounges worldwide with complimentary food, drinks, and Wi-Fi. A genuine quality-of-life upgrade for frequent AA flyers.
  • $100 Annual Inflight and Admirals Club Credit: Statement credits on inflight and eligible Admirals Club purchases. Easy to use if you buy food or drinks on board or in the club.
  • $500 Annual AA Vacations Credit: Up to $250 per half-year on eligible American Airlines Vacations packages. Only worth counting if you book packages.
  • $120 Annual Car Rental Credit: Credits on prepaid Avis or Budget rentals. Useful for road warriors.
  • Free Bags (8 companions): Tied with the Citi AAdvantage Globe for the most generous bag benefit among AA cards — up to 8 companions vs. 4 on the Platinum Select.
  • $180 Annual Lyft Credit: $15/month in Lyft credits after taking 3 eligible rides per month. Useful for frequent rideshare users.
  • Global Entry/TSA PreCheck Credit: Up to $120 every 4 years toward Global Entry or TSA PreCheck application fees.
  • Authorized User Lounge Access: At ~$58 per user (3 for $175), this is the cheapest way to get Admirals Club access for family members.

Between the up-to-$1,400 lounge membership, $180 Lyft, $120 car rental, $100 inflight and $500 AA Vacations credits, and $30/yr Global Entry amortized, the face value of benefits is over $2,300 — more than three times the $695 fee. The question is whether you'll actually use all of it.

sections.title: Competitor Comparison
sections.content:
• vs. Citi AAdvantage Platinum Select ($99/yr): Save $596 but lose the Admirals Club, downgrade to 2x on AA, lose the Lyft, car rental, inflight and AA Vacations credits, and only get free bags for 4 companions. The Platinum Select is the smart choice unless you specifically need lounge access.
  • vs. Amex Platinum ($895/yr): The Amex Platinum gives you Centurion Lounges (generally nicer than Admirals Clubs) plus Priority Pass, Delta Sky Club access (10 visits when flying Delta), and a broader set of credits. More versatile for multi-airline travelers, but no AA-specific benefits.
  • vs. Chase Sapphire Reserve ($795/yr): Priority Pass lounge access, $300 travel credit, 8x on Chase Travel, 4x on flights and hotels booked direct, 3x on dining, and transferable points. Better overall value unless you specifically need Admirals Club.
  • vs. Capital One Venture X ($395/yr): Capital One Lounges + Priority Pass, $300 travel credit, 10K anniversary miles. Lower fee with competitive lounge access — but no Admirals Club specifically.
  • vs. Delta SkyMiles Reserve ($650/yr): Delta's equivalent premium card with Sky Club access. Similar concept for Delta loyalists. Pick based on your airline.

sections.title: Best For
sections.content:
• Frequent AA flyers who want lounge access: If you fly AA 10+ times a year and want Admirals Club access, this is the cheapest way to get it ($695 vs. up to $1,400 for a standalone membership).
  • Families flying AA: The 8-companion bag benefit and authorized user lounge access make this great for traveling families.
  • AA mile accumulators: 4x on AA purchases and 12x on AA portal bookings accelerate your mile balance fast.
  • Road warriors: The Lyft and car rental credits add up to $300/year in practical value for business travelers.

Not ideal for: Occasional AA flyers (get the Platinum Select), travelers who fly multiple airlines (a card like Amex Platinum with multi-airline lounge access is better), or anyone who won't use the Admirals Club regularly — the $695 fee is hard to justify without it.

title: Atmos Rewards Summit Visa Infinite
scouts_verdict:
The Atmos Rewards Summit is a genuinely impressive premium airline card — and at $395, it undercuts the Delta Reserve ($650) and United Club Infinite ($695) while arguably delivering more flexible value. The star of the show is that 25,000-point Global Companion Award. Unlike Delta's companion cert (U.S., Mexico, Caribbean and Central America only), this one works on partner airlines in any cabin. Book a companion on Cathay Pacific business class or Japan Airlines first class and it knocks up to 25,000 points off their seat, while the 100K version you unlock at $60K in spend can cover most of a long-haul business-class award.

The 8 Alaska Lounge passes a year (2 per quarter), 3X on dining and foreign transactions, and 10,000 annual status points round out a genuinely strong package. And if you're a big spender who can hit $60K, that 100,000-point Global Companion Award is gravy.

Here's the honest take: if you fly Alaska or Hawaiian regularly and have any interest in Oneworld partner redemptions, this is the best premium airline card you can carry in 2026. The earning rates won't blow you away on everyday spend (1X on non-bonus categories is par for the course), but the perks-to-fee ratio is best-in-class. Just make sure you'll actually use the lounge passes and companion award — if those go to waste, you're better off with the Ascent at $95 and pocketing the $300 difference.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
The Atmos Rewards Summit Visa Infinite is the top-shelf personal card in the Alaska Airlines/Hawaiian Airlines ecosystem, issued by Bank of America. At $395 per year, it slots in as a genuine premium airline card — and unlike some competitors, it actually earns its keep if you fly the Alaska/Hawaiian network regularly.

The headline perks: a 25,000-point Global Companion Award every anniversary (usable on partner airlines in any cabin, including business and first), quarterly Alaska Lounge passes, 3X on Alaska/Hawaiian purchases, dining and foreign transactions, and a path to a second Global Companion Award worth up to 100,000 points if you spend $60,000+ in a card anniversary year. It launched as a brand-new premium tier when Alaska and Hawaiian merged their loyalty programs into Atmos Rewards (the old Alaska Airlines Visa Signature became the $95 Ascent).

If you fly Alaska or Hawaiian even a handful of times per year and value lounge access and companion awards, this card deserves a hard look. If you don't, the Ascent at $95 is probably the smarter play.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• 25,000-point Global Companion Award — issued every card anniversary. Valid on Alaska, Hawaiian, Oneworld partners, and other Atmos partners in any cabin, including business and first class. It takes up to 25,000 points off a companion's award (you pay any points above that, and any unused value is forfeited), which TPG values at about $388.
  • 100,000-point Global Companion Award — earn this on top of the 25K award when you spend $60,000+ in your anniversary year. Big spenders take note.
  • Alaska Lounge access — two quarterly lounge passes (8 per year) to any Alaska Lounge location.
  • 10,000 status points on every card anniversary, getting you halfway to Atmos Silver status. Plus 1 status point per $2 spent on the card with no cap.
  • Free first checked bag for you and up to 6 companions on the same reservation when you buy the ticket with the card.
  • Preferred boarding for you and up to 6 guests on the same reservation, on flights operated by Alaska, Horizon and SkyWest, when you pay with the card and add your Atmos Rewards number.
  • 20% back on inflight purchases — food, drinks, Wi-Fi on Alaska and Hawaiian.
  • $50 instant travel delay credit when your Alaska or Hawaiian flight is canceled the same day or delayed 2+ hours, plus Visa Infinite benefits including concierge and travel protections.
  • Up to $120 TSA PreCheck / Global Entry Credit — statement credit every 4 years when you charge the application fee to your card.
  • No foreign transaction fees

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:
Annual Fee: $395 per year.

Foreign Transaction Fees: None.

Other Fees: Standard Bank of America fee structure.

The real math:

  • $395 annual fee
  • Minus the 25K Global Companion Award (conservatively worth $300-$500+ on partner business/first class bookings)
  • Minus 8 Alaska Lounge passes per year (worth $65 each = $520 at day-pass pricing)
  • Minus 10,000 status points annually
  • Minus free checked bags ($45 each way, adds up fast with family)

If you use the companion award and hit the lounges a few times, you're already ahead. The $395 fee looks steep on paper but pencils out quickly for regular Alaska/Hawaiian flyers.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
Current public offer: Earn 70,000 bonus Atmos Rewards points plus a 25,000-point Global Companion Award after spending $3,000 in the first 90 days.

Recent offers: This bonus moves around. The card launched in 2025 with 100,000 bonus points plus the 25K Global Companion Award after $6,000 in 90 days, and from April to early July 2026 it offered a 50% flight discount code on approval plus 100,000 points and the companion award after $6,500 in spend. Both have expired. An 80K-for-$4,000 version ran from October 2025 to April 2026 and again from July to September 2026.

At a conservative 1.5 cents per point valuation, the 70K public offer is worth roughly $1,050 in flights, plus the companion award on top. The 100K versions pushed that to $1,500+. It's the smallest bonus this card has offered, though its $3,000 spend requirement is also the lowest yet.

Scout's tip: Check your Alaska/Atmos account and the Alaska Airlines app for targeted offers before applying through the public link. And if you're not in a rush, it can pay to wait: this card has already hit 100K twice.

sections.title: Earning Rates
sections.content:
3X points per $1 on:

  • Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines purchases
  • Dining (restaurants worldwide)
  • Eligible foreign transactions

1X point per $1 on all other purchases.

Bank of America bonus: Eligible BofA checking/savings account holders get a 10% bonus on all card purchases, bumping those rates to 3.3X and 1.1X respectively.

Status points: Earn 1 status point per $2 spent on the card (no cap), plus 10,000 status points on each card anniversary.

The 3X on dining is a nice touch that most airline cards don't offer — it means you don't need to relegate this card to airline-only duty. The foreign transaction bonus at 3X is also unusual and makes this a legitimate travel-abroad card.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
Award flights are where Atmos points shine brightest. You can book flights on Alaska, Hawaiian, and the full Oneworld alliance (including Cathay Pacific, Japan Airlines, Qantas, British Airways, and more).

  • Best value: Partner business and first class redemptions — Cathay Pacific business class to Hong Kong, Japan Airlines first class to Tokyo, or Qantas business to Australia can deliver 3-5+ cents per point.
  • Solid value: Alaska/Hawaiian domestic flights typically redeem around 1.5-2 cents per point.
  • Global Companion Award: Your annual 25K companion award takes up to 25,000 points off a companion's award on Alaska, Hawaiian or any partner bookable at alaskaair.com, in any cabin — far more flexible than the regional companion fares on most airline cards.

Summit primary cardholders can also transfer points to hotel partners like Marriott Bonvoy and Shangri-La Circle (ratios vary by partner), but that's rarely the best use. This is an airline-focused currency, and that's fine because Alaska's partner network is one of the best in the game for aspirational redemptions.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• 8 Alaska Lounge passes per year (2 per quarter) — usable at any Alaska Lounge location, and each one covers you plus up to two kids under 21 for the whole travel day. They don't work at Hawaiian's Premier Club or Plumeria Lounge, and they don't roll over, so use them or lose them.
  • 8 Alaska Wi-Fi passes per year (2 per quarter, valid through the end of the quarter they're issued).
  • Free first checked bag for cardholder + up to 6 guests on the same reservation.
  • Preferred boarding (group C) for you and up to 6 guests on the same reservation, on flights operated by Alaska, Horizon and SkyWest.
  • 20% back on inflight purchases: food, drinks and Wi-Fi on Alaska and Hawaiian flights, paid back as a statement credit.
  • Up to $120 TSA PreCheck / Global Entry Credit: Statement credit every 4 years when you charge the application fee to your card.
  • $50 instant travel delay credit when your Alaska or Hawaiian flight is canceled within 24 hours of departure or delayed 2+ hours. It's for the primary cardholder only: you have to be on the flight, with your Atmos Rewards number on the reservation and the ticket bought on alaskaair.com with the card. Use the voucher within 48 hours (one per day).
  • Visa Infinite benefits: Concierge service, luxury hotel collection access, travel and purchase protections, auto rental coverage.

The lounge pass system is generous — 8 visits per year at $65 per pass means $520 in lounge value alone. Combined with the companion award and checked bag savings, the travel perks stack up quickly.

sections.title: Competitor Comparison
sections.content:
How does the Summit stack up against other premium airline cards?

CardAnnual FeeLounge AccessCompanion BenefitBest For
Atmos Summit$3958 Alaska Lounge passes/yr25K Global Companion Award (any cabin, partners)Alaska/Hawaiian + Oneworld flyers
Delta Reserve$65015 Sky Club visits/yrCompanion cert (U.S., Mexico, Caribbean & Central America; First Class eligible)Delta hub flyers
United Club Infinite$695United Club membershipNoneUnited hub flyers
Citi AAdvantage Executive$695Admirals Club membershipNoneAA loyalists wanting lounge access

The Summit's $395 fee is the lowest in this group, and the Global Companion Award — valid on partner airlines in business and first class — is arguably the most valuable companion benefit of the bunch. The Delta Reserve's Sky Club access is more generous, but the Summit compensates with a lower fee and better partner award flexibility.

sections.title: Best For
sections.content:
• West Coast flyers who use Alaska and Hawaiian as their primary airlines — especially those based at SEA, SFO, LAX, PDX, or HNL.
  • Oneworld alliance enthusiasts who want to book partner business and first class using Atmos points — the companion award and earning structure support aspirational redemptions.
  • Frequent travelers with families — the free checked bags for up to 6 companions and the Global Companion Award make family travel significantly cheaper.
  • Lounge lovers who fly through Alaska Lounge airports and want quarterly access without paying for a full membership.
  • Diners who appreciate 3X on restaurants — unusual for an airline card and means you can use this beyond just flights.

This card is not the best fit for infrequent flyers, people who don't fly Alaska/Hawaiian/Oneworld, or anyone looking for a simple cashback setup. If you fly Alaska a few times a year at most, the Ascent at $95 gives you free checked bags and a $99 Companion Fare (once you spend $6,000 a year on it) without the premium price tag.

title: Atmos Rewards Ascent Visa Signature
scouts_verdict:
The Atmos Rewards Ascent is the card I'd recommend to 80% of Alaska/Hawaiian flyers, and it's not even close. At $95, you get a $99 Companion Fare that can save $200-$500 on a single trip, free checked bags for your whole group, and a 50,000-point welcome bonus worth around $750 in flights. The fee-to-value ratio here is absurd.

The earning structure is quietly excellent too. 3X on Alaska/Hawaiian, 2X on gas, streaming, and transit — these aren't aspirational categories, they're your actual monthly bills. And you earn 1 status point per $3 on all purchases (no cap), so everyday spend steadily chips away at Atmos elite status. The $395 Summit earns faster (1 per $2), but for $95 this is a solid start.

The honest comparison: the Summit gives you lounge passes and a Global Companion Award for partner premium cabins, but it costs $300 more per year. Unless you're booking Cathay Pacific business class with that companion award, the Ascent's $99 Companion Fare on North American flights delivers more tangible savings for the average traveler. Get this card, hit the $6K annual spend for the companion fare, and enjoy what is quietly one of the best-value airline cards in 2026.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
The Atmos Rewards Ascent Visa Signature is the entry-level personal card in the Alaska Airlines/Hawaiian Airlines lineup, issued by Bank of America. At just $95 per year, it's the sweet spot of the Atmos card family — delivering the core airline perks (free bags, companion fare, bonus earning) without the $395 premium of the Summit.

This is the card that most Alaska/Hawaiian flyers should start with. The annual $99 Companion Fare alone can save you $200-$500 on a single domestic round trip, and you get free checked bags, 3X on Alaska and Hawaiian purchases, and 2X on everyday categories like gas, streaming, and transit. It's a practical, no-nonsense airline card that pays for itself almost immediately.

If you're trying to decide between this and the Summit, the question is simple: do you need lounge access and the Global Companion Award for partner premium cabins? If yes, Summit. If you just want a killer companion fare and solid everyday earning for $95, this is your card.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• $99 Companion Fare — earn a $99 companion fare (plus taxes/fees from $23) each anniversary year when you spend $6,000+ in the prior year. Valid on Alaska and Hawaiian flights within North America.
  • Free first checked bag for you and up to 6 companions on the same reservation when purchased with the card.
  • 20% back on inflight purchases — food, drinks, and Wi-Fi on Alaska and Hawaiian flights.
  • $100 off Alaska Lounge+ annual membership when purchased with the card.
  • 1 status point per $3 spent on all card purchases with no cap — slower than the Summit's 1 per $2, but it all counts toward Atmos elite status.
  • Preferred boarding on Alaska and Hawaiian flights operated by Alaska, Hawaiian, Horizon or SkyWest for you and up to 6 guests on the same reservation when you pay with the card.
  • No foreign transaction fees

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:
Annual Fee: $95 per year.

Foreign Transaction Fees: None.

The value math is simple:

  • $95 annual fee
  • Minus the $99 Companion Fare (saves $200-$500+ on a domestic round trip — you just need to spend $6K on the card first)
  • Minus free checked bags ($45 each way = $90 per round trip for one person)
  • Minus 20% inflight savings

One companion fare trip and a couple of checked bag savings, and you're already in the black. This is one of the easiest airline card fees to justify in the entire market.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
Current offer: Earn 50,000 bonus Atmos Rewards points plus a $99 Companion Fare (plus taxes/fees from $23) after spending $1,500 in the first 90 days.

At roughly 1.5 cents per point, those 50,000 points are worth around $750 in flights. Add the companion fare on top and you're looking at $900+ in first-year value from a card with a $95 fee. That's an exceptional return.

The $1,500 spend requirement is very reasonable — most people can hit that with normal spending in 90 days without trying to manufacture anything. The offer was 70,000 points as recently as summer 2026, so if you're not in a hurry, keep an eye out for a bump.

sections.title: Earning Rates
sections.content:
3X points per $1 on:

  • Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines purchases

2X points per $1 on:

  • Gas stations and EV charging
  • Streaming services and cable
  • Local transit (ride-hailing, trains, tolls, ferries)

1X point per $1 on all other purchases.

Bank of America bonus: Cardholders with an eligible Bank of America account get a 10% boost on all earnings, turning 3X into 3.3X, 2X into 2.2X, etc.

Status points: 1 status point per $3 spent on all purchases with no cap — a slower status-earning rate than the Summit's 1 per $2.

The 2X bonus categories are thoughtfully chosen for everyday spending. Gas, streaming, and transit are expenses most households already have, so you're earning bonus points without changing behavior.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
Atmos Rewards points redeem for flights on Alaska, Hawaiian, and the Oneworld alliance, plus additional airline partners.

  • Best value: Partner business and first class — same access as the Summit card. Cathay Pacific, Japan Airlines, Qantas, and other Oneworld partners offer premium cabin redemptions worth 3-5+ cents per point.
  • Good value: Alaska/Hawaiian domestic flights at roughly 1.5-2 cents per point.
  • Companion Fare: Your annual $99 companion fare works on Alaska and Hawaiian flights within North America — great for domestic and Hawaii trips.

The key difference from the Summit: you get a $99 Companion Fare (North America only) instead of the 25,000-point Global Companion Award (any cabin, any partner). For most people flying domestically, the companion fare is arguably more practical and guaranteed to save real money.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• $99 Companion Fare annually (after $6K spend) — valid on Alaska and Hawaiian flights in North America.
  • Free first checked bag for cardholder + up to 6 guests on the same booking.
  • Preferred boarding on Alaska and Hawaiian flights operated by Alaska, Hawaiian, Horizon or SkyWest.
  • 20% back on inflight purchases — food, beverages, Wi-Fi.
  • $100 off Alaska Lounge+ annual membership — not free access, but a nice discount if you're considering it.
  • No foreign transaction fees
  • Visa Signature benefits: Travel protections, auto rental collision damage waiver, extended warranty.

You don't get lounge passes like the Summit, but every other core travel perk is here. The companion fare is genuinely the anchor benefit — if you fly with a partner or friend even once a year, it pays the annual fee and then some.

At $95 with an annual companion fare, the Ascent is the value leader in this tier, even though its current 50K bonus is at the low end of this table. The Delta Platinum costs $255 more for its own Main Cabin companion cert. The United Explorer is free the first year but $150 after that, and has no companion benefit. The AA Platinum Select has no companion cert at all; its closest perk is a $125 flight discount that takes $20K in spend and a renewal. The Ascent punches well above its weight.

sections.title: Best For
sections.content:
• The practical Alaska/Hawaiian flyer who wants maximum value without a premium annual fee.
  • Couples and travel partners — the $99 Companion Fare is one of the best companion benefits at any price point.
  • Everyday earners who want 2X on gas, streaming, and transit without carrying a separate card for those categories.
  • Casual status earners — 1 status point per $3 with no cap nudges you toward Atmos elite status (serious chasers should look at the Summit's 1 per $2).
  • First-time airline cardholders — the $95 fee and $1,500 spend requirement are low barriers, and the rewards are disproportionately generous.

Skip this card if you don't fly Alaska or Hawaiian at least a couple of times per year, or if you want lounge access and global companion awards (get the Summit instead).

title: Atmos Rewards Ascent Business Visa
scouts_verdict:
The Atmos Rewards Business card is essentially the personal Ascent in a business suit — same $95 fee, same $99 Companion Fare, same free bags. The only meaningful ongoing difference is that shipping replaces streaming in the 2X categories, which is a perfectly sensible swap for any business that ships products.

Let's be real about what this card is: it's a companion fare delivery vehicle that also happens to earn decent points on business spending. And that's not a criticism — the companion fare alone justifies the $95 fee every single year. Add the checked bag savings, 2X on shipping and gas, and the ability to earn Atmos status points through business spending, and you have a quietly excellent business card.

The one caveat: if Alaska and Hawaiian aren't part of your regular travel patterns, this card has no reason to be in your wallet. The Chase Ink Preferred at the same $95 offers far more flexibility with transferable Ultimate Rewards points. But if you fly the Alaska/Hawaiian network for business and want a companion fare and airline perks at a rock-bottom fee, there's nothing else like this. It's the most efficient way to turn business spending into Alaska/Hawaiian travel value.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
The Atmos Rewards Ascent Business Visa is the business version of the Ascent card, issued by Bank of America for small business owners who fly Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines. At $95 per year ($70 account fee + $25 per card), it mirrors most of the personal Ascent's benefits while adding a business-relevant bonus category: shipping.

The value proposition is nearly identical to its personal sibling — a $99 Companion Fare, free checked bags, 3X on Alaska/Hawaiian, and 2X on gas, transit, and shipping. If you run a business that ships products and flies Alaska/Hawaiian for work, this card earns its keep quickly. And since it's a business card, the spending won't affect your personal credit utilization.

One important note: the business card's 2X categories swap out streaming/cable for shipping — a sensible trade for business owners. Everything else carries over from the personal Ascent.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• $99 Companion Fare — earn a $99 companion fare (plus taxes/fees from $23) each anniversary year when you spend $6,000+ in the prior year. Valid on Alaska and Hawaiian flights in North America.
  • Free first checked bag for the cardholder and up to 6 companions on the same reservation when the ticket is purchased with the card.
  • 20% back on inflight purchases — food, beverages, and Wi-Fi on Alaska and Hawaiian flights.
  • $100 off Alaska Lounge+ annual membership when purchased with the card.
  • 1 status point per $3 spent on all purchases — no cap. Same generous status-earning rate as the personal Ascent.
  • Preferred boarding on Alaska and Hawaiian flights for you and up to 6 guests on the same reservation when the ticket is bought with the card.
  • Business spending separation — keep business expenses on a dedicated card for cleaner bookkeeping and tax prep.
  • No foreign transaction fees

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:
Annual Fee: $95 per year ($70 account fee + $25 per card). Additional employee cards are $25 each.

Foreign Transaction Fees: None.

The business case:

  • $95 annual fee
  • Minus the $99 Companion Fare (saves $200-$500+ per trip — you need $6K annual spend to unlock it)
  • Minus free checked bags on business travel (up to $90 per person per round trip at Alaska's current $45 first-bag fee)
  • Minus 2X on shipping costs (a real expense for product-based businesses)

If your business flies Alaska/Hawaiian even a few times a year and ships products, the card pays for itself almost immediately. The $25 per employee card fee is also reasonable for businesses that want to consolidate spending and earn points across the team.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
Current offer: Earn 70,000 bonus Atmos Rewards points plus a $99 Companion Fare (plus taxes/fees from $23) after spending $4,000 in the first 90 days.

The personal Ascent's bonus varies by where you apply, but this one holds its own — 70K points worth roughly $1,050 in flights at 1.5 cents per point, plus the companion fare. For a $95 business card, this is an outstanding welcome offer.

Business owners can often hit the $4,000 threshold faster than personal cardholders since business expenses (supplies, shipping, services) add up quickly. This shouldn't require any manufactured spending.

sections.title: Earning Rates
sections.content:
3X points per $1 on:

  • Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines purchases

2X points per $1 on:

  • Gas stations and EV charging
  • Local transit (ride-hailing, trains, tolls, ferries)
  • Shipping purchases

1X point per $1 on all other purchases.

Bank of America bonus: If your company has an eligible BofA small business checking or savings account (or a Merrill business investment account), you get a 10% boost on points earned from card purchases.

Status points: 1 status point per $3 spent on all purchases — no cap.

The key difference from the personal Ascent: shipping replaces streaming/cable in the 2X categories. This is a smart swap for businesses — if you're shipping products via couriers like UPS or FedEx, those 2X points add up fast (the category covers courier and freight-carrier merchants, so don't count on USPS postage earning 2X). Office supplies, software, and other business expenses earn the base 1X rate.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
Points earned on the Business card go into the same Atmos Rewards account and redeem identically to points from the personal cards.

  • Best value: Partner premium cabin flights — Oneworld business and first class on Cathay Pacific, Japan Airlines, Qantas, etc. can deliver 3-5+ cents per point.
  • Good value: Alaska/Hawaiian domestic awards at 1.5-2 cents per point.
  • Companion Fare: The annual $99 companion fare works on Alaska and Hawaiian flights in North America.

For business travelers, the ability to earn points through business expenses and redeem for personal or business travel on Alaska's extensive partner network is a major advantage. Points pool with any personal Atmos card earnings, so you can combine household and business earning into one stash.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• $99 Companion Fare annually (after $6K spend) — valid on Alaska and Hawaiian within North America.
  • Free first checked bag for cardholder + up to 6 guests on the same booking when you pay for the flight with the card.
  • Preferred boarding on Alaska and Hawaiian when the ticket is bought with the card.
  • 20% back on inflight purchases — food, beverages, Wi-Fi.
  • $100 off Alaska Lounge+ annual membership
  • No foreign transaction fees — useful for international business travel or overseas vendors.
  • Visa business card protections: Purchase protection, extended warranty, auto rental coverage.

The perks mirror the personal Ascent almost exactly. No lounge passes (that's a Summit perk), but every other core travel benefit is present. For business travelers making regular Alaska/Hawaiian trips, the checked bag and companion fare savings stack up quickly across multiple trips per year.

The Atmos Business card can't match the Chase Ink Preferred's flexibility or the Venture X Business's premium perks, but neither of those offers a companion fare. If Alaska/Hawaiian is your airline and you want a dead-simple $95 card that delivers a companion fare and airline perks, this fills a niche no flexible-points card can.

sections.title: Best For
sections.content:
• Small business owners who fly Alaska/Hawaiian for work — the companion fare, checked bags, and preferred boarding make business travel cheaper and smoother.
  • E-commerce and product businesses that ship frequently — 2X on shipping is a category most business cards ignore.
  • Businesses wanting to separate spending while still earning airline points for personal or business travel.
  • Solopreneurs and freelancers who want a low-fee business card with outsized travel rewards.
  • Existing Atmos personal cardholders who want to pool business and personal earning into one Atmos Rewards account.

Skip this card if your business doesn't fly Alaska/Hawaiian, if you need broader bonus categories (get the Ink Preferred), or if you want premium lounge access (look at the Venture X Business or Amex Business Platinum).
